items.statement: FY26 volume growth guidance 10-15% and EBITDA spread INR 4,600-5,000 per ton
items.quote: Now first half into financial year of '26, we are fairly confident that we will be able to meet our guidance, which we gave in the quarter 1 call, which was 10% to 15% volume growth and EBITDA spread of INR 4,600 to INR 5,000 per ton.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 volume target 9 lakh tons, Q4 FY26 target 9.2-9.5 lakh tons with EBITDA ~INR 5,000/ton
items.value: 9 lakh tons Q3; 9.2-9.5 lakh tons Q4; ~INR 5,000/ton EBITDA
items.quote: Now, I understand it in my language, the target of 9 lakh tons will be Q3, the target of 9.2-9.5 lakh tons will be Q4. In that, the EBITDA of around INR 5,000 is INR450-INR450, INR900 crores, and INR 800 crores has come, so INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA target INR 1,700 crores
items.quote: And almost INR 1700 crores EBITDA target that we have taken, we will definitely beat that.

items.statement: INR 1,500 crores capex for 7 million ton capacity expansion over 2-3 years, 100% funded from internal cash flows
items.quote: 100% will be funded from internal cash flows. If you look at our operating cash flow to EBITDA, that's like above 90%. So this will help us to fund 100% of capex, so.

items.statement: Current capacity 5 million tons, adding 7 million tons (6M India, 1M Middle East) over 2-3 years; Raipur 1.5M tons, Dubai expanding to 500k tons
items.quote: Right now, we are close to a capacity of 5 million tons; and in the last 2 or 3 years, we are going to build up the capacity of further 7 million tons. Out of 7 million tons, there is 1 million ton capacity in Middle East.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 70% overall; Raipur ~65-70%, Dubai ~80-85% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: We are right now 5 million ton capacity. We are going to do this year 3.5 million tons, so 70% capacity utilization we are running.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA spread INR 5,200/ton, up INR 500/ton QoQ from brand premiumization, operating leverage, value-added mix
items.quote: So this is the breakup of INR500 per ton improvement in EBITDA.

items.statement: General category EBITDA spread doubled to INR 3,400/ton in last 2-3 quarters after Jan 2025 price hike of INR 2,000-3,000/ton
items.quote: Number one was the brand power of APL Apollo, which we are able to demonstrate in the EBITDA spreads of general category, which have almost doubled to INR3,400 per ton in last 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA spread target INR 6,000/ton blended over next 4-5 years
items.quote: And the next four, five years, definitely, the trajectory could be from INR5,000 to INR6,000 per ton.

items.statement: Steel price changes 100% passed through to NSR; GP/ton improvement driven by value-added mix not inventory gains
items.quote: Now for example, if you look at Q1 versus Q2, our NSR declined by INR5,000 per ton and the steel -- our raw material cost also came down by a similar level.

items.statement: Value-added mix improvement from Raipur and Dubai plants (EBITDA >INR 5,500-6,000/ton); new 1000x1000mm mill and capsule roofing products
items.quote: Second reason for margin expansion was the value-added mix improvement, which is mainly coming from our Dubai and Raipur plant, where the EBITDA per ton on -- for these plants is above INR5,500, INR6,000 per ton.

items.statement: SG Premium brand launched at ~10-15k tons/month to compete with secondary steel; EBITDA near breakeven on this brand
items.quote: Today, Apollo is higher than almost with all the other brands, INR3,000 minimum or maybe maximum INR 5,000 to INR 6,000 per ton. Apollo product is costly in the market.

items.statement: No demand boost seen yet; H1 FY26 weak due to monsoon, holidays, steel price decline; expect H2 better as monsoons over and channel empty
items.quote: Very frankly, I am saying that we are not seeing any boost up in demand. But due to our brand leverage, due to our size, due to our systems, we are sustainable.

items.statement: Steel prices downtrend ended in October; channel inventory empty so restocking demand expected from November
items.quote: Now in October it seems that the downward trend has ended. If it doesn't increase from November then it won't decrease either. So the channel is completely empty so the demand should pick up.

items.statement: 12% safeguard duty on HRC imports supports domestic prices; import parity at INR 52-53k/ton vs domestic INR 46k/ton
items.quote: Yes, 100% you are correct. Like right now, the HR coil for the month of October is close to INR46,000 per ton landed Ghazi abad or anywhere in the country, or if we do any import wit h the duties, it cost us to INR52,000 or INR 53,000 per

items.statement: Working capital days at 0 as of September 2025; ROCE >32% sustainable
items.quote: Lastly, on working capital front, our working capital days remain in single digit, in fact, 0 as at September 2025, which boosted our ROCE upward of 32%, 33%.

items.statement: No external debt for capex; 100% internal funding; focus on reducing payables to get supplier discounts
items.quote: First, our strategy is to remove the liabilities from the book and get some more discounts from the suppliers.

items.statement: Excess cash after capex and dividends to be used for higher dividends or buybacks; not kept as FDs
items.quote: The remaining money is a good problem to solve. We will increase dividends or buy back. We will do something. Keeping in company -- we will not make an FD.

items.statement: Dubai plant 8% of volume; opening warehouses in Liverpool and Antwerp to improve service and increase EBITDA spread by EUR 50/ton
items.quote: We are already supplying from Dubai. But if we open a warehouse there and make the service better, then we think that our EBITDA spread should increase by EUR50.

items.statement: Freight cost target reduction from INR 1,900/ton to INR 1,500/ton; salary cost target from INR 950/ton to INR 600/ton at 5M tons volume
items.quote: We are targeting to bring it to INR1,500 per ton. And number three on the front of our salary cost. We are targeting that today our salary is 5 million per ton. Minimum wages should increase. Nothing much will increase. So as soon as we achieve 5 million per ton then that cost will also increase a lot. Which is now running around INR950. My target is to bring down to INR600 per ton.

items.statement: Not focused on competitors; lowest cost producer globally; new capacity in new markets/products not competing with existing players
items.quote: We don't pay much attention to the competitor to be frank. We are working on our own strategy on how we have to do. We are going in a new area and we are not building up any capacity in our competitive items.

items.statement: Key risk is further GDP deterioration from current levels; no significant downside if demand stable
items.quote: Except further deterioration in GDP from existing levels.

items.statement: Pre-galvanized pipe volume 2 lakh tons/quarter (Coast Guard pipe category)
items.quote: 2 lakh ton is the sale of our quarter. Chetan Khandelwal: The product break-up that you will see in our presentation, the Coast Guard pipe in it, all that is pre

items.statement: Salary cost per ton to decrease from INR 950 to INR 600 as volume scales to 5M tons; minimum wage increases expected
items.quote: We are targeting that today our salary is 5 million per ton. Minimum wages should increase. Nothing much will increase. So as soon as we achieve 5 million per ton then that cost will also increase a lot. Which is now running around INR950. My target is to bring down to INR600 per ton.

items.statement: Long-term volume target 10 million tons; structural steel tube market 10% CAGR to 2030; conversion from secondary to primary steel key driver
items.quote: Most market is already there. But in India, there is the biggest problem there is a one secondary material is there, which is a very low quality material and it has a low cost. So, people are very much worried about the brand, about good material. So, as soon as the market is over, then 10 million tons will reach very easily.

items.statement: White space cost reduction target of ~95% by September 2026
items.quote: we remain committed to our target, which I had shared last time in the call that by September of next year we will reduce our white space cost by about 95%.

items.statement: White space reduced by over 20% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: I'm pleased to share with you that we have, in the last quarter alone, achieved a reduction of 20% plus of our white space in the last quarter.

items.statement: Express business turned gross margin positive for first time at 0.2% in Q2 FY26
items.quote: This is our first GM positive quarter with 0.2% gross margin as compared to minus 5.2% in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: No new BTS warehouse space additions planned; future expansion via RTM model
items.quote: We have no plans to add in the near future any BTS space. However, if some client comes in and gives to us a back-to-back kind of a commitment, we will consider that. But broadly, expansion will happen is by RTM ready to move, where there are no long-term commitments to any landlord.

items.statement: Warehouse network fully built out; peak rental cost reached
items.quote: As I mentioned earlier in this call, we have completed most of our warehouse expansion. And so, therefore, the way I look at it is that lease cost. And therefore, the depreciation cost arising from Ind AS 116 is at its peak and fully built out in the current quarter financials.

items.statement: Consolidated debt reduced from INR601 cr to INR73 cr after rights issue; INR187 cr retained for general corporate purposes
items.quote: As a result, we have reduced our consolidated debt obligation from INR601 crores at the end of quarter 1 to INR73 crores at the end of quarter 2. This will help us realize interest cost savings of INR40 crores to INR45 crores per annum.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR749 cr completed in August 2025; proceeds used for debt repayment
items.quote: let me share an update on the successful completion of our rights issue of INR749 crores in August 2025. The proceeds have been prudently utilized towards the repayment of debt, resulting in a stronger balance sheet.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin expanded to 10.1% in Q2 FY26 from 9.2% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated gross margin is at 10.1% in Q2 FY26 compared to 9.2% in Q2 FY25, driven by more favorable business mix, customer mix as well as volume leverage.

items.statement: Festive demand strong; grocery fulfilment center handled 8.2 lakh units in a single day
items.quote: For example, one of our grocery fulfilment center, I don't want to mahindra share the name of our customer. We handled 8.2 lakh units in a single day. This is our best ever, 8.2 lakh units in a single day from one site

items.statement: Key customer expansions from Cummins, Bosch, Amazon, Flipkart, Mahindra
items.quote: Also, repeat expansion projects from key customers such as Cummins, Bosch, Amazon, Flipkart, Mahindra, etcetera, reflect our robust customer partnership and strong execution capabilities.

items.statement: Express tonnage grew 7% YoY; yield improved by ~INR0.90 per kg year-to-date
items.quote: Our tonnage has improved 7% Y-o-Y and our share of Value-Added Services, which we call VAS has also improved.

items.statement: Last-mile pricing pressure persists; strategic customer mix decisions taken
items.quote: customer-driven pricing pressure continues to be a concern in last-mile delivery, and this has led to a few strategic decisions taken by us on our customer mix.

items.statement: Launched Alyte Prive premium B2C mobility service in Delhi NCR; expansion planned for Noida International Airport
items.quote: We have launched Prive service only in the region of Delhi NCR, and we have expansion plans now for Noida International Airport. There is a lot of growth that can be achieved in NCR, and we will keep the Prive focus on NCR for the whole of next year.

items.statement: INR50 cr equity infusion into MESPL to support journey to EBITDA positive
items.quote: Further, MLL is infusing additional equity capital of INR50 crores in MESPL to support in its journey to become EBITDA positive.

items.statement: Express PAT loss narrowed to INR20 cr from INR24 cr YoY; gross margin improvement flowing to PAT
items.quote: We have a PAT loss of INR20 crores in Q2 FY26 compared to INR24 crores in Q2 FY25. The improvement in gross margin is flowing down to PAT as well. We have improved gross margin by about INR5 crores, and you will see about INR4 crores improvement in the PAT.

items.statement: One-time PDD charge of INR4.8 cr for bankrupt 3PL customer
items.quote: During the quarter, we have recognized a onetime charge of INR4.8 crores under Provisions for Doubtful Debts or PDD arising from the bankruptcy filing of one of our 3PL customers.

items.statement: GST rate cuts positive for economy; e-way bill growth supports domestic resilience
items.quote: increasing domestic resilience, which is evident in the growth of e-way bills supported by GST cuts, very, very positive for overall economy

items.statement: Express market share maintained; focus on high-yield loads over volume
items.quote: No, we have not gained market share if that's what you mean. Achal: Yes. Hemant Sikka: I think there our improvement is on a very thought through strategy of improving our customer mix and that is helping us to improve our yield per kg

items.statement: Isha Dalal joined as new CFO with 15+ years experience across media, IB, PE, corporate finance
items.quote: I would like to extend a warm welcome to Ms. Isha Dalal as she joined us for her maiden earnings call in the capacity of Chief Financial Officer of Mahindra Logistics Limited. Ms. Isha has over 15 years of diverse experience spanning media, investment banking, private equity and corporate finance.

items.statement: PDD provision reflects prudent accounting for credit exposure on outstanding receivables
items.quote: This adjustment was undertaken as a prudent accounting measure to reflect potential credit exposure on our outstanding receivables.

items.statement: Freight forwarding volumes grew 9% YoY despite global headwinds
items.quote: Overall volumes grew by 9% Y-o-Y despite, as we all know, there are very strong global challenges, headwinds because of global tariffs and geopolitical challenges. Still, our cross-border business has done exceedingly well, growing by 9% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Depreciation of INR72 cr (mostly Ind AS 116 lease cost) at peak; expected to stay stable quarterly
items.quote: So the depreciation cost of the INR72 crores that we see in our consolidated P&L, actually, most of it belongs to the cost of the leases under Ind AS 116. And most of the year-on-year increase of the INR18 crores that you see also belongs to the impact of leases under Ind AS 116.

items.statement: Warehousing revenue up 20% YoY to INR333 cr driven by new sites and volume ramp-up
items.quote: Revenue from the warehousing segment stands at INR333 crores as compared to INR278 crores in Q2 FY25. That's up by approximately 20%, driven by the addition of new sites and the volume ramp-up in our existing sites.

items.statement: Infrastructure push and e-commerce/quick commerce expansion positive for coming quarters
items.quote: Further infrastructure push and rapid expansion of e-commerce and quick commerce have set a very positive tone for us in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Global tariff and geopolitical challenges create cross-border headwinds
items.quote: We continue to face headwinds like global uncertainty, cross-border price volatility and elevated input cost on the cross-border side.

items.statement: Operationalized 8 new projects across manufacturing and e-commerce; launched 3 lakh sq ft facility in Nashik
items.quote: Happy to share that we have operationalized 8 new projects across manufacturing and e-commerce and launched a 3 lakh square foot facility in Nashik.

items.statement: MD Dr. Prasada Raju resigned for personal priorities; will stay for transition through FY25
items.quote: Dr. Prasada Raju will be stepping down from his role as Managing Director of Cohance. Dr. Prasad a Raju has resigned from his position considering his personal priorities and to continue his learning journey. Prasad will remain associated with the company to orderly transition for an extended period ending this fiscal

items.statement: Board approved new org structure with three business CEOs reporting to Executive Chairman; platform COO joining shortly
items.quote: The board has approved a revised organizational structure, one that better reflects our multi- business portfolio and expanding global footprint and positions Cohance strongly on its path towards a $1 billion U.S. vision. This new structure is designed to bring greater agility, faster execution, and deeper accountability across our businesses.

items.statement: CFO Himanshu Agarwal appointed to board as director
items.quote: Additionally, I am pleased to share our CFO, Mr. Himanshu Agarwal will be joining the company's board as director, ensuring continuity and alignment across leadership and governance levels.

items.statement: Platform COO to join in next few weeks; based in Hyderabad with 30+ years experience
items.quote: We will also be welcoming a platform COO shortly, a seasoned industry leader who will be based out of Hyderabad. A techno- commercial professional with over three decades of experience, he brings a strong blend of operational excellence and on-the-ground project execution.

items.statement: Reaffirmed US$1 billion revenue vision by 2030 with significant CDMO contribution
items.quote: Our vision of a US$1 billion business by 2030 remains there. We are committed to reach there. And as part of that, we're bringing in more global leaders, more talent that can help us reach there faster and improve our chances of reaching there.

items.statement: RFP pipeline becoming more robust with strengthened BD team and commercial infrastructure
items.quote: Our RFP pipelines, which, you know, with the addition of a BD team and all these investments we've been making in commercial infrastructure is becoming more and more robust.

items.statement: Oligonucleotide unit at Nacharam completed equipment validation; on track for Q4 commissioning
items.quote: Surya, our oligonucleotide unit, has successfully completed equipment validation and remains on track for commissioning in Q4, marking another important milestone in expanding our advanced therapy capabilities.

items.quote: OI classification of our Nacharam FTF unit, which we updated to the stock exchange last week, we are in the process of appointing a leading U.S. FTA consulting firm to also help us in addition to an Indian firm to guide us through the remediation process. We're working proactively with external experts to address observations and engage with the agency in the best possible manner. However, as we h

But at the senior level, my hope is that we are reaching that po

items.statement: Aggressively pursuing inorganic opportunities with in-house M&A team; focus on niche tech capabilities for CDMO
items.quote: On your second question, in terms of the non -- the inorganic growth, we are aggressively committed. We actually have in -house M&A team of two people that is very experienced. We are aggressively looking at opportunities all the time, and as we are talking, there are some discussions going on. These are, again, focusing on our strategic direction that we said that we want to be a key CDMO player

items.statement: M&A funding primarily through internal resources; open to borrowing if needed; target cash positive at strategy period end
items.quote: Our plan is to fund everything with internal funding. If required, we can borrow money, but right now we're looking at everything with internal funding. Our idea is to remain cash positive and then just leverage our internal resources and the kind of opportunities in the capital structure we are looking at for equity structure aligns with our vision that should be just with internal funding and mi

items.quote: there is cost involved with the new people that are coming in and there will be some overlap also, because when new people come in, old is there. items.statement: Biosecure Act progress positive for India CDMO; companies pursuing China-free strategies regardless of legislation
items.quote: Listen, people are moving towards figuring out a China-free strategy. I think that trend, irrespective of biosecure, I think companies are trying. However, the pace at whi ch they move depends on company -to-company. Indian companies will definitely continue to benefit. Now, the Act, as you know, is still being reviewed and it's not fully passed, but it's a step in the right direction

items.statement: M&A targeting differentiated assets in ADC, oligonucleotide and other niche tech modalities; capability-focused not capacity-focused
items.quote: So, idea is to look for capabilities, not capacities. ADC, we have an East capability. We have a West capability. Oligo, we have an Eastern capability. You know, if we find something in the west, then Oligo will be happy, but we are looking at assets that are profitable, that bring unique capabilities to our portfolio. And they are all part of niche tax, s omething with niche capability

items.statement: Revenue target INR 200+ crore for FY26, INR 300 crore by end of FY27, INR 500+ crore vision for FY28
items.quote: The vision for 2026 is to reach revenue of INR 200 plus, which is definitely in our control. 2027, touching revenue of INR 300, and that's why, by the end of 2027.

items.statement: PAT margin target 9-10% for FY26, 12-15% for FY27, 18-20% by end of FY28
items.quote: If we had closed it at 6% last year, then next year, which will close this year, I have to close it at 9-10% and in the future, I have to close it at 12-15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance 15% range for FY27, moving toward 20% thereafter
items.quote: So, in FY '27 it will be in the 15% range? Manprit Singh Chadha: Yes.

items.statement: Factory capex less than INR 1 crore; 30-bed hospital phase 1 capex INR 2 crore; 5-10 lakh per bed average
items.quote: A 30 bed hospital would say require a capex of anything between INR 2- 2.5 crores.

items.statement: PAT margin jumped from 5% in H1 FY25 to 8.81% in H1 FY26 (100% growth); EBITDA improved 200+ bps
items.quote: H1 '25 to H1 '26 was a PAT margin of 5%, which grew to 8.81%, a 100% growth. Even in EBITDA terms may be H125 to H126, 200 plus basis points improvement.

items.statement: Advertisement cost may remain same or reduce 100-200 bps; future profitability from infrastructure utilization
items.quote: This advertisement cost, in the future, will either remain the same, or can come down 100-200 basis points.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated revenue INR 91.9 crore (18% YoY); standalone INR 88.35 crore (17% YoY); May slowdown caused ~INR 6 crore top-line hit
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue stood at INR 91.9 crores, reflecting a healthy 18% year-on-year growth compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Capsule and powder represent 50% of revenue; factory will produce up to 50% of capsule needs (25% of total); tablets not yet launched
items.quote: we plan to just make not more than 50% of our capsule intake, which translates to not more than 25% of our total intake

items.statement: Hospital expansion funded entirely through internal accruals; no plan to raise equity
items.quote: We, right now, we don't have any plan to raise equity [inaudible 00:40:59]. Right now, the entire plan is through internal accruals

items.statement: Ayurveda hospital approvals from Ministry of AYUSH pending; first 30-bed facility operational Q1 FY27
items.quote: It will take some time for that. We have just started it and yes, we will take time for the approval.

items.statement: High customer acquisition costs anticipated; increases from Google/Meta to be offset by operational efficiency and repeat rates
items.quote: I have kept my - like every time a question comes why advertisement cost is high, it would remain the same even when Meta and Google increases that and that increase will be mitigated by my operational efficiency and the repeat rate of the product.

items.statement: ESOP 2025 scheme approved by Board for all employees based on tenure; no distinction by level
items.quote: The ESOP 2025 scheme has been approved by the Board, because we know that Sat Kartar's biggest strength is its people. The best part? We made no distinction between employees, be it at whatever level, except tenure-based eligibility.

items.statement: Acquired Plantomed for low-ticket diabetes product (INR 1,300 vs own INR 2,500-2,600); currently ~INR 60 lakh/month, targeting INR 1 crore+/month in 2 months
items.quote: The rationale of that acquisition was that we are at a high ticket size. Our diabetes is at a ticket size of 2,500 to 2,600. Plantomed also runs a diabetes product, but it is at a ticket size of 1,300.

items.statement: US subsidiary prepared; international territories opened; no immediate revenue expected
items.quote: We have opened international territories, we have prepared our US subsidiary, all these things will not give revenue immediately.

items.statement: May revenue hit ~INR 6 crore due to India-Pakistan tension causing delivery partner denials and distribution disruption; safety prioritized over profits
items.quote: Because of this, we suffered approximately a top line hit of INR6 crores, and a negative bottom line during that period.

items.statement: Premium pricing justified by lifestyle positioning; first-sale ROI model with profitable repeat purchases; high ticket size sustainable
items.quote: My vision is, return for investors, and best of the best product for customers. Because of that, our model is, in the first sale, we should be able to generate an ROI, the second and third and fourth sale, should actually add on to that profit.

items.statement: AI beta testing complete, rollout starting; will enhance CRM, digital ops, customer experience; leverages categorized disease data to convert low-ticket Veda range
items.quote: Our AI initiatives are also entering an exciting phase. The beta testing is complete, and we are now ready for rollout. Through AI-based automation and analytics, we will enhance CRM intelligence, digital operations, and customer experience.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% annual growth while maintaining strong margins
items.quote: As already highlighted in the investor presentation, going forward, we are targeting 20 %-25% annual growth while maintaining strong margins.

items.statement: Planned FY26 capex of Rs 100 crores, Rs 83.30 crores deployed in H1 FY26
items.quote: The total planned CAPEX for the current FY is Rs.100 crores and we are well on track to complete the same.

items.statement: No upward revision to FY26 capex currently; Rs 17 crores balance may be deployed if new opportunities arise
items.quote: And going forward, as of now, we do not see an upward revision. That could come up once we have more clarity on the new opportunities that are coming up.

items.statement: Order book of Rs 129.9 crores executable in FY26, 60% equipment rental, 40% warehousing
items.quote: As of October 2025, our order book stands at a healthy Rs.129.9 crores executable entirely in FY26, 40% from the warehousing segment and 60% from the equipment rental segment.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts order book at Rs 12 crores from current order book
items.quote: So, at present, if I remember correctly, about 12 crores odd currently from the current order book in hand.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 39.20%, up 300+ bps YoY; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin up 300+ bps YoY
items.quote: Importantly, we achieved this while growing our EBITDA by 21% to 26.34 crores with the margin rising by more than 3 00 basis points to 39.20%.

items.statement: Equipment rental standalone EBITDA margin 64% in H1 FY26, committed to 60%+ guidance
items.quote: The overall EBITDA for this segment stood at 56% while the standalone EBITDA for equipment rentals stood at 64% for the said period.

items.statement: Specialized service contracts target EBITDA margin above 20% by end of FY26
items.quote: Our target remains to go upwards of 20% and we are confident that by the end of this year we will be able to achieve them as well.

items.statement: Robust demand across all segments with long-term client visibility; cement, metals, minerals driving growth
items.quote: In the present market scenario, we are witnessing robust demand across all segments and sectors that we operate in. We have long-term visibility from a majority of our clients giving us immense confidence that we shall continue to grow aggressively while maintaining healthy profitability.

items.statement: Shifted from rural/urban infra (20%) to metals/minerals (32%), cement (30%), renewable energy (9%) in equipment rental
items.quote: Among the major sectors served by us in the equipment rental segment, there was a jump in contribution for metals and minerals at 32%, cement at 30% and renewable energy at 9% while rural and urban infrastructure contribution was reduced at 20%.

items.statement: Renewable energy target above 10% of equipment rental revenue for FY26, up from 9% in H1
items.quote: This year, as of H1, it is at 9% and for the entire FY we are targeting that it will be above 10%.

items.statement: Planning to add EV trucks to logistics fleet for new opportunities with current and prospective clients
items.quote: Going forward, while we continue with the CAPEX drive in our equipment rental segment, the company is also working on addition of EV trucks to its logistics fleet with a view to tap into new opportunities with our current as well as prospective client base.

items.statement: Receivable days maintained at 85 days; net cash flow from operations up 268% to Rs 49.99 crores in H1 FY26
items.quote: This has led to the receivable days being maintained at 85 days for the same period last year. The debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.96 while the net cash flow from operations rose by a whopping 268% and stood at a healthy Rs.49.99 crores for

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.96 as of H1 FY26
items.quote: The debt-to-equity ratio stood at 0.96 while the net cash flow from operations rose by a whopping 268% and stood at a healthy Rs.49.99 crores for H1 FY26.

items.statement: Chinese crane imports increasing but no yield impact seen; yields improved over last year
items.quote: There is definitely a lot of increase in the import of cranes from China because of the demand that has been there for the last few years, and they are more cost competitive as you rightly pointed out. items.statement: Nexperia chip shortage largely covered for Q3, expected to ease by Q4 with substitution underway
items.quote: We have a reasonably high confidence that Q3 is fairly covered. We believe that the situation will ease out by Q4.

items.statement: Precious metals up 60-80% year-to-date but hedged positions offsetting impact currently
items.quote: From January to now, on average 3 precious metals have gone up between 60%-80%. So, you are absolutely right. But we are not as exposed to this phase because we have taken hedges.

items.statement: SUV EV penetration at 8.7%, up 90 bps sequentially with 30,000 cumulative electric SUVs sold
items.quote: The penetration in our portfolio is now 8.7%, which we think is a very good number at this stage of the launch with the two products that are out.

items.statement: 85% of BEV buyers are new to Mahindra, very few first-time vehicle buyers
items.quote: What we do see is a very substantial portion of non- Mahindra, almost 85 of our BEV buyers have not owned a Mahindra earlier.

items.statement: Revenue market share up 390 bps YoY in auto, LCV share up 100 bps to 53.2%, tractor share up 50 bps
items.quote: Market share, this is a remarkable number, up 390 basis points from a revenue standpoint year over year for the same quarter, literally 4 percentage points of market share gain. LCV market share, despite it being 50% plus has increased as well by 100 basis points to 53.2%

items.statement: CAFE norms draft not final, industry inputs under discussion, confident of meeting norms with EV portfolio
items.quote: So, the fundamental word draft means it is not final and we treat it as such. So, there is a process of dialogue and discussion which is on, which was the purpose of the draft, and that process is right now under discussion.

items.statement: TREM-V implementation timeline under discussion, TMA proposed delay for 25-50 HP to 2028 and <25 HP from April 2026
items.quote: Right now, there is a dialoguing on which is the TMA proposal to move the 25-50 horsepower from '2026 to '2028, that is the TMA proposal. And for the less than 25 horsepower, the date was April'26. Again, there is a conversation on to postpone that as well.

items.statement: GST simplification for farm business (from 12-18-28 structure) significantly improving working capital management
items.quote: The simplification on the working capital side for the farm business is pretty significant. I do not know whether that was as obvious earlier, that is a business which used to have a 12-18-28 kind of structure, right, and now it is far simpler for the team to manage and working capital will be better managed as a result and should free up some as well.

items.statement: No rights issues planned in near future; capital investments to continue as per growth plans
items.quote: There are no rights issues planned in the near future. Capital investments will be made in all businesses as they need them as part of our growth plans.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance GNPA maintained steadily below 4.5%, actually below 4% this quarter
items.quote: Asset quality is maintained steadily at less than 4.5 for GNPA. It is at less than 4 in fact for this quarter.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance NIM improved 47 bps, AUM grew 13%, PAT up 45% in Q2
items.quote: We also see a NIM improvement this time of 47 basis points, AUM growth of 13%. This is despite not really focusing on growth for the last couple of years but we will as I said earlier, pivot to growth now and that has overall resulted in a very strong number of operational performance, 45% profit after tax growth for this quarter.

items.statement: Tech Mahindra operating PAT up 35% YoY, margin progression on track with AI efforts accelerated via Orion launch
items.quote: Tech Mahindra on track, gains in BFSI, manufacturing and retail in a tough industry. Accelerated our AI effort, have launched Orion. Margin progression is on track as has been outlined by us as well and therefore, we feel good about where this business is and again reflected in some ways in the operational PAT number for 35% growth.

items.statement: Hospitality occupancy hurt by weather but average unit realization up 85%, member growth 1%
items.quote: Hospitality, occupancy hurt by some of the weather related issues in this quarter and that has been offset by average unit realization being much higher at 85%. We are starting to focus a lot more on quality and on the average unit realization, as compared to just number of members. So number of members, you will see 1% growth

items.statement: Nexperia chip supply risk being mitigated with substitution; dealer CESS refund matter sub judice; precious metal volatility hedged but trend continuation could increase costs
items.quote: We have a reasonably high confidence that Q3 is fairly covered. We believe that the situation will ease out by Q4. If not, I am sure you have, Raghu, been tracking Nexperia closely, it is a very low value commodity kind of chip, roughly 20 cents. So, it is not hard to substitute.

items.statement: Management commits to sustaining 30%+ CAGR over the next few years
items.quote: We are committed to sustaining 30% plus CAGR over the next few years, supported by industry tailwinds, our sales engine, technology leverage and a sharper client mix.

items.statement: FY26 PAT guidance of INR11 crores likely to be beaten given H1 performance
items.quote: But there is a good chance we will beat that because of the H1 performance.

items.statement: Current order book stands at over INR20 crores
items.quote: We ar e today sitting in an order book of over INR20 crores, and we'll definitely keep this momentum, more meetings, more demos, more wins, because it's a no -brainer

items.statement: Bidding pipeline of over INR35 crores with conservative expectation of INR8-12 crores conversion
items.quote: So, currently, we have almost -- I don't have the exact figure, but if you're asking bidding, what is in b idding, we have over INR35 crores worth of projects in bidding

items.statement: 80% of revenue from episodic work providing pipeline visibility and consistent cash conversion
items.quote: Today, 80% of our revenue is episodic, which provides pipeline visibility, seasonality balance, and more consistent cash conversion relative to one-off terms.

items.statement: Direct work share increased from 20% to 50% with target of 80% by end of FY27
items.quote: This year, we have achieved almost 50 :50 ratio, which is 50% direct work compared to last year, which was only 20% direct work. And our goal over the next year, that is by the end of FY '27, is to be at 80% direct work.

items.statement: Approved by major studios including Disney, Marvel, Netflix, Amazon, Paramount, Warner Brothers, Lionsgate, Legendary, CBS, HBO
items.quote: We are among a handful of India-origin VFX studios that have been audited and approved by TPN, Disney, Marvel, Netflix, Amazon, Paramount, Warner Brothers, Lionsgate, Legendary, CBS, HBO, and several other production studios in the U.S. and Europe.

items.statement: INR45 crore QIP to be completed in November for working capital, market presence, high-margin initiatives and partial debt reduction
items.quote: We will be completing our INR45 crore QIP fundraise in November. So, this is designed to give us additional working capital flexibility to scale delivery, invest in on-ground market presence, accelerate high-margin initiatives, and strengthen balance sheet by certain loan reduction partially from the QIP fundraise.

items.statement: Promoters intend to infuse INR20 crore via convertible warrants post-QIP
items.quote: Following the QIP, the promoters also intend to infuse INR20 crore via convertible warrants. So, t his signals unambiguous promoter confidence in Digikore Studios growth trajectory and creates skin -in- the-game alignment with all our shareholders

items.statement: INR20 crores from QIP proceeds allocated for debt reduction to strengthen balance sheet and reduce interest cost
items.quote: INR20 crores out of our fundraisers is what we plan to use for debt reduction and the balance towards working capital, primarily towards expanding our European and US presence in terms of manpower and production teams and all of that.

items.statement: VFX PAT margins expected to settle at 16-18% with blended target of 20-22% in 3-4 quarters driven by high-margin verticals
items.quote: Going forward, I anticipate VFX will settle in the same range of 16% to 18%. But our other divisions, which are extremely high margin divisions of brand jingles, or SaaS - based platforms, or VP sets monetization, I do t hink we should be able to start pushing up our margin slowly over the next few quarters, with a target of, you know, touching again, 20%, 21%, maybe 22% PA T margins over the next

items.statement: Branded content shows Kaise Banta Hai Season 2 and Heroes Season 1 now streaming on JioHotstar
items.quote: Well, I'm happy to let you know that season two of Kaise Banta Hai and season one of our new show Heroes are now streaming on JioHotstar. In fact, it just went live last week.

items.statement: Branded content revenue expected at INR10-12 crores for FY26 with 40% booked in H1
items.quote: So, this year, we should do a revenue, Digikore revenue of around INR10 crores to INR12 crores odd from our branded content shows.

items.statement: Hybrid brand jingles business averaging INR3-3.5 lakhs/week in India and UAE with ROAS of 6-8x
items.quote: Brand jingles, we are currently averaging between India and UAE at an average. For that, it will be a weekly average, actually, not a daily average. But yeah, so, it's more of a weekly average. Around INR 3 lakhs, INR3.5 lakhs a week is what we are doing in terms of brand jingles currently between India and UK.

items.statement: Board approved New York subsidiary to anchor North America growth and improve response time
items.quote: We have just got approval from our board, and we are working towards establishing a subsidiary in New York, basically to anchor North America growth and response time.

items.statement: Aggressive Europe sales drives across London, Paris, Madrid, Glasgow, Edinburgh with new vendor enrolments, active bids, NDAs and award momentum
items.quote: our recent mega sales drives across Los Angeles, London, Paris, Madrid, Glasgow, and Edinburgh have translat ed to tangible outcomes, new vendor enrolments, active bids, NDAs, and award

items.statement: Trade receivables improved with debtor days reduced from ~400 to ~200; expect majority recovery in 6-9 months
items.quote: In fact, our debtor days, if you look at it, has come down from 400 to 200 approximately, if you actually, if you do a calculation of that. So, that gives you a sign that a trade receivable has improved, not gone up.

items.statement: Other current assets increased due to WIP buildup from higher project uptake
items.quote: One of the things in the other current asset is obviously our WIP that we have, that is your stock. In normal production, you would call that stock. In services, we call that WIP, because of the uptake in the projects that have come up.

items.quote: See, the VFX margins, like you've seen, they've shrunk a little now, because everybody in the market right now are hungry tigers. Everyone is starving for 12-18 months. They are all hungry. So, you know, we also did have to cut down a little on our margin to win some projects.

items.statement: AI tools deployed for roto, clean-up, match-move, tracking and QC improving backend productivity (e.g., 3 people x 5 days -> 1 person x 0.5 day)
items.quote: So, technically, AI does not make anything good for VFX. It only helps us a little in improving our productivity by, let's say, there are certain manual tasks which we do in our production pipeline and we are able to use AI to improve, because let's say, three people spend five days to do a certain job on the backend side, AI is able to get that done, let's say, by o ne person in half a day

items.quote: And the tax rebates, obviously, is a massive magnet right now to attract work, because when the producers are going to give us, let's say, a INR2 crores or INR3 crores or INR4 crores rupee project, and that's already a massive thing compared to US and European rates. And on top of that, they get back 22.5% of the work.

items.statement: Targeting Europe revenue equal to US by end of FY26; currently almost 100% US revenue
items.quote: Now, we've come to a sizable revenue from Europe. And by the end of this year, I would like to think that Europe would be equal in US in terms of revenue mix for us, which is very important.

items.statement: No acquisition plans for 6-8 months due to AI uncertainty; greenfield approach preferred to avoid white elephant risk
items.quote: So, right now, we don't have immediate plans of acquisitions because, like I said, it could become more of a threat than a muscle for us, because if whatever reason you acquire a VFX company, pay $10 million, $20 million or $5 million also, you are acquiring also talent, you are acquiring a salary bill of probably $10 million a month. items.quote: Trump tariffs cannot be applied to services, firstly. There is no way you can tariff services. So, everybody... Pradeep: Indirect impact. Abhishek More: Right now, we have no indirect impact on the business at all. Zero. Zero indirect impact

items.quote: GST reduction of -- from 28% to 18%, where all the benefits have got passed to the customers. And I'm sure this will bring more demand for especially good brands like Adani Cement and more so, the demand for the premium cement.

These divisions formally recognize degree apprenticeships within the framework of the act and include provision of a tripartite agreement among the employer, apprentice and the academic institution.

items.statement: Staffing DSO at 7 days, overall DSO at 15 days; staffing funding exposure maintained at 14%
items.quote: DSO in Staffing business stands at 7 days and the overall grew at 15 days. Funding exposure in the Staffing business is maintained at 14% and free cash balance stands at Rs. 320 crores.

items.statement: Free cash balance Rs. 320 crores; all balance sheet metrics stable and steady
items.quote: Funding exposure in the Staffing business is maintained at 14% and free cash balance stands at Rs. 320 crores. All balance sheet metrics are stable and steady.

items.statement: HR Tech capex investments already done; only sales and marketing opex for next two quarters
items.quote: The CapEx investments are already done, it's only sales and marketing that would continue for another two quarters for us to see an improvement in the revenue for HR-tech.

items.statement: HR Tech business to reach sizable revenue and bottom-line contribution in two more quarters
items.quote: Yes, so it would take two more quarters for the HR-tech business to get into a sizable number both in terms of revenue as well as bottom line contribution.

items.statement: General staffing absolute EBITDA flat; incremental improvement expected as fixed costs absorbed and variable markup kicker comes next year
items.quote: Yes, general staffing plus DA put together, right now our absolute margins are also flat. But again, as I mentioned earlier, now that the fixed costs are absorbed, incrementally there will be an improvement in absolute profits in general staffing business as well.

items.statement: PAPM held stable; large clients at lowest PAPM growing faster; variable markup on smaller clients gives 3-3.5x PAPM but volume from large clients
items.quote: Like we had always called out, the large customers have been growing larger and they are the ones who typically are at the lowest PAPM. But I think our focus of trying to get variable markup model in place and some element of a higher traction of customers in the medium and small who pay a higher PAPM has what has been kind of holding the PAPMs, per se.

items.statement: BFSI showing early stabilization with controlled hiring in Tier 2/3 and frontline roles; consumer resilient in semi-urban/rural; telecom targeted expansion
items.quote: BFSI remains in transition following the hiring slowdown through FY '25 due to regulatory curbs on unsecured lending. Q2 FY '26 showed early signs of stabil ization. Several banks and NBFCs resumed controlled hiring, particularly in Tier 2 and 3 locations and in frontline roles across sales, collections

items.statement: Watchful of incremental government notifications; no specific annual concern but policy changes could be headwind
items.quote: I do think that government has been giving incremental notifications on a continuous basis, some way or the other. So anything of that sort coming to play is really where I would be watchful about.

items.statement: No internal recruiter headcount increase in last two years; continuous productivity improvement via AI and technology
items.quote: On the recruiter front, we have not been increasing headcounts internally in the last two years. On the margin front of the specialized staffing business, we do not do firm hiring, we only do the staffing side in our specialized staffing business.

items.statement: Specialized staffing margin improvement unlikely to double; focused on incremental improvement as GCC share rises
items.quote: While there is an element of margin improvement that comes to play as GCC share goes up, I think doubling it is unlikely, but we will work to improving it.

items.statement: Aspirational profit growth higher than revenue growth; double-digit high-teen EBITDA CAGR aspirationally
items.quote: It should be. Aspirationally, that's what it is.

items.statement: Global business 4% of specialized staffing net revenue and EBITDA positive; integrated consulting-led approach creating offshore opportunities
items.quote: Our global business contributed a net revenue of about 4% in the last quarter and has become EBITDA positive. Synergies between India delivery and global operations have created an integrated consulting-led starting approach, opening new revenue streams and offshore delivery opportunities for us.

items.statement: All three employment businesses hit bottom and growing; net positive growth in degree apprenticeship post-NEEM exit
items.quote: Subject to all things being status quo, we do think all three businesses have hit the bottom and will kind of continue to grow. The only variable that we see is any new guideline or government notifications that come to play depending on sectors or specific to time.

items.statement: Madras High Court quashed PF/80JJAA litigation for AY 2017-18; all refunds received; no reversal or incremental provision needed
items.quote: So, there is no reversal that has to be made in this regard, Amit, because we have received all refunds. So even for those years that the department has gone for a litigation, so they have already cleared all the refunds.

items.statement: Technology and productivity initiatives ongoing to handle future growth with same headcount
items.quote: I think also, the various initiatives on technology and productivity gain improvements should continue to play out for us to be able to handle the growth that comes in future with the same headcounts that we have.

items.statement: Revenue expected to grow at 45-50% CAGR over FY26 and FY27 driven by core business excluding acquisition
items.quote: Looking ahead, we expect revenue to grow at a CAGR of 45% to 50% over FY26 and FY27 driven solely by the core business excluding any contributions from the recent acquisition.

items.statement: Unit 3 Phase 1 structure complete, Phase 2 civil started, partial production begun, full production by end FY26 or Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the capex side, Unit 3 Phase 1 Single structure is complete. Phase 2 civil structure has already started and partial production in the phase 1 has already started and the full-fledged production will be starting from end of this financial year or probably by Q1 next financial year.

items.statement: Unit 3 will enhance production capacity 8x over current facility
items.quote: If you compare the present facility and once Unit 3 is ready, we are enhancing our capacity to eight times. Present this thing to, once our Unit 3 is ready, it is almost eight times enhancing the production capacity.

items.statement: Order book slightly under INR800 crores as of September end plus new development orders received in last 1-1.5 months
items.quote: So, little less than INR800 crores is the order book as on September end, actually. Okay. Over and above that in last 1, 1.5 month, we have received a few more orders, you know, and little amount of production orders, but significant amount of new development orders for the next generation weapon programs and next generation platform programs, actually.

items.statement: Order book expected to reach 3x FY25 level by March or Q1 FY27 driven by large cap projects like MIGM, QRSAM, ESWT
items.quote: We have initially given a guidance by March, you know, we will be having owing to some large caps projects which we were expecting. As the day stands, it is actually going on track. We are also fingers crossed waiting keenly for it. Even if it in case misses by March, you know, by first quarter, it should happen.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 28% in H1 FY26, Q2 at 26.3%; margins vary quarterly by product mix but expected in 26-28% range for FY26
items.quote: Yes. As we told, quarter-on-quarter basis, the different product mix have a different margin profiles actually. So, broadly, it is all guided based on that actually. So, it will be varying in those ranges actually.

items.statement: Production currently 25-30% of revenue vs development; expected to rise to 40-45% as large projects convert to production
items.quote: 25% to 30% in between band, you know, is the production size compared to the development, development to core development, development cum production orders, actually. Going forward, it may increase up to 45%, you know, that is what we are contemplating.

items.statement: Receivables INR360 crores; significant reduction expected by Q4 FY26 as long gestation projects complete and production orders with 30-day payment cycles increase
items.quote: So this financial year end, you will see a significant reduction in the receivables, actually. Some of the long gestation projects which the receivable, this thing is over. It has almost come to a final phases, actually. I think, Q3 to some extent visibility will be there. Q4 significant reduction will be there.

items.statement: Export opportunity pipeline >INR100 crores for critical avionic system; export process requires MOD/DRDO approvals; no revenue split guidance yet
items.quote: As the day stands, we are having a little over about, INR100 crores opportunity of, you know, as an export order, which is presently a kind of a development project, actually. Okay. And it's a very critical avionic system. And as far as the mix is concerned, at this point of time, we are not able to give any guidance for it.

items.statement: ALWT AON approval received; EHWT order from Navy expected by March; QRSAM in RFQ stage with order expected before March or Q1 FY27; MIGM DAC approval expected by Dec, order 2-3 months after
items.quote: ALWT AON approval has already come, which is there in the market last couple of weeks back, Ministry of Defense already given. You will also see a good order flowing for EHWT to Bharat Dynamics Limited from Indian Navy and we having a significant participation in the program, we are also going to get. Most likely that this EHWT order, most likely we may get within March, is what we are getting to

items.statement: BrahMos: one subsystem order received, 5-6 projects in technical evaluation, more orders expected in 2-3 months
items.quote: BrahMos, one project already we are doing. And if I remember correct, some five to six projects already we have participated, technical evaluation is going on. Once that completes, they are going to decide actually. We are expecting more and more orders from BrahMos next two, three months' time.

items.statement: Mechatronic Fuse ToT from DRDO absorbed; prototypes in 1-2 quarters, validation in ~1 year, customer interest already emerging
items.quote: Mechatronic Fuse, recently we have taken a mechatronic, so basically a mechanical fuse. We have developed few mechanical and mechanical plus electronic fuses indigenously. But for certain applications, instead of redeveloping, we have taken a ToT from DRDO, which is applicable for certain motor applications, that is the thing. The opportunity size is very big, it is a recent ToT. So, we will be ab

items.statement: UK order INR113 crores held; expecting more orders from Saudi and Europe; overseas companies auditing Unit 3 for MOUs
items.quote: I think we have already announced one project, a good project from the UK. We are holding one order. It is the INR113 crores order we are holding and we are expecting more and more orders from Saudi also. We are expecting some orders and Europe side also we are expecting some orders.

items.statement: Government considering allowing wholly-owned foreign defense subsidiaries as Indian vendors; management sees both risk and opportunity but limited impact on DRDO strategic programs
items.quote: Particularly, you know, we would not say that, it's not a welcoming gesture, but definitely not a very good move is what we can say. But in one way, we can also say that by this fully owned companies, which are 100% investment by these companies. Once these companies start establishing their offices here in India, a lot of further, you know, ecosystem also gets developed, and the existing ecosyste

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduced to ~35%; targeting zero pledge within 6 months
items.quote: Yes, like if you see, we are reducing. I think next one week time, we are going to see, you know, I think every month we are reducing something. Yes, definitely. Next six months' time, I'm going to close all the pledge part. That's what I'm planning.

items.statement: Board evaluating funding options for IDL overhaul and growth; will announce when approved
items.quote: I would reserve my answer for this. You know, there are certain things which we are contemplating as and when the Board gives the kind of an approval, I think, we will reach out to you for packaging.

name: Home First Finance Company India Limited

items.statement: AUM grew 26.3% y-o-y and 5.2% q-o-q to Rs. 14,178 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: The AUM growth remains strong, growing at 26.3% y-o-y and 5.2% q-o-q to reach Rs. 14,178 crores.

items.statement: Guiding for 25% plus AUM growth for FY26
items.quote: We are guiding to that 25% plus AUM growth, so this quarter it was 26%.

items.statement: Credit cost expected at 40 bps for full year FY26
items.quote: On credit cost, we are still looking at 40 bps for the full year.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing targeted under 8% by March 2026
items.quote: We are aiming to get it under 8%, let us say, by March.

items.statement: Spreads expected to be maintained in 5% to 5.25% range
items.quote: The spread, we should be able to maintain in the 5% to 5.25% that we have always guided.

items.statement: NIMs expected to expand faster than spreads in coming quarters
items.quote: As far as the NIM s are concerned, they will marginally expand from here with now large part of the cash consumption done post the QIP and leverage also picking up. So, NIMs will expand faster than spreads

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q2 FY26; plan to add 4-5 branches in Q3 FY26
items.quote: In this quarter, we added five branches, with the latest additions comprising three in Maharashtra, one in Andhra Pradesh and one in Gujarat. We plan to add four to five new branches in the upcoming quarter.

items.statement: Branch expansion guidance of 5-7 branches per quarter going forward
items.quote: Branch count, again, around that five to seven branches per quarter is what we have been maintaining as a guidance.

items.statement: Net interest margin improved to 5.4% in Q2 FY26 from 5.2% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Net interest margin for Q2 was 5.4%, up from 5.2% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Ex-co-lending spread at 5.3% with cost of borrowing at 8.1% and disbursement yield at 13.3%
items.quote: With proactive management, we were able to reduce our cost of borrowing, excluding co-lending, by 30 bps at 8.1%, supporting our ex-co-lending spread of 5.3%. Disbursement yields for the quarter were at 13.3%.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing reduced by 30 bps q-o-q to 8.1% ex-co-lending; incremental borrowing at even more competitive rates
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing has already reduced by 30 bps, driven by downward shift in benchmark rates, with incremental borrowing now being secured at even more competitive rates.

items.statement: Individual housing loans constitute 83% of portfolio; LAP growing faster due to base effect
items.quote: Our origination yield continues to be healthy at 13.3% despite an 83% share of individual housing loans.

items.statement: Co-lending disbursements up 179% y-o-y and 24% q-o-q to Rs. 97 crores; co-lending book at Rs. 508 crores (3.6% of AUM); target 10% of disbursements
items.quote: Our disbursements under co-lending business increased by 179% y-o-y and 24% q-o-q to Rs. 97 crores for Q2, taking co-lending book to Rs. 508 crores or 3.6% of the total AUM. Co-lending will continue to be an important part of our strategy to strengthen our ability to cater to higher ticket size segments. We aim to take co-lending contribution to 10% of disbursements as we scale.

items.statement: Long-term 1+DPD expected around 5%, 30+DPD between 3-3.5%
items.quote: Broadly, I would say , if you were to ask me for a very long-term trend, I would say it should remain in that 5% ballpark number. Siraj Khan: 1+DPD, and 30+? Manoj Viswanathan: 30+, between 3% to 3.5%, in that range it should be, on a long-term basis

items.statement: Disbursements at Rs. 1,289 crores, up 9.6% y-o-y and 3.7% q-o-q; growth moderated due to proactive credit restrictions in stressed segments
items.quote: Disbursements for the quarter stood at Rs. 1,289 crores, up 9.6% y-o-y and 3.7% q-o-q. Overall, disbursement momentum has remained healthy despite subdued macroeconomic environment stemming from prolonged monsoon and tariff uncertainty.

items.statement: Rejection rates increased; certain customer cohorts restricted proactively due to delinquency trends
items.quote: Yes. In fact, rejection rate has gone up and, in some cases, we have softly conveyed to the market that these are certain segments of customers that we will not be onboarding.

items.statement: Market share increased from 1.5% to 2.2% over three years; 4-5% in mature markets like Indore, Surat, Ahmedabad, Nagpur
items.quote: If you see a three -year period, market share has moved up from 1.5% to about 2.2%. This is across all the markets that we are operating in. Of course, in some of the specific markets our market share is touching, somewhere between 4% to 5% where we have ope rated for a longer period

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 48.4% (Tier 1 48.0%) as of Sep'25
items.quote: Our Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio as of Sep'25 stands at 48.4%, with Tier 1 at 48.0%.

items.statement: Employee count ~1,700; attrition inched up to 34% from ~30%; productivity lower due to moderated disbursements
items.quote: Attrition has slightly inched up. We used to be trending at around 30%, but last quarter it was 34%. But for productivity, the number is basically a derivative of disbursement. Since we have moderated disbursement, the productivity is also looking a bit lower.

items.statement: PMAY 2.0 traction: 3,500+ applications received, 38 customers received first subsidy tranche, 53 more approved
items.quote: PMAY 2.0 scheme saw further traction. As on date, we have received over 3,500 customer applications. Of these, 38 customers have already received their first tranche of the subsidy, with an additional 53 cases approved, where the subsidy will get credited shortly.

items.statement: Tariff uncertainty impacting leather (Chennai), textile (Coimbatore-Tirupur), diamond (Surat), shrimp (southern TN/coastal AP); spillover from MFI/MSME stress amplifying delinquencies
items.quote: It got accentuated by this whole tariff uncertainty. And so, in some places, the impact became even larger. That is really what it is. Also, some of it is also spilling over to the disbursement side, because when you see a clear impact in certain segments, then you obviously do not want to underwrite those segments.

items.statement: Digital adoption strong: 83% approvals via account aggregator, >80% loans digitally fulfilled, 96% customers on mobile app, 87% service requests digital
items.quote: 83% of our approvals in Q2 were facilitated via the account aggregator framework. o More than 80% of our loans are digitally fulfilled through e-agreements and e-NACH mandates. o 96% of our customers registered on the mobile app, with 87% of the service requests now raised

items.statement: ESG: 240 Green Homes certified; Morningstar Sustainalytics reaffirmed 'Low ESG Risk' with improved score 13.6 vs 16.2
items.quote: During Q2, we got 50 additional Green Homes certified, taking the total to 240. I am pleased to share that Morningstar Sustainalytics reaffirmed our 'Low ESG Risk' category with an improved score of 13.6 versus 16.2 last year.

items.statement: UPI interchange is 1.1-1.2% to issuer; merchant pays ~1% with acquiring margin added on top
items.quote: UPI has a concept of interchange, which means that the issuer side will get something like 1.1 - 1.2%, depending on the category of merchants. Everything around it comes out about merchants paying 1%.

items.statement: Acquiring business can sell to merchants at 1.5% or 1.9% depending on commercial choice
items.quote: So can we sell it for 1.5 or 1.9%, depending on who and what commercial is the choice of acquiring business, which is also approved into our acquiring side of business.

items.statement: EMI ecosystem aggregates financial institutions, brands, and merchants; three subvention types exist
items.quote: So three kinds of EMI work in the market. Straightforward, customer base. Number two, brand subventions. Number three, financial institutions also subventions. And in one product, like Apple, by the way, all three could be subventioning.

items.statement: Paytm is gaining market share in EMI and capturing large market during festivities
items.quote: We are cornering, actually. We are taking away the market share, chipping off the market share from the erstwhile existing players.

items.statement: Hired 5,000 sales employees this quarter vs typical 1-2k to dominate merchant ecosystem offline
items.quote: This quarter it's been 5000. What's the sort of thought process behind, you know, hiring so many? Mr. Vijay Shekhar Sharma: You want to dominate in the merchant ecosystem. I will acquire a large number of enterprise onboarding now offline or online. And we will be even more aggressive in offline small merchants. I mean, 5000, I wish we could have done like 2x of this

items.statement: AI agents for small businesses will generate subscription and inference fee revenue
items.quote: Paytm is selling agents for small business and charging subscription and inference fees once the subscription usage grows ahead of it.

items.statement: No material capital investment plan for AI; investments beyond $20-50M will be proactively announced
items.quote: Whenever we are going to do any capital investment, capital investment is an investment that goes beyond $20 - $50 million onwards, we will be very much sizing it up, we will be very much proactively announcing it in advance, et cetera. So right now, what you are hearing, there is no material investment plan here.

items.statement: Postpaid launched in September; numbers currently insignificant; merchant loans growing QoQ with better collection performance increasing take rate
items.quote: Postpaid was launched in September. So the numbers, financial numbers currently are insignificant. That was not a driver. Merchant loan continues with a nice trajectory of quarter on quarter growth on volume terms. In revenue terms, we are seeing better collection performance, which is increasing take rate.

items.statement: Personal loans facing headwinds but slightly better take rates; non-lending financial services (Paytm Money, Wealth, gold) showing positive signs
items.quote: Personal loan, we have given commentary that due to headwinds, we're not seeing growth there, but we are seeing slightly better, slightly better take rates on economics, but again, not a major driver. And we are seeing this growth in other financial services like Paytm money or Wealth and gold, as Vijay mentioned.

items.statement: Focus shifting from bottom-line generation to revenue generation; acceleration expected on revenue-generating line items
items.quote: Up till now, we are bottom line generating focused. We have started to become revenue generating focused, so you can start seeing it.

items.statement: Credit card on UPI market share is better than generic UPI market share; generic UPI share skewed by P2P
items.quote: Our credit card, UPI credit card market share is better for us than our generic UPI market share. Generic UPI market share is actually skewed towards P2P transactions because they're always larger in volume, per ticket is very large.

items.statement: Subscription revenues expected to be overtaken by MDR revenues in near future
items.quote: We do foresee that, that month is not very far when our subscription revenues get toppled by our MDR revenues.

items.statement: Omni-channel merger enables new VAS (spend analytics, settlement, payout) increasing per-payment revenue
items.quote: Yes, not just this element, but there are other VAS elements like spend analytics, like settlement, like payout. All those things start to show up as new value-add items. So per payment, we make more bps or more money than we will make standalone and offline or standalone and online.

items.statement: Postpaid early days with tens of thousands users; targeting couple of million; 10-12M previous customers on platform
items.quote: Numbers are very early, tens of thousands. So the opportunity is way more forward. I mean, the good thing I can say is that we experienced that this country, we had signed up around 10 - 12 million customers.

items.statement: GMV growth should be higher than UPI growth (20%) driven by market share gains and improving unit economics
items.quote: We do think that if UPI is growing at 20%, our GMV growth should be higher than that. And that's what we'll continue to drive.

items.statement: Guided 5-7% quarter-on-quarter AUM growth and credit cost may increase 10-15 bps before peaking
items.value: 5-7% QoQ AUM growth; credit cost +10-15 bps
items.quote: We hope to continue to grow at 5% to 7% AUM quarter-on-quarter. And we hope that the credit cost here will start getting range-bound, but may increase another 10-15 basis points from here.

items.statement: ROE guidance maintained at 15%
items.quote: We had guided a 15% ROE. Let us first build to that and then we will talk about plans ahead. At the moment, the guidance continues to be 15%.

items.statement: Spread at 9.05% in Q2, above guided range; no further increase anticipated
items.quote: No, we are already above our guided range and do not anticipate any further increases from here.

items.statement: AUM reached Rs 10,000 crore, up 29% YoY and 6% QoQ; MSME AUM 82% of total
items.quote: Our AUM as of September is Rs. 9,938 crore, and as Aseem said, we achieved Rs. 10,000 crore now, and this is with a growth of 29% on a YOY basis and 6% on a QOQ basis.

items.statement: Added 5 branches in Q2, total 220; plan 20-25 branches per year
items.quote: We have added five branches during the quarter, with the total branch count at 220 as of September 2025.

items.statement: Gold loans offered in 185 of 220 branches; plan to add ~15 gold loan branches in next two quarters
items.quote: We are currently closer to 185-odd branches out of 220 branches where we offer gold. Incrementally, you would see more number of branches coming in for gold. My sense is that in the next two quarters, we should add close to around 15 branches for gold.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost down 80 bps vs book cost at start of fiscal; OPEX down 112 bps since IPO
items.value: 80 bps borrowing cost reduction; 112 bps OPEX reduction
items.quote: Incremental borrowing cost is down 80 basis points over the book cost at the beginning of this fiscal. Over time, this will keep feeding into the P&L. Cost of operations has come down 112 basis points since our IPO, and incremental benefits will keep feeding into the P&L.

items.statement: GNPA 2.77%, PCR 46.17%, credit cost 1.29% in Q2; 1+ DPD flow calmed but not fully stemmed
items.quote: In terms of asset quality, our GNPA is range-bound in Q2 at 2.77%, with PCR at 46.17%, with credit cost at 1.29% for the quarter.

items.statement: Stopped lending below Rs 7 lakh; minimum CIBIL 700; tightened credit screens further this quarter
items.quote: We have further tightened our credit screens, stopped lending below 7 lakhs and raised the gate of entry to a CIBIL of 700 at a minimum level.

items.statement: Karnataka exposure ~12% of AUM; portfolio stressed since Jan 2025 ordinance; recovery will take several quarters
items.quote: Karnataka is a classic case in point where a superb portfolio till January '25 got rudely shaken up in two months, and this now is going to take several quarters to fix once it starts to flow.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity sub 2x; permitted up to 5x by covenants; target 3-4x before raising equity
items.quote: Our debt-to-equity is sub 2, while asset-to-equity is 3, but debt-to-equity is sub 2. From a banking covenant point of view, we are permitted to go to debt equity of 5. But what we believe is anywhere between 3 and 4 is somewhere we will go to the market and start raising equity capital.

items.statement: ROA 4.56%, ROE 14.09% in Q2; PAT Rs 109 crore, up 30% YoY and 8% QoQ
items.quote: Our Return on Average AUM for the quarter is 4.56%, with Return on Average Tangible Equity further improving from 13.53% in Q1 to 14.09% in Q2. We made a PAT of Rs. 109 crore for the quarter, thereby reporting a growth of 30% on a YOY basis and 8% on a QOQ basis.

items.statement: Average ticket size increased to Rs 10.2 lakh from ~9 lakh; driven by higher co-origination with ICICI
items.quote: If you look at our average ticket size for this particular quarter, that's moved up marginally from closer to 9 lakhs to 10.2 lakhs for this quarter, and that's largely also because of a higher co-origination with ICICI.

items.statement: 95-96% of new disbursals to customers with CIBIL >700; approval rates dropped below 40% from 45-50%
items.quote: If I were to talk about the new disbursal, almost I think 95%-96% of the customers onboarded are more than 700 and some of them more than 725.

items.statement: Disbursements ~Rs 800 crore per quarter; leaving ~10% on table due to tighter filters
items.quote: We are disbursing close to around Rs. 800 crores in a quarter. If we were to just stay where we are, that's Rs. 3,200 crores in a year.

items.statement: NBFCs lack SARFAESI advantage available to HFCs; resolution timeline 3-3.5x longer; regulatory arbitrage exists
items.quote: It is a level playing field that NBFCs deserve to be on. And there is a regulatory arbitrage against the NBFC, and I hope that it gets recognized and removed.

items.statement: Political risk and climate risk emerging; Karnataka ordinance caused portfolio stress; credit cost may rise 10-15 bps before peaking
items.quote: What has changed over the years are the two risks that did not exist to this level earlier, political risk and climate risk. Karnataka is a classic case in point where a superb portfolio till January '25 got rudely shaken up in two months.

items.statement: Gold loan business employs ~1,500-1,600 staff across front and back end
items.quote: Coming to answer your question on gold, we have close to around 185 odd branches. There are close to around 8 to 10 people in a branch that comes in. So, roughly around 1500 to 1600 odd employees, including the front end and the back end would be on the gold side.

items.statement: Promoter Aseem Dhru sold shares for personal liquidity; all personal wealth was in company stock
items.quote: Since eight years, all the money that I have ever made is in this stock, and the purpose is to create liquidity for myself.

items.statement: Order book visibility remains strong for contrast media marketed products and NCE intermediates; iodinated intermediate commercial scale expected in Q4 FY26
items.quote: The visibility of our order book in this segment on the marketed product is stable. The order book for intermediate for the NCE molecule is encouraging. The commercial scale of the iodinated intermediate is expected in Q4 of this financial year.

items.statement: Mahad backward integration facility CAPEX increased from Rs 250 cr to Rs 300 cr due to automation; Rs 135 cr incurred in H1 FY26; commissioning on track for H2 FY26
items.quote: We envisage that the earlier planned CAPEX of Rs. 250 crores that we had spoken to you about, this will increase to about Rs. 300 crores because of this automation. Of this, we have already incurred about Rs. 135 crores in H1 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Vizag Phase-I greenfield project at ~Rs 1,000 cr for 4 blocks (2 contrast media, 1 sweetener, 1 multipurpose); master planning complete; groundbreaking expected next quarter; completion by FY28
items.quote: In Phase-I, at an approximate CAPEX of Rs. 1,000 crores, we are planning 4 blocks, 2 for Contrast Media, 1 for high-intensity Sweetener that Shiven mentioned in his opening comments, and the fourth block, which is a multipurpose block, where we will do several new chemistries, including the peptide fragments for GLPs. We envisage that by FY '28, we will complete Phase-I. The master planning of thi

items.statement: R&D center planned in Hyderabad at ~Rs 40 cr for peptides, GLP-1 intermediates, biocatalysts, immobilized catalysts to strengthen innovator pipeline
items.quote: A state -of-the-art R&D center is being planned at a cost of about Rs. 40 crores and we will have newer chemistry platforms like peptides, intermediates for GLP 1s, biocatalysts, particularly on the immobilized catalysts, and work to augment and strengthen the innovator -oriented pipeline of the company with a focus once again on chronic diseases.
