items.statement: ALMM List 2 implementation from June 2026 will mandate local cell procurement
items.quote: ALCM or we call it ALMM list 2. So, that will be implemented from the June of 2026. So, that will make all cell, sorry, module manufacturers to buy the local cells.

items.statement: Many new entrants lack industry depth; Alpex focuses on understood businesses (cell, frame, EPC)
items.quote: Many people are not from the industry without solid backgrounds or solid knowledge base. So, they are coming up with these projects and because the valuations in the stock exchange are reasonably good, I would say. And that is attracting many, once again, not to go against anyone, but yes, non-serious kind of people are trying to join the bandwagon.

items.statement: Overcapacity risk mitigated by vertical integration and ALMM; slight margin pressure possible
items.quote: Since we are vertically integrated and at the same time, yes, vertically integrated means backward and forward integration. The cell with the ALMM already in place, our cell plant, the plant is coming up. So, we do not see any dip in demand. Yes, there might be a slight margin pressure, but it will not be too large.

items.statement: Forming JVs for Junction Box and other components to insulate profits
items.quote: And we are again also forming joint ventures for Junction Box and some other businesses to, I would say, safeguard and insulate our profits.

items.statement: First in India to produce G12R TOPCon cells directly, skipping mono-PERC
items.quote: We will be the first company to come up with G12R cell directly, which is the most efficient and most popular worldwide cell size.

items.statement: Management team (Vipin, Dhamija, Sakshi, Aditya, plant heads) described as pillars driving growth
items.quote: Mr. Vipin Sehgal, Sakshi, Mr. Dhamija, Aditya and Monica and our plant heads and our top team, we call them pillars. So, these make a company and this company is on a solid footing and ready to take this upcoming growth.

items.statement: Management confident of meeting double-digit revenue growth aspiration for full year FY26 despite H1 decline
items.quote: I'm very confident of meeting these targets.

items.statement: Standalone order book excluding small pumps at Rs.2,127 crores, up 13% YoY
items.quote: Excluding the small pumps business, our standalone order book stands at Rs.2,127 crores, a strong 13% growth over the previous year, underscoring a healthy pipeline and sustained customer confidence.

items.statement: International order book expanded 25% YoY to Rs.1,289 crores
items.quote: While the UK operations faced temporary softness due to delay of certain orders to subsequent quarters, the overall international order book remains s trong, expanding 25% year- on-year to Rs.1,289 crores

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA Rs.124 crores at 12% margin; H1 EBITDA Rs.251 crores; moderation due to product mix and forex revaluation
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs.124 crores with margins at 12%. For the first half of fiscal year '26, EBITDA was Rs.251 crores. The year-on-year moderation was primarily due to changes in product mix and forex revaluation impact.

items.statement: Demand across small pumps and industrial segments remained robust despite extended monsoon impact
items.quote: However, demand across both the small pumps and industrial segments remained robust, demonstrating the inherent strength and resilience of our diversified portfolio.

items.statement: Group captive solar implemented at TKSL foundry to reduce energy costs; digitization and EREP packages at subsidiaries
items.quote: One other thing that we've done is the Group Captive Solar to ensure that costs, especially in our foundry at TKSL, the energy costs can be brought down.

items.statement: Debottlenecking at KPML to match small pump business output; improved machining and processing lines
items.quote: As far as KPML is concerned, we have taken a few steps to ensure that the output can be in step with the small pump business. As you're aware, the small pump business is heavily dependent on KPML for motor components and motors. So we've been able to put in facilities as well as improve the machining lines as well as the process -- other processing lines to ensure that output can be faster and the

items.statement: Zero receivables exposure on Jal Jeevan Mission due to strict commercial policies; pumps withheld until payment certainty
items.quote: As far as exposure on receivables is concerned, it is zero. As you are aware, and I mentioned that in my speech as well, the company maintains its strict commercial policies. do not dispatch anything from the factory unless we are sure of the payment.

items.statement: US firefighting market share 15-20%; India firefighting market share 55-60%
items.quote: In firefighting, our market share in the US continues to be about between 15% and 20%. In India, of course, our share in firefighting is much higher at -- closer to 55% to 60%.

items.statement: UK deindustrialization due to high power costs (GBP280/MWh vs GBP120 Germany, GBP52 Sweden) reducing service contracts in chemicals/steel; offsetting with water/power contracts
items.quote: I think over the last few calls, I've mentioned the point that you have made that there has been heavy deindustrialization in the UK, because the power prices are close to GBP280 a megawatt hour. If you compare that to Germany, it's about GBP120 per megawatt hour. And if you compare it to Sweden, it's about GBP52 a megawatt hour.

items.statement: Data center focus in US: ~25-30 projects executed; 4-5 projects on shop floor; addressable systems include fire, primary/secondary cooling, intake water
items.quote: Till now, maybe we've done about 25 to 30 projects. And at the moment, any time in our plant, we have about four to five projects worth of data centers in the US because that's mainly where a lot of the data center work is happening.

items.statement: Nuclear primary coolant pump development progressing: hydraulic performance proven; main casting in progress
items.quote: The progress continues. There are various components of that for the primary pump. And as far as we are concerned, I think like I said earlier, the hydraulic performance is proved. The casting of the main one is in progress.

items.statement: Provisions for doubtful debts reducing quarterly; Rs.15 crores in H1 FY26 vs Rs.41 crores full FY25; policy-based provisioning despite good recoveries
items.quote: I think if you see the numbers, it is reducing on a quarterly basis. And I think -- it is as per our policy, we need to provide it is passed through P&L. It's our policy, we need to provide that in our books.

items.statement: Mr. Chheda on leave; Mr. Hemant Shaligram (AVP, Deputy) representing finance on call
items.quote: As Mr. Chheda is on leave, Mr. Hemant Shaligram, AVP, who is his Deputy, is also here.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 40-50% CAGR year-on-year; may surpass in H1 FY26
items.quote: We already have given the guidelines of 40%, 50% CAGR year-on-year. And probably, this time, we may surpass it.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue projection of Rs 250-280 crore
items.quote: And in first half of the year, we have given the projections of around ₹250 crore plus, somewhere around ₹270 crores, ₹280 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target around 20% on the higher side; PAT margin sustainable at 15% plus/minus a couple of percent
items.quote: We already have stated like in terms of EBITDA and PAT to what we focus is upcoming trending technologies and ODM kind of a model. So, EBITDA and PAT level probably like 20% on a Northern side of it, probably we can expect that. And PAT also 15% plus or minus a couple of percent here and there definitely is going to be a sustainable one.

items.statement: PAT margin target 15% plus/minus 1-2% for H2 FY26
items.quote: That would be a bonus. But whatever right now, we are targeting 15% plus, minus 1 or 2.

items.statement: Order book at end of September stands at Rs 4,635 million, about 3x FY25 revenue
items.quote: Our order book as of the end of September stands at a record-breaking ₹4,635 million, which is about 3x our fiscal year 2025 revenue.

items.statement: Major deals include Rs 975 million ODM contract with US infrastructure firm, domestic AI IoT box build order for 50,000 units worth over Rs 4.62 crore, and strategic order from Navratna PSU in communications
items.value: Rs 975 million ODM contract; 50,000 units AI IoT box build; Navratna PSU order
items.quote: On one hand, we have a ₹975 million ODM contract with leading U.S. infrastructure firm. We have a domestic AI IoT box build order for 50,000 units worth over 4.62 Crores, as well as a strategic order from a Navratna PSU in the communications domain.

items.statement: Received tooling and prototype manufacturing order from existing Texas-based drone military customer for naval and ground-based troop applications
items.quote: We've received a tooling and prototype manufacturing order from an existing Texas-based drone military customer. This project supports the naval as well as ground-based troop applications and marks Aimtron's next major step into high precision design and prototyping for the defence industry.

items.statement: Started construction on new 3-acre greenfield facility with six state-of-the-art SMT lines and dedicated ODM research and defence zone
items.quote: We've started construction on a new 3-acre greenfield facility, which will include six state-of-the-art SMT lines as well as a dedicated ODM research and defence zone helping us build smarter, faster and greener manufacturing for the future.

items.statement: Greenfield facility to be operational with first SMT line by end of next year Q3 or early Q4; two SMT lines added per year thereafter
items.quote: Initially, one SMT lines, we are planning to get it operational by end of next year, Q3 or early Q4.

items.statement: Current capacity Rs 450-500 crore; new greenfield adds another Rs 500 crore capacity to reach Rs 1,000 crore revenue capability
items.quote: Basically for ₹1,000 crores like to what current capacity we have is around ₹450 crores to ₹500 crores, the current infrastructure that we Aimtron Electronics Limited (AIMT) H1 FY26 Post Earnings Conference Call November 6, 2025 have. So, our next new coming facility that we are going to add up. So that is going to have additional ₹500 crores kind of capacity, on top of the current ₹500

items.statement: Maintenance capex 3-5% of top line over next three years
items.quote: 3% to 5%. So next three years, we no need more than…

items.statement: One SMT line can generate approximately Rs 100 crore revenue; current five SMT lines (four in Vadodara, one in Bangalore)
items.quote: So probably even the current SMT lines to what we have in state-of-the-art. So, with one SMT line, we can approximately generate around ₹100 crores kind of a revenue.

items.statement: Box build contribution 35% in H1 FY26, expected to increase to over 50% in H2 FY26
items.quote: So box build in first half of the year was almost 35%. And down the line, that would increase to more than 50% in second half of the year.

items.statement: Focus shifting to ODM model and complete system integration; targeting Tier 1 prospects with larger RFQs
items.quote: Way forward like strategies, more focusing on ODM model and the complete system integration.

items.statement: Domestic revenue 60-65% with global clientele; export revenue 35-40% in H1 FY26
items.quote: And so, this time, almost like 60%, 65% was our domestic revenue with global clientele. And then down the line, around 35%, 40% was approximately an export market.

items.statement: New remote sales office in Germany and office in Texas, US under Aimtron Electronics India
items.quote: Our geographical expansion is in place, like post IP also, we started one remote sales office in Germany. And then one office in Texas, U.S. under Aimtron Electronics, India directly.

items.statement: Exploring participation in PLI ECMS scheme for electronic component manufacturing; already working on ECMS component side
items.quote: PLI ECMS scheme. We are also exploring on that front. We already explored like a couple of things on that. So, once we have a right time, probably, we'll go with that discussion. But ECMS on component side, we already have started working on that front.

items.statement: Exploring SFT (small fibre optics) under ECMS due to traction in telecom and network security
items.quote: We are exploring on ECMS, Electronic Component Manufacturing Scheme and specific to SFT small fibre optics, but probably we'll give you more glimpse when we get 100% clarity on it.

items.statement: Evaluating 5-6 M&A opportunities; Nirmal visited all six facilities; preliminary discussions focused on culture, talent, and access to new sectors; not replacing organic growth
items.quote: We have a lot of expertise in how we can manufacture well. We have a lot of expertise in driving profitability from a seemingly low margin business structure. And for us finding a company with the right culture, finding a company with good talent and helping guide them towards a stronger bottom line performance can be something that can bring a lot of value to the table.

items.statement: Company debt-free as of 30th September 2025
items.quote: Till today, we are still debt-free as on 30th September.

items.statement: EMS industry projected to reach Rs 500 billion by 2030; government targeting $1 trillion opportunity; ODM market globally $1.2 trillion in 2024, projected $2 trillion+ by 2030
items.value: Rs 500 billion EMS; $1 trillion govt target; ODM $2 trillion+
items.quote: Industry insights, like by 2030, everyone is expecting ₹500 billion, and that's even government is tailwinding this sector on how can we just see to it. And down the line, even AI contribution to like what target we are eyeing out Government of India. So the $1 trillion opportunity is something that we are eyeing on.

items.statement: Defence programmes have longer qualification cycles, lumpy nature, higher working capital needs; consciously limiting near-term contribution to double-digit percentage of revenue
items.quote: Because if you see defence programme have like much longer qualification cycles and they are lumpy nature with higher working capital needs. So, we would rather grow sustainably, then change the near-term optics.

items.statement: Focus on culture fit and talent in M&A evaluation; Aimtron culture of humility, teamwork, performance to be maintained
items.quote: when going and evaluating these opportunities, what I'm really looking for is, do they have the right people in place? Do they have the right talent in place? Is this a culture that can work with us, that can work with Aimtron, that can work with India and really grow our global footprint

items.statement: Aimtron 2.0 strategy built on three pillars: Innovation (AI, IoT, EV, defence, aerospace), Integration (global operations under one system), Impact (jobs, learning, sustainability)
items.quote: We are building Aimtron on three strong pillars, like 3Is: I for innovation, creating a new design and manufacturing solution in AI, IoT, EV, defence and aerospace, you name it, we have it, I for integration, bringing together India global operations under one system.

items.statement: NIM guidance above 3% for Q3 and Q4 FY26
items.quote: Our guidance still stands good that we will be above 3% in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Long-term NIM guidance above 3% through the cycle
items.quote: And we still are holding that our guidance, long term NIM above 3% through the cycle.

items.statement: AUCA recovery guidance of Rs 2,000 crores per quarter continues
items.quote: AUCA recovery, Chairman's guidance was 2000 crores per quarter, we have done 2400 crores and the guidance continues.

items.statement: Corporate credit growth visibility of at least 10% in next two quarters
items.quote: with the pipeline what we have the visibility of at least reaching 10% corporate credit growth in the next two quarters.

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline of Rs 7 lakh crores, half sanctioned awaiting disbursement
items.quote: So, the pipeline is 7 lakh crores, 7 trillion, which is a consistent number across quarters, half of it is already sanctioned and awaiting disbursement and half is in the discussions.

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved 7 bps QoQ to 3.09% driven by deposit repricing
items.quote: Our domestic NIMs for the quarter improved by 7 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 3.09%, driven by repricing of deposits.

items.statement: NIM uptick despite 100 bps asset side rate reduction due to liability management
items.quote: So, your NIM uptick is basically on account of tha t, despite that 100 basis point reduction in the interest rates and asset side

items.statement: CRR full cut benefit available by end of November for NIM pickup
items.quote: Obviously, the CRR full cut benefit will be available by the end of November. So, that will give some pickup on the net interest margin side.

items.statement: Fixed deposit repricing takes 12-14 months, 6-8 months completed
items.quote: Fixed deposit repricing generally takes about 12 to 14 months. That means, you know, we are, we have completed 6 to 8 months, another one or two quarters.

items.statement: Credit growth secular across segments, reversed negative trend with 7.1% growth in Q1
items.quote: we have reversed the trend and have posted a good 7.1% credit growth

items.statement: Private capex pipeline strong in power, renewable energy, commercial real estate, iron and steel
items.quote: from a capital expenditure point of view, power, renewable energy, commercial real estate and a bit of iron and steel.

items.statement: Cost of deposits and borrowings reduced; stayed away from wholesale deposit pricing
items.quote: we not only have focused on reducing the reliance on the wholesale deposits, where the market was going berserk in terms of pricing those deposits, we stayed away from there.

items.statement: Daily average balance improvement in CASA reduced cost of deposits
items.quote: Number two that we focused on the daily average balance improvement in the current account and savings bank account. And that has contributed to the reduction in the cost of deposits and cost of resources.

items.statement: Interest on borrowings down 26% YoY due to surplus liquidity and lower rates
items.quote: And interest on borrowing has also gone down by 26% this year. While we have borrowed less, the cost has also gone down.

items.statement: LCR at 143.8%, up from 139% in June
items.quote: How much is the LCR of the bank? LCR of the bank is 143.8%, up from 139% as on 30th June.

items.statement: GNPA Rs 76,000 crores, AUCA Rs 1,63,000 crores as of 30 Sept
items.quote: Gross NPA as on 30 th September is ₹76,000 crores and AUCA is ₹1,63,000 crores

items.statement: Written-off portfolio recovery rate placed at 6-8% based on security value
items.quote: We place it around 6% -8%. We started saying about 10% but as the security value is coming down, you know, based on the security value and accumulated written off accounts our recovery rates are likely to be around 8%.

items.statement: ECL impact limited; 4-year roadmap to April 2031, strengthening collections to reduce SMA 1/2
items.quote: we have to assess overall expected credit loss requirement on the 1st of April '27, we will have time up to 31st March '31 to take that, and we want to utilize that road map which is going to be given to us.

items.statement: 70% retail collections automatic via sweep; focusing on remaining 30% delays
items.quote: Today, in our retail side, 70% of the collections happen automatically. It is just sweeping from savings account to the loan account.

items.statement: Loan mix: EBLR 31%, MCLR 29%, fixed rate 22%, T-Bill linked 15% as of 30 Sept
items.quote: As on 30 th September EBLR is 31%, MCLR is 29%, fixed rate is 22% and T-Bill linked is 15

items.statement: CASA ratio 39.63%, CASA market share 23% vs deposit market share 22%+
items.quote: Our total deposits of 56 lakh crores, CASA deposits of more than Rs. 21 lakh crores with CASA ratio at 39.63% while CASA market share 23% versus overall deposit market share of more than 22%.

items.statement: Project SARAL first outcomes expected by April 2026 quarter
items.quote: the first drop from this Project State Bank of India November 04, 2025 SARAL is 1st of April’2026, I think April quarter we would talk more about what are those benefits we are getting out of this

items.statement: Raised Rs 25,000 crores equity via QIP, largest ever in India, oversubscribed 4.5x
items.quote: In this quarter, we also raised Rs 25,000 crores of equity capital by way of qualified institutional placement with a demand book of more than Rs. 1.1 trillion. This was the largest ever QIP offering in India.

items.statement: SBI AMC and SBI General Insurance are right candidates for listing; boards to decide timing
items.quote: SBI AMC and SBI General are right candidates for listing in our stable. It also provides some value unlocking and, more importantly, value recognition for the industry. We would soon be working on that.

items.statement: Draft M&A funding guidelines cap at 10% of capital; final guidelines awaited
items.quote: I think the draft guidelines put some cap on that, 10% of capital.

items.statement: Deposit rates stabilized; further repricing only on repo rate action
items.quote: I think the deposit rates have stabilized. Further deposit repricing or recalibration will only happen if there is any monetary, I mean, Repo rate action.

items.statement: 10-year G-Sec yield range-bound at 6.2-6.65% internal view
items.quote: I think it is now range bound. We feel like the range can be 6.2-6.65 kind of range for the 10-year G-Sec. It is just an internal house view.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margin through material cost, logistics, fixed cost, scheme optimization and counter-level extraction
items.quote: Our intent is to achieve double-digit margin by addressing all the five points which I have spoken now along with the enhancing counter-level extraction and expanding the market share on each individual product category.

items.statement: Material cost reduction initiatives expected to deliver Rs 200 cr annualized savings for appliances division
items.quote: ongoing material cost reduction initiatives are expected to deliver annualized savings of Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Rs 14 cr material cost savings realized in H1 FY26; Rs 60-70 cr expected in H2 FY26
items.quote: Out of that, Rs. 14 crores we have realized already in first half and balance amount of around Rs. 60 crores to Rs. 70 crores will be realized in second half of the year.

items.statement: Logistics cost optimization project targeting 10% reduction on Rs 154 cr base with Alvarez & Marsal
items.quote: On logistic cost of approximately Rs. 154 crores, a cost optimization project targeting a 10% reduction has been initiated.

items.statement: Fixed cost reduction project with Alvarez & Marsal; initial results expected from Q4 FY26
items.quote: On fixed cost reduction, we did not do well in this area. The team has been prepared, the team is focusing now to address this area, and initial results are expected to materialize from Q4 of the current fiscal.

items.statement: Reversed Rs 28 cr from dealers missing volume targets; annual scheme payout Rs 1,500 cr
items.quote: Up to 30th September 2025, we have reversed Rs. 28 crores from dealers who did not achieve their volume target as part of the tie-up letter. The annual scheme payout, including consumer finance and scheme of service stands at Rs. 1,500 crores up to 31 March 2025.

items.statement: Home Appliances division to grow at more than double-digit pace, faster than industry
items.quote: It has to be more than that. It has to be around double-digit. It will be more than double-digit.

items.statement: Washing machine demand momentum continuing; October good, November secondary sales on track
items.quote: What we feel is the momentum is still continuing. And October was good. And November also, if we see the secondary sales, it's on track. So, we expect the momentum to continue in both the categories.

items.statement: Refrigerator volumes 30% short of internal target despite no-frost addition and 5% realization increase
items.quote: However, in refrigerator overall if you see, we are still unhappy with the volumes. And as a percentage if you see, there has been sizable i ncrease, but compared to our internal target we are still about 30% short

items.statement: Front-load capacity 85,000/month at 92-93% utilization in Sep-Oct; planning 10-15% capacity increase
items.quote: As far as the front load is concerned, our capacity has been 85,000 per month. And in the month of September and October, we are almost used to 92% to 93%. And going forward, we are doing activities which we want to enhance the capacity by another 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Top-load capacity 60,000/month at 95% utilization in September; planning 10% capacity increase
items.quote: As far as top loader is concerned, our capacity is 60,000, and in September, we have almost achieved 95% utilization. Same way, we are looking forward to about 10% increase in our capacity.

items.statement: Engineering division expanding stamping capacity in Bangalore and planning greenfield plant in Gujarat near Maruti/Hero
items.quote: We are also looking at setting up a plant in close to Maruti, in Maruti and Hero in close to Manesar. So, two facilities to come up, one in Gujarat and one close to Manesar is what we are thinking of.

items.statement: Engineering division debottlenecking fine blanking with newer technology tools to free up capacity
items.quote: In Fine Blanking, there's marginal, there's some CapEx going in, but a lot of work is going into productivity improvement, including making tools with newer technology, which will free up existing capacity and all.

items.statement: Bid for railway engineering company (Rs 300 cr sales) but outbid; evaluated 60 targets, formal bids on 3-4
items.quote: We bid for a company recently; it was significantly into the railway segment. We bid for a company, but we were outbid by others. The company had sales of close to about Rs. 300-odd crores.

items.statement: Advanced Electronics division started machining for Titan; more updates expected in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Advanced Electronics venture has started. We supply to Titan. We are doing work for Titan. So, that has started. And it has started slowly. I think we will have a lot more to say about this in the January quarter.

items.statement: AC capacity 65,000/month; peaked at 55,000 (90% utilization); OEM development underway
items.quote: As far as the air conditioner capacity is concerned, we are about 65,000 per month. Capacity is available. And in the peak, we have touched about 55,000, about 90%.

items.statement: BLDC motor production started for washing machines (full supply to Goa plant) and ACs (20,000-30,000 in November); OEM development ongoing
items.quote: Washing machine supplies have started full-strength to IFB Industries Goa plant. We do not have any other customers though. We are only supplying internally now, and AC has also supplied now. I think we supplied in October certain dates, certain number, and November I think we will do about 20,000 or 30,000 numbers.

items.statement: Price increases implemented in top-loaders from Nov 1; front-loader increases under evaluation to offset commodity/forex
items.quote: In top-loader, we have increased the price from 1 of November. In front-loading washing machines also, we are looking at price increase, and judicially, we will do the price increase.

items.statement: Dishwasher GST benefit offset by 10% euro appreciation on imported inputs; no net margin benefit
items.quote: Since the inputs are denominated in euros, so the cost has gone up by 10%. So, to that extent, the price has gone up. So, after the GST increased, after passing on the benefit to the customer, there is no net benefit to IFB in terms of margins.

items.statement: 521 IP points contributing 12% of sales
items.quote: Currently, we have got 521 IP points across the country, and they contribute to around 12% of our sales.

items.statement: CSR headcount increased by 600-700 to 5,300; variable pay structure being rationalized by city by mid-November
items.quote: 700 we have increased and our current number of CSRs is 5,300 across the country.

items.statement: Customer satisfaction score above 90% and improved YoY; monitored weekly by service director
items.quote: The customer satisfaction survey is being done. The score is above 90% and it has improved over last year.

items.statement: Cashback/consumer finance attachment 40-50% for industry and IFB; competing on features not cashbacks
items.quote: In this current season, Diwali season, our cashbacks and schemes, they have been very competitive in line with the competition. And for the industry and also for IFP, the attachment for cashbacks, consumer finance is 40% to 50%.

items.statement: McKinsey 12-month engagement on e-commerce modernization and marketing cost optimization (target 15-20% on Rs 100-120 cr spend)
items.quote: It's about a 12-month thing basically on e-commerce. We realize that the processes, etc., we may need to update, or the better word is modernize that we have internally vis-à-vis the best practices followed by other leading firms.

items.statement: Ancillary cost Rs 140 cr in FY25 (78-80% engineering, 18-20% appliances); includes apprentice allowance regrouping impact of Rs 9 cr YTD
items.quote: If you talk about '24-'25, Rs. 140 crores, out of that, approximately 78% to 80% is pertaining to our engineering division. Engineering division, they are doing many ancillary jobs which are happening inside the factory, which are going outside the factory, that are being booked under ancillary cost.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 revenue Rs 1,327 cr (+11.5% YoY); PBDIT Rs 102.5 cr (7.7% margin, +30% YoY); PAT Rs 50 cr (3.8% margin)
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter was Rs. 1,327 crores against last year's Rs. 1,189 crores, which is a growth of 11.5%. PBDIT for the period was Rs. 102.5 crores and its percentage to revenue is 7.7% as compared to last year's Rs. 79.04 crores, which was 6.6% on revenue. PBDIT amount came across a growth of 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue Rs 2,637 cr (+8.4% YoY); PBDIT Rs 172.45 cr (6.5% margin); PAT Rs 75.11 cr (2.8% margin)
items.quote: Revenue for the period was Rs. 2,637 crores against last year's Rs. 2,434 crores which is a growth of 8.4%. PBDIT for the period was Rs. 172.45 crores, its percentage to revenue is 6.5% as compared to last year's Rs. 165.57 crores which is 6.8% on revenue.

items.statement: Engineering division growth below internal target due to customer schedule drops and marketing underperformance
items.quote: Our internal target was much, much more. But many customer schedules dropped. And I think marketing has not done what they are supposed to do, because our internal thing was much, much better, but it's not happened.

items.statement: Front-load growth below potential in states with weak management; changes being made
items.quote: There was room for further improvement. And in some of the states where the management is not good in that state, changes are being made.

items.statement: Poultry segment margins fell unexpectedly in Q2 FY26 due to lower realizations in day-old broiler chicks, CBF birds, and broiler hatching eggs.
items.quote: For the quarter ended September '25, the company's financial performance was affected mainly due to the unexpected fall in the profit margins to the poultry and poultry products segment.

items.statement: Demand was impacted by festivals (Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri, Pitrapaksh) and abnormal rains/flooding in the northern region.
items.quote: This is mainly also due to the festival during this period, which is like Ganesh Chaturthi, Navratri, Pitrapaksh and abnormal rains and flooding in the northern region where the company operation is there.

items.statement: Day-old broiler chick realization dropped to INR26.48 per chick in H1 FY26 from INR37.22 in H1 FY25, a decline of INR10.74.
items.quote: Day old broiler chick prices for this half year period in 9 months -- 6-month period is INR26.48 per chick, whereas the previous year, the same period of 6 months, it was INR37.22. That means there is a decline of INR10.74 per chick in broiler chick segment, day old chick segment.

items.statement: Soya meal price averaged INR36,154/ton in H1 FY26 vs INR43,316/ton in H1 FY25, down INR7,163/ton.
items.quote: In regard to the soya, the price of this 6 months is average of INR36,154 per ton, whereas last year, it was INR43,316 per ton soya prices. So there is a reduction of INR7,163 per ton soya prices -- soya meal prices.

items.statement: CBF bird production cost is INR85-86/kg for H1 FY26, similar to prior period.
items.quote: As far as our costing is concerned of CBF bird -- CBF bird it is almost INR85 -- INR86 per kg is the production cost of commercial broiler bird for this 6-month period, whereas the last time, it was again on the similar line, almost

And hopefully, we'll cover up the -- not only the losses, we will try to make the money also because we are having the pack production with us.

items.statement: Animal Health Products revenue was INR335 cr in FY25; targeting INR370-380 cr in FY26.
items.quote: Last year, we closed something at INR335 crores. This year, we are hoping to cross INR370 crores, INR380 crores in the year-end further.

items.statement: AHP revenue split: 45% external customers, 55% group companies.
items.quote: In the outside customer, it is to the extent of 45% is the business. And in the group companies, it is 55% business of that AHP segment.

items.statement: Layer segment capacity expansion planned for FY27-28; SPF expansion ongoing post-monsoon; AHP expansion completed at Kesavadi.

items.statement: Soya and maize trading 25% below MSP in October; soya prices stable for next 6 months.
items.quote: It is true. The soybean and maize, both the prices are -- even the Bajra, even the pulses, all in October, they have traded 25% below the MSP prices in the whole country.

items.statement: Maize cost benefit expected to reflect in Q3 FY26; soya prices likely stable for next 6 months.
items.quote: It should reflect in the second -- yes, third quarter.

items.statement: US-India tariff talks on soy create uncertainty; US corn imports for ethanol may not benefit due to DDGS export logistics.
items.quote: Another thing that we are -- that the USA, our tariff discussions are pending. So there's a quite uncertainty about the soya factor, what kind of a treaty, what kind of a tariff arrangements are going to take place with the USA.

items.statement: No structural change in competitive intensity; Q2 weakness attributed to seasonal factors.
items.quote: Yes. Yes, it is there. Yes.

items.statement: Oilseed segment EBIT margins near 3%, below prior 4.5-5.5% levels due to soybean trading below MSP and weak demand.
items.quote: There are 2 things are taking place. One thing, the soybean, which is a raw material for the company, that has grown by the minimum support price. And material is already trading below almost 20%, 25% below MSP. So the possibility of getting a good margins happens only when there is upward trend in the market.

items.statement: Poultry segment assets at INR814 cr as of Q2 FY26.
items.quote: So if you see our financial results on the segment asset side, the poultry and poultry products for the quarter ended, it is INR814 crores whereas -- which is the same for all the periods.

items.statement: GST reduction on QSR (18% to 12%) passed through to customers; no impact on company realization.
items.quote: If the price was INR100 and the GST was 18%, now it is INR12%. So ultimately, we are collecting less and paying the same thing to the government. So it's not having our -- impact on our realization and all.

items.statement: SSG expected to grow 30-50% over next 6-12 quarters; last year SSG grew ~22-23%
items.quote: Last year, we grew about 22%, 23%, if I aggregate all of the SSG pieces year-over-year. But this year, we can already see directionally we headed 40-plus. So, we will continue to work on it.

items.statement: PC refresh cycle and AI PC penetration seen in India; overseas PC market flattish
items.quote: We see signs of the PC refresh cycle. And we also see increased AI PC penetration, especially in the commercial space, and we see that in India, and estimate that the growth could be higher in the second half of the year if this trend continues.

items.statement: Mobility grew 18% driven by premium segment demand and NPIs; strong D2R execution in India
items.quote: Mobility grew by 18%, contributing to 35% of the top line, driven by stronger demand in the premium segment, impactful NPIs.

items.statement: Group PAT margin 1.33% for quarter; excluding Arena PAT margin 1.57%
items.quote: Overall, PAT for the group was standing at 1.33% for the quarter, and excluding Arena, PAT was at 1.57%.

items.statement: SSG delivers higher-than-average PAT vs group; gross margins higher on SSG business
items.quote: It also delivered higher-than-average PAT compared to the group, which contributed to our results being what it is.

items.statement: Several large TSG deals in pipeline for Q3 and Q4 in India and overseas
items.quote: We also have several deals in the pipeline on Technology Solutions, which we expect to fruition in Q3 and Q4, both in India and overseas.

items.statement: Investing in CloudQuarks digital platform, technical presales teams, Redington Academy, and marketplace ecosystems for SSG
items.quote: continue to invest on the digital platform, CloudQuarks. We have been talking about that. We already have the platform, and we are continuing to improve it to add more analytics, to add white labelling, to add automation, to add marketplaces, etc

items.statement: Working capital days lowered to 31 due to efficient management and higher mobility mix
items.quote: I want to talk a little bit about working capital and opex, very efficient management of working capital and a higher mix towards mobility led to the overall lowering of working capital days to 31.

items.statement: Arena debt currently ~$130M, down from ~$160M; Connect divestment to reduce debt by $50-55M
items.quote: Arena debt levels are currently at about 130-odd million, used to be about 160 plus.

items.statement: Arena interest cost high due to Turkish lira loans; winding down lira business to significantly reduce debt and interest
items.quote: See, the important point is the interest cost today is very high in Arena because of Turkish lira loans. If we exit or wind down significantly the Turkish lira business, then the debt that we need to raise in the local currency is much lower.

items.statement: Factoring cost Q2 FY26 INR 45 cr vs INR 33 cr YoY; total interest and factoring cost INR 161 cr vs INR 117 cr YoY (37% increase)
items.quote: Okay. So overall, the factoring cost for this quarter is about INR 45 crores. And for last year, same period, about INR 33 crores. That takes the total interest and factoring cost to INR 161 crores vis-a-vis INR117 crores last year, a 37% increase.

items.statement: SSG now 16% of revenue, grew 48% YoY; cloud, cybersecurity, application software, professional services all double-digit growth
items.quote: It grew by 48%, contributing to 16% of the top line. If you remember, we talked about it the previous Information Classification: RL\General Business\Redington quarter that this group for last year grew somewhere between 20% and 25%, so we clearly see signs of accelerated growth in this area

items.statement: SSG revenue mix roughly equal between security, cloud, software; software slightly higher; professional services <10%
items.quote: you can say that there is somewhat of an equal mix between security, cloud and software business with software being a little bit higher, but somewhat of an equal mix. And the professional services part of it is less than 10% right now

items.statement: D2R channel in India with 5,000+ outlets selling premium phones key growth driver for mobility
items.quote: The D2R channel, the direct to retail channel, that we have built with over 5,000 outlets are getting only premium phones, has been one of the key drivers for this.

items.statement: Two distributors (Ingram and Redington) for Apple in India; share roughly 50/50; upcountry growth expanding distribution TAM
items.quote: As you may be aware, there are only 2 players in India, Ingram and us in the Apple space. And there are times when we do a bit better, and there are times that they do a little bit better. So, the numbers are roughly 50 plus minus.

items.statement: Turkey concordat cases elevated at ~4,400 Jan-Sep vs normal 2,000-3,000/year; collections slow, 18-24 month timeline
items.quote: Roughly in the current year, between January to September, about 4,400 cases had got reported, which normally would be in the range of 2,000 to 3,000 entities in a year.

items.statement: AI PCs 22% of commercial PC sales in India this quarter; consistent monthly activation growth for 6-7 months
items.quote: Specifically on AI, we've seen about 22% of our commercial PCs in this quarter came from the AI classified PCs.

items.statement: Hardware commoditization risk in TSG and ESG; OEMs pushing for lower margins; SSG digital platform stickiness critical
items.quote: Now clearly, hardware part of the market is getting more commoditized. And as it gets more commoditized, the expectation from brands and OEMs is to really give lower and lower margins to you.

items.statement: ~125 professional services resources in India focused on migration, modernization, DevOps; scaling via productized models
items.quote: So, our own resources, we roughly have about 125 resources in the company, mostly in India in professional services. And these resources are focused on things like migration, modernization, spinoffs, DevOps, a range of services.

items.statement: Exploring small inorganic opportunities in SSG (cybersecurity, cloud, competencies); early stages
items.quote: We are exploring, I would say, very early stages right now.

items.quote: We will bring it to our Board as well and have a discussion. But your point is bang on because if -- we don't want to leave growth on the table at the cost of dividend

items.statement: Positive outlook for India, UAE, KSA for next 2-3 quarters across all business units including mobility, PC, TSG
items.quote: In terms of outlook, so far, India, UAE, KSA, all 3 geographies, we definitely see good outlooks. At least in the near term, the next 2, 3 quarters, there is good reason to believe in all business units as well

items.quote: That will be roughly around $500 million plus/minus, Sarvesh. And that business will continue. Right now, it's flat to decline because of the market situation. We expect it will be depending on the market size and our share, roughly $500 million next year as a number

items.statement: Order backlog stands at Rs. 9,895 crores with 30% large orders and 70% smaller monthly execution orders
items.quote: And our order backlog stands at Rs. 9,895 crores, gives us a good visibility of revenues in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Base orders grew 13% year-on-year while overall orders declined 3% due to absence of large orders
items.quote: We had 13% base order growth and 14% revenue growth. But if you compare last year, we around in this quarter, we had some large contracts, large orders. So, if you look into the overall order growth, that looks (-3%). But the base order growth was quite healthy.

items.statement: Revenue grew 14% year-on-year driven by backlog execution
items.quote: So, we saw a good revenue growth of 14%, and as I said, net of large orders, we had (-3%) orders growth, plus 13% in the base orders.

items.statement: PBT margin at 16.4% vs 14.9% sequentially and 20.5% year-on-year, impacted by material cost, mix, QCO and FOREX
items.quote: And profitability, we are at 16.4% on PBT compared to 14.9% sequentially, and 20.5% compared to the previous year . We will dwell upon this as we go forward. And that is more due to the material cost impact.

items.quote: Our focus on diverse business market segments spread in 23 market segments; we continue to see high engagement and high response in data center, electronics and renewable and our portfolio is resonating well in these and these are the long-term gains. items.quote: Our global CEO in the last call has made it very clear that ABB is looking for large ticket inorganic options around the world. And whenever such options are exercised, they also have a footprint effect in India and we participate with our books in those acquisitions as well.

items.statement: Robotics divestment to SoftBank; India assets to be evaluated by Board for separation into new company
items.quote: As far as India assets are concerned, these assets will be evaluated by the Board, Independent Directors included. And we will follow the due process of evaluating it. items.statement: Cash balance at Rs. 4,500 crores, down from ~Rs. 5,000 crores due to strategic inventory build
items.quote: And the cash balance, Rs. 4,500 crores. Of course, we could have done slightly better over here. We have stocked up strategically inventory to make sure that we are not bound by any QCO obligations which could come up as a surprise or a delay in certification.

items.quote: Probably I think the QCO should be addressed in another three to four quarters is what we see because that is the timeline what the government has also given. items.quote: We continue to expand our portfolio and bring more premium products to the market because market is demanding it. And we have introduced IE5 ultra-premium efficiency LV motors. And this is proven induction motor technology and free from rare earth materials.

items.quote: Our target for reducing the GHG emission was 87%. We have achieved it at 87.05 %. Zero waste to landfill units we had target that in 2025 four units will be zero waste to landfill. items.quote: For 2025 outlook, I think tailwinds are private consumption, government capital expenditure, and moderating inflation, but headwinds, as we know, trade uncertainty is playing out around India. And of course, there is a volatility in the global financial markets, and there is

items.statement: Customer connect programs across country width and depth, all segments and customer sizes driving growth impulse
items.quote: Our team does customer connect programs across the width and the depth of country in the market segments as well as geographies and the large and the medium and the small size customer base and that is something that keeps us growth initiatives and the growth impulse that we need inside the company and that has been the drumbeat for last many years and our team continue to have that drumbeat going

items.statement: Targets 25% revenue growth for FY26 with H2 stronger than H1
items.quote: We remain confident of achieving around 25% revenue CAGR growth for FY '26 with an even stronger performance expected in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Expects full-year EBITDA margins similar to H1 levels of 10-10.5%
items.quote: Yes. We expect this to be at a similar level for the full year also.

items.statement: Targets closing order book of INR9,000-10,000 crores by end of FY26
items.quote: We expect that this should be somewhere between INR9,000 crores to INR10,000 crores as a closing order book by the end of the year.

items.statement: Targets order inflow of INR6,000 crores plus for FY26
items.quote: For the full year, we have guided that, okay, we will be -- we are targeting an intake of INR6,000 crores plus.

items.statement: Aims to double capacity to 600,000 tonnes by FY28 end
items.quote: By FY '28, we do expect to double our capacity to 600,000 tonnes.

items.statement: Targets polymer business revenue of INR1,000 crores in next couple of years with double-digit EBITDA margin
items.quote: We do believe that we can make it INR1,000 crores brand in the next couple of years' time itself and certainly target a double-digit EBITDA margin at those revenue numbers.

items.statement: Long-term aspiration to reach 12% EBITDA margins
items.quote: Long term, we do aspire that our margins should move from the current 10%, 10.5% level to 12% level in the longer term.

items.statement: Targets 50-50 domestic-export order mix in 2-3 years
items.quote: Our internal aspiration is that long term, we should be having an order mix of 50 -50, 50% of exports and 50% of domestic. But I think it will take us at least 2, 3 years to get there.

items.statement: Order book reached record INR8,820 crores as of September 2025 with 89% domestic, 11% export
items.quote: On the business development front, our order book reached its highest ever level of INR8,820 crores as of September '25, comprising 89% domestic and 11% export exposure, providing a strong foundation for future growth.

items.statement: H1 FY26 order inflows of INR3,221 crores, up 33% YoY
items.quote: Cumulatively, H1 FY '26 order inflows stood at INR3,221 crores, a 33% year -on-year growth, supported by sustained traction in both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline robust at over INR30,000 crores including INR10,000 crores export
items.quote: Our bidding pipeline remains robust at over INR30,000 crores, reflecting strong visibility across T&D and infrastructure opportunities.

items.statement: Revenue split traditionally 40% H1, 60% H2 supporting 25% FY26 growth target
items.quote: Yes, absolutely, because traditionally, we have seen that the revenue split between H1 and H2 has always been in the range of 40 -60 as in 40% of the year's revenue coming in H1 and 60% coming in H2.

items.statement: Monsoon delays in Rajasthan deferred some revenue to H2 but projects back on track
items.quote: The monsoon has disrupted a lot of logistics and civil works at multiple of our project sites and led to temporary execution delays and just deferment of revenue recognition for certain projects and supply schedules for certain projects into the second hal f of the year

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 10.4%, H1 10.3% vs 9.9% last year on better project mix and operating leverage
items.quote: Our EBITDA reached an all-time high at INR131 crores, up 16% year-on-year, with margins expanding to 10.4%, reflecting improved project mix, operating leverage and efficiency in execution.

items.statement: Finance cost as % of sales improved to 4.1-4.2% from 4.7% last year
items.quote: We are very happy that we have been able to deliver that where finance cost as a percentage of sales this year is closer to about 4.1%, 4.2%.

items.statement: New 75,000 tonnes capacity fully operational; additional 75,000 tonnes expansion initiated targeting 600,000 tonnes by FY28
items.quote: Our new 75,000 tonnes capacity is now fully operational with commercial production commenced. We have also initiated plans for an additional 75,000 tonnes expansion, taking us closer to our target of 600,000 metric tons per year total capacity by FY '28 end.

items.statement: Operating at 85%+ capacity utilization
items.quote: We are operating at about 85% plus capacity utilization.

items.statement: Export revenue grew 27% YoY to INR523 crores in H1 FY26

items.statement: US market <2% of business; pursuing approvals in North America for future growth
items.quote: Yes. So the U.S. as of now doesn't make much of our overall business, less than 2% of our business comes from the U.S. market.

items.statement: Board approved 3 foreign marketing subsidiaries in US, UAE, Brazil for export expansion
items.quote: See, in the last Board meeting in quarter 1, we also took the Board approval for setting up 3 new foreign marketing subsidiaries, one in U.S., one in UAE and one in Brazil.

items.statement: Won two 765 kV transmission line projects from PGCIL strengthening high-voltage position
items.quote: Notably, we won 2 prestigious 765 kV transmission line projects from PGCIL in Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, further strengthening our position in the high-voltage segment.

items.statement: Executing ~5,000 circuit km of EHV & HVDC projects; HVDC projects in bid pipeline offer better margins
items.quote: The EPC division is currently executing around 5,000 circuit kilometers of EHV & HVDC transmission line projects as of September '25.

items.statement: Polymer business H1 revenue INR242 crores vs INR199 crores last year; targets INR600 crores full year

items.statement: Resin prices believed to have bottomed out; expects polymer margins to improve

items.quote: On the substation side, the company is executing 2 small and medium-sized projects right now. And we are targeting commissioning of these projects in the next financial year.

items.statement: Net debt plus acceptances reduced to INR1,268 crores from INR1,312 crores YoY; debt-equity stable at 0.61
items.quote: If you look at last year September quarter, we were at net debt plus acceptance of about INR1,312 crores versus this year, in September, we're at INR1,268 crores.

items.statement: ISTS waiver phase-out not expected to materially impact transmission demand due to CEA planning and private participation
items.quote: I don't think so because the transmission projects is as per CEA , Central Electric Authority planning, and that is done on the basis of all the expected renewable energy additions, the 500 gigawatt of renewable energy additions.

items.statement: Export market conversion cycles extremely long; not all INR30,000 crores pipeline will finalize in 6 months
items.quote: However, the -- it's not necessary that all INR30,000 crores will come up for finalization in the next 6 months. So especially in export markets, we have seen that the conversion cycle is extremely long.

items.quote: once biotech revenue start, biotech should see. 20:12 Healthy double digit margins then our welding division should also once our brand established and by FY28 of course we're aiming to establish a brand that should also be a comfortable double digit margin. 20:26 I wouldn't say 25%, but 10 to 15 is highly possible

items.quote: We are watching the market closely and are prepared to resume full capacity operations the moment conditions stabilize and become rational.

items.statement: FY26 top-line growth guided at 15% overall

items.statement: Raipur EBITDA loss for FY26 expected at INR10 crores

items.statement: Jamshedpur FY27 EBITDA loss expected at INR4-5 crores
items.quote: And in that FY, we expect around INR4 crores to INR5 crores losses for Jamshedpur.

items.statement: Raipur occupancy expected to reach 25% by end of FY26

items.statement: Raipur added renal transplants, chemotherapy, oncology surgeries; liver transplant license received
items.quote: We have started renal transplants, chemotherapy and oncology surgeries at this facility and received the license to start liver transplant, which we shall be commencing very soon.

items.quote: We've recently a dded the surgical robot for orthopedics also, which is the first of its kind in Eastern India

items.statement: 92% revenue from cash and insurance patients
items.quote: Approximately 92% of our business continues to come from cash and insurance patients, reflecting the strength of our neighborhood tertiary care model.

items.statement: Dum Dum facing increased competition but revenue dip due to intentional department mix realignment
items.quote: So with increased hospitals, definitely, there is a sense of, there is an increased competition in that area, but it is more from a perspective of us realigning our department mix in that hospital.

items.statement: Ranchi project stuck awaiting government clearances
items.quote: It is still, we are still awaiting clearances from the government. That is still stuck

items.statement: Actively evaluating Varanasi, Patna, Cuttack for organic and inorganic growth; greenfield preferred asset-light

items.statement: Doctor-led organization helps consultant retention via remuneration, facilities, clinical comfort
items.quote: Being a doctor -led organization, there is obviously a higher level of comfort consultants have than interacting with our mana gement team and promoters because we can understand the viewpoint of doctors

items.quote: Our average revenue per occupied bed stood at INR38,376, aligned with our focus on middle to high-income segment.

items.quote: Bed occupancy currently stands at around 44.7%, mainly due to the operations of the new hospital.

items.statement: Raipur rent INR35 lakhs per month (~INR4 crores annually) sits in depreciation and interest
items.quote: That's around INR4 crores. That's around INR35 lakhs per month.

items.quote: So we should be in that. I think the guidance was about 16% to 17%. So we should be between the 15% to 16% given the projections.

items.statement: Advanced discussions for new projects worth approximately INR2,700 crores
items.quote: Additionally, we are in advanced discussions for new projects worth approximately INR2,700 crores with encouraging conversion costs.

items.quote: EBITDA margin have been compressed in H1 nearly 3% compared to 11.6% in last H1.

items.statement: Targeting 18-20% EBITDA margin over longer term for CBG business
items.quote: As I said, for any business that we like to run, we generally like to target about 18%, 20% sort of EBITDA numbers over longer terms.

items.statement: IPO proceeds to fund capacity expansion up to INR1,300-1,400 crores revenue capacity
items.quote: with the new investments that we will be putting in from the proceeds that we raised in the IPO, getting up to INR1,300 crores, INR1,400 crores is not a problem

items.quote: We want it to kind of grow to 40%, 45% of revenues.

items.quote: I think, you know, the relationships that we've had with the large corpo rate, especially people like Tata Motors, Tata Steel, we are reaping those benefits today

items.statement: L1 in seawater desalination tender worth ~INR400 million for nuclear sector
items.quote: this is a seawater desalination tender that we have – we are L1 in that tender.

items.statement: Expect nuclear desalination order to materialize by end of November or early December
items.quote: we are currently expecting this to – order to materialize end of November, early December.

items.statement: CBG projects expected to contribute INR45+ crores revenue in next two quarters
items.quote: we have penciled in about a INR45 plus crores top-line in the next two quarters, so in terms of execution of two of the three tested projects.

items.statement: Carbon capture pilot stabilizing in Q4 FY26, revenue expected from H2 2027
items.quote: Consequently, we expect kind of revenue to come in H2 of kind of 2027 from thereon.

items.statement: Operating cost advantage up to 50% vs global players in ZLD
items.quote: we are able to provide, in certain cases, a very massive advantage to the client in terms of operating costs, where the technology that we provide can lead to up to a 50% operating cost advantage in many cases.

items.statement: Captive power requirement 12-18% lower than competing bids in recent desalination orders
items.quote: our captive power requirement has been at least 12% to 18% lower than what the other bids our customer has received.

items.quote: we have switched our order currency mainly to US dollars. So wherever we are taking new orders, the exposure for supply of equipment, which is done from our India and Sharjah entities, is all going to be dollar denominated.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected between 12-14% given UAE free zone status and India operations
items.quote: we expect the average tax rate to be between the 12% and 14% sort of a wage.

items.quote: And the balance, about $5.7 million, is what we expect to go next year, I mean, in terms of execut next year.

items.statement: Long-term growth target remains 20% annually
items.quote: the long-term guidance remains at 20%. We see the business growing very strongly over the years.

items.statement: Higher employee costs due to leadership and business expansion for CBG and carbon initiatives
items.quote: higher employee costs. This is mainly due to ongoing leadership and business expansion with the CBG and carbon initiators for the business

items.statement: India launching recycling mandates for large water consumers
items.quote: India is kind of launching certain recycling applications to large water consumers. So that will also kind of help the business in the upcoming years.

items.statement: India is global leader in ZLD technology and experience
items.quote: India is being one of the leaders in zero-liquid discharge and recycling. So, if you look at the global marketplace, on a global scale, India is the leader.

items.statement: Technology licensing deals in advanced stages, deployment expected in current quarter
items.quote: There are a couple of advanced stages that we are in. So in the current quarter, we expect to kind of deploy some of these funds.

items.statement: Management targets 20-25% year-on-year revenue growth and aims to outperform prior year EBITDA margins, but declines to give a specific EBITDA margin range to avoid overcommitment.
items.quote: As Aman just mentioned, from last H1 to this H1 and last year to this year, we always look for a sustained growth from 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 90,441.87 lakhs as of July 31, 2025, with a 7-9% incremental growth seen by September 2025.
items.quote: Our order book remains strong at INR90,441.87 lakhs as on July 31, 2025, providing a clear visibility for the sustained revenue momentum in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Management sees a hot pipeline with ~9% quarterly order conversion growth; order book grew 7-9% from July to September 2025.
items.quote: If I would say there is a 9% growth per quarter that we are looking at in terms of the order conversions. This year it was 90,441.87 lakh order book as of Jul y 2025 and we have seen a 9% growth as of September 2025

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 14.7%; management focuses on structural efficiencies and aims to sustain and grow margins yearly, not quarterly.
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR2,839.99 lakhs, with margins improving significantly to 14.7%.

items.statement: Management expects FY26 EBITDA margins to be better than last year, targeting sustenance and growth, but refuses to commit to a specific range.
items.quote: Better than last year, for sure. Our main focus has been to outperform each quarter and each year. But the main goal in management is sustenance and growth.

items.statement: Strong demand in MENA/GCC/ECO Zone regions driven by pharmaceutical self-reliance and healthcare infrastructure investment; Saudi Vision 2030/2040 supports long-term opportunity.
items.quote: During the period, we secured several high -value turnkey projects across the MENA, GCC, and ECO Zone regions, markets that continue to drive growth through increased investment in pharmaceutical, self -reliance and the healthcare infrastructure.

items.statement: Projects in emerging pharma markets typically have 18-24 month cycles; clients progress from generic facilities to more complex, regulated plants over time.
items.quote: Each project moves in a cycle of 18 to 24 months for us. And we have a strong pipeline from the region.

items.statement: In-house manufacturing covers ~30% of turnkey project supply (process, air, water systems); rest is integrated procurement and engineering.
items.quote: About 30% is in -house manufactured of the products that we supply to a turnkey plant. So, process, air and water. But these are the lifelines of the facility. And the rest is integrated in the entire project.

items.statement: Receivable days currently in market range of 120-150 days; management sees room for incremental improvement via better collection procedures and timely project completion.
items.quote: So the market average range is in this period, between 120 to 147, 150 days. So we have not a drastic, but yes, there is a room for improvement, which we are working on.

items.statement: Signed MOU with KP Group for sustainable energy solutions to broaden service offerings and enhance market positioning.
items.quote: Currently, we have signed a positive MOU for sustainable energies with KP Group and we are looking at entering new projects with our partnership in MOU terms with KP Group so that we can broaden our services, go after sus tainable offering in the projects that we currently do and increase our product profile also by offering these sustainable solutions to our existing and new clients

items.statement: Differentiation via in-house manufacturing of critical process/air/water systems, 30+ years experience across 62 countries, and single-window turnkey model ensuring speed and compliance vs Western competitors.
items.quote: Number one, the in-house manufacturing of process air and water, the criticalities is what makes us positioned better than competitors from the West, which is European mostly. Number two, experience that Fabtech already has in over 62 countries up to now in the design and build space.

items.statement: Projects target compliance with USFDA, EU GMP, Saudi FDA, African regulatory bodies, UK MHRA; regulatory adherence is a key client requirement in all emerging pharma markets.
items.quote: Be it USFDA, be it EU GMP, be it Saudi FDA, or PPB and the African regulatory bodies, be it UK, MHRA, each one of these regulatory approvals are very important, independently for the client to produce effective and compliant facilities and medicines.

items.statement: Operates across 22 countries with focus on pharmaceutical emerging markets (Middle East, Africa, GCC, Persian Gulf); revenue is international.
items.quote: FTL today operates across 22 countries, delivering start -to-end turnkey solutions across processes, air, water systems, three critical pillars of clean, compl iant and efficient pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturing setup.

items.statement: Project execution timeline of 18-24 months from concept to completion is a key sector KPI for turnkey pharma engineering.
items.quote: So, execution plan of all our projects has a total period of 18 to 24 months. Right from concept, design, complete supply chain and then execution. 18 to 24 months.

items.statement: Revenue and margins are lumpy quarter-to-quarter due to project-based model; management emphasizes yearly guidance over quarterly predictability.
items.quote: We are into a project company where our business and projects go as per the client readiness. So sometimes our business is lumpy in some quarters and we do not measure our EBITDA quarter on quarter. Generally, we focus only on the yearly model.

items.statement: Core offering is end-to-end turnkey design and build for pharma/healthcare/biotech covering process, air (HVAC/cleanroom), and water (purification/WFI) systems; not pursuing data center or semiconductor segments.
items.quote: If a client wants to make medicines, medical products, devices in the pharma, healthcare, biotech industry, then we design those plants and we build those plants. End to end turnkey project management, design and build. We have in-house process, air and water, the critical lifelines of the facility.

items.statement: Clarified that Fabtech Technologies Limited (mainboard) is separate from Fabtech Technologies Cleanrooms Limited (SME), which paid a dividend; FTL did not commit to dividend.
items.quote: in the Fabtech universe, we have these two dedicated segments. One is Fabtech Technologies Limited, who you are currently talking to. That is the international pharma, healthcare, biotech, design and build company, focused in the pharma emerging m arket international, right. And the second company is Fabtech Technologies Clean rooms Limited. That is the integrated clean room player focused in Indi

items.statement: Monthly run rate guidance of Rs.35-40 crores by March FY26 reiterated with confidence from IndiaAI orders
items.quote: Now, we had made a guidance for FY26 March for the monthly run rate where we mentioned a number of anywhere say between 35 and 40 CR per month.

items.statement: Received two large orders from IndiaAI Mission worth Rs.88 crores and Rs.177 crores for domestic LLM model building
items.quote: So, your company received two reasonably large orders from IndiaAI Mission for Rs.88 crores and Rs.177 crores.

items.statement: Planning to acquire 2,048 Blackwell GPUs (mainly B200) immediately, potentially doubling to 4,096 before March FY26
items.quote: So, as we are immediately planning to acquire about 2,048 Blackwell, so as soon as they are deployed or while we are in the process of deploying them if we see that like there is potentially more capacity that can be utilized based on the input that we keep getting from overall the market and the ecosystem, we might decide to kind of like double up that number all the way to 4,096 before March.

items.statement: Chennai facility went live on August 1st; total data center capacity ~10 MW supporting 8,000-10,000 cloud GPUs with ability to expand at Chennai
items.quote: We have some of the older capacity that we classify close to 1 megawatt or so. Then the newer capacity that we built in the recent past like last two years or so including the Chennai one, the capacity available to us is about 9 megawatts plus 1 megawatt older capacity. So, that is an overall of about 10 megawatts or so of capacity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 41% in Q2 FY26 from 29% in Q1 FY26; medium-term target remains 70%+/-
items.quote: EBITDA margin has significantly improved to 41% from 29% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin on newly deployed assets expected to range 80-85%
items.quote: So, from a GP margin perspective, what we foresee across our GP margin should be ranging from 80% to 85% across on that newly deployed assets.

items.statement: Robust global demand for cloud GPUs at H100 and Blackwell price points; IndiaAI Mission orders indicate strong domestic demand
items.quote: Now, we are also continuing to see a very robust global demand for cloud GPUs. The demand continues at a price point at which Hoppers are available globally, and at a reasonably higher price point for Blackwell GPUs, we are also seeing a lot of demand globally.

items.statement: Debt facility of Rs.450 crores to be fully utilized by end of March or early April FY26
items.quote: So, debt what we have taken the facility is Rs.450 CR, which would be utilized as per the terms of agreement with the vendor during the payment cycle. So, by end of March or earlier April, that completely should be utilized.

items.statement: Other current assets increased due to advances given for procurement of new GPUs; GST input already factored in March financials
items.quote: During the current quarter, it has gone up primarily because of advances given for the procurement of new GPUs.

items.statement: Focus on NVIDIA GPUs (H100, H200, Blackwell) where customer demand exists; no immediate plans for AMD GPUs
items.quote: Currently, we are very focused on where the customer demand is coming from. So, primarily, we feel that the customer demand today is for NVIDIA GPUs, especially at least in India.

items.statement: Purchase of services and consumables run rate ~Rs.14 crores; not expected to change drastically unless adding more GPU clusters
items.quote: See, some difference would be there before the Blackwell capacity gets added, when your utilization goes high, the cost obviously goes higher, and we continue to build capacity for non-flagship GPUs or GPUs for storage and many other things. So, that being said that like broadly that is in range that like it will not change drastically unless we add a few more clusters of a couple of thousand GPUs

items.statement: Depreciation run rate ~Rs.42 crores; expected to increase to ~Rs.50 crores with Chennai cluster active from August 1st
items.quote: So, I think the number will be broadly similar, but only one point that Chennai cluster became active on 1st August. So, one month depreciation would be an additional number.

items.statement: GPU useful life assumed at 6 years for depreciation (Companies Act); economic life seen as 7-8 years with demand across Ampere, Hopper, Blackwell generations
items.quote: For the depreciation purpose, I believe it is like as per the company's act which is six years for all the GPUs, and mostly useful life we see that like for GPUs or CPUs is at least like happily and easily about seven, eight years.

items.statement: Committed to sovereign technology stack built on open-source with minimal reliance on international software; three levels of sovereignty: Indian-owned infrastructure, India-located data centers, homegrown/open-source software
items.quote: So, essentially, sovereignty, we have defined it for our customers. One is that we are an Indian cloud GPU provider, where the infrastructure is owned by us. The data centers are physically located in India. And the software being operated on our cloud is primarily built by us or is Open-Source with an ability to redistribute that Open-Source however we see fit.

items.statement: Acquisition of Jarvis Labs assets completed to access global self-service demand cohort and tech talent
items.quote: I would also like to once again share the news about the ongoing acquisition of Jarvis Labs assets. items.statement: Authorized capital increased by ~Rs.1,000 crores; no imminent fund raise timeline or details disclosed
items.quote: So, we will obviously keep everyone informed about our plan. So, we will make it when appropriate.

items.statement: Obsolescence risk managed through prudential capacity planning across multiple GPU generations; regulatory compliance with Indian and origin-country laws for equipment procurement
items.quote: We have been in the compute business for almost past 16 years. We have seen multiple cycles of these. So, essentially, there are so many moving parts to kind of like take care to kind of like not have to worry about obsolescence as long as we have done things like in a prudential manner.

items.statement: Exit MRR Rs.16 crores in Q2 FY26 vs Rs.14.5 crores in Q1 FY26; held capacity for IndiaAI Mission workloads causing temporary dip
items.quote: See, broadly as soon as we receive the long-term order from IndiaAI Mission, we had to kind of free up the capacity from longer-term users or refuse from longer-term users and kind of like work with only capacity which could be deployed as per plan.

items.statement: Differentiation through full-stack cloud platform, customer support, solutions, and team; not a data center player but cloud services provider
items.quote: We are a cloud player, not a data center player. Essentially, we have this whole stack of services. So, we have been supporting GPUs all the way since 2019-20 kind of timeframe, and we have been working on our software platform for the last so many years, and then we have the ability to provide the solutions of the kind that customers need.

items.statement: Compliance with Indian laws and equipment origin-country laws; no services to unauthorized users; Trump administration Blackwell export restrictions question deferred as above pay grade
items.quote: I think that question is a bit above my pay grade. So, basically like we do our level best to kind of like follow like all our laws of India and laws of the country of origin of where we are buying our equipment. So, we ensure fully that like none of our services are utilized by anyone who is not allowed to utilize those services.

items.statement: L&T partnership opens doors and conversations; exploring inside and outside use cases for collaboration

items.statement: Jarvis Labs team integrated into E2E Networks; continued focus on acquiring tech talent in India
items.quote: And even more importantly for the people who were a part of Jarvis Labs, now they are a part of E2E Networks. And essentially, we believe in their ability to contribute overall to building up like a very fine DNA for E2E Networks.

items.statement: No current talks with TCS for their planned 1 GW data center; will evaluate when capacity available for sale
items.quote: I think this is a question which is a bit premature. I think we would like to see a data center where we are buying capacity. So, once they build those data centers and they have the capacity available for sale, we would be happy to consider them along with all the other players.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs. 2,000-2,200 crores for FY26 maintained
items.quote: Guidance was somewhere near Rs. 2,000 crores, Rs. 2,000 crores to Rs. 2,200 crores, and which was based on the commissioning of our Line-3 and Line-4.

items.statement: Working capital expected to reduce to 80-85 days by end of FY26
items.quote: we expect working capital to reduce to approximately 80 days to 85 days by the end of FY '26.

items.statement: Rs. 1,300 crores WIP orders to deliver by March 31 plus Rs. 153 crores finished goods inventory

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin improved to 14.7% from 9.6% YoY due to scale and own-brand mix
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 14.7 % compared t o 9.6 % in H1 FY ‘25, supported by economics of scale and operational efficiency

items.quote: we will stick to our 6 % to 7% of our PAT . But then, with thi s efficiency, we will improvise it
