But as we are the early entrant and we had focused not on Central Province Whiskey in Maharashtra, we had focused on Hillfort, which is the premium product for which t

items.statement: IMFL Proprietary revenue INR41 cr (+35% YoY); IMIL INR56 cr (+8%); Merchant ENA INR37 cr; Ethanol INR71 cr
items.quote: In terms of segment performance for the quarter, IMFL Proprietary revenue stood at INR41 crores, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 35%. IMIL revenue stood at INR56 crores, growing by 8%. Merchant ENA contributed INR37 crores and ethanol revenue for the quarter was around INR71 crores.

items.statement: New state entry takes 6-12 months to stabilize; high upfront scheme costs in Maharashtra; UP collections risky
items.quote: So see, whichever states you enter new state, at least minimum it takes 1 year to stabilize and to work in the business in that state. So just for an example, if I give you the state of Maharashtra. So Maharashtra, the shops are owned by private. There is a private association to enter or to Associated Alcohols & place your product initially in one store, you have to give 4 cases free for every 10

items.statement: Capex of INR150 crores planned, INR80-90 crores by end of FY26, remainder in H1 FY27
items.quote: In terms of road map, I think by end of this year, we should be adding close to 8,000 to 9,000 tons, and the remaining will get added in FY '27 before H1.

items.statement: Bangalore facility capacity addition started, expect 80% consolidated utilization by end of FY27
items.quote: We expect the order flows to start from Q4 onwards. In terms of reaching 80%, I think progressively by end of FY '27, we should be at 80% utilization of the consolidated capacity.

items.statement: Three-year visibility for lamination sales of 93,000-94,000 tons vs current 70,000 tons target; machine components visibility of 15,000 tons vs current 10,000-11,000 tons
items.quote: So in terms of lamination, if I talk three years out, including new customers that we are targeting down south, we have a visibility to get to about 93,000, 94,000 tons of lamination sales, up from our current year's target of about 70,000 tons.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 16.3% in Q2; subsidiary Pitti Industries margin temporarily lower due to new capacity ramp-up, expected to recover from January quarter
items.quote: Margins remained stable at 16.3%, reflecting a strong degree of operating leverage in the business.

items.statement: Sustained order inflows and steady demand in traction motor, railway, data center, renewable energy; data center revenue doubled YoY to 4% of total, further 50-60% volume growth expected
items.quote: Surge in global data center requirements have significantly boosted the need for power generation solutions, presenting a major growth opportunity for our business.

items.statement: High value-added assemblies grew 16.5% to 3,168 tons; stator frame and shaft integrated assemblies grew 33.4% to 1,146 tons; loose lamination down 2%
items.value: 3,168 tons high value-added; 1,146 tons integrated assemblies
items.quote: High value-added assemblies grew by 16.5% to 3,168 tons. Stator frame and shaft integrated assemblies grew by 33.4% to 1,146 tons.

items.statement: Railway traction motor revenue 32% of total in Q2, of which 8% from Indian railways/metro; added Xylem and SKF for casting business; two new European clients in approval process
items.quote: So for Q2 FY '26, our revenue from traction motor and railway components was about 32%, of which the demand from Indian railways, including Vande Bharat trains, freight locomotives would have constituted about 25% of the total railway business.

items.statement: Exports 28% of operating revenue in H1 FY26; North America ~30-35%, Mexico ~INR80 crores, Europe remainder; US revenue ~$16M, Mexico ~$35M annually
items.quote: So about INR477.72 crores was operating revenue, of which total exports say about INR135 crores, that's 28%. And the North American part of the business would be about INR40 crores.

items.statement: Electrical steel shortage due to QCO/BIS restrictions on Chinese imports; importing 25% requirements from Korea/Japan; deficit of 200,000 tons in India; JSW capacity expected FY27
items.quote: As a strategy, we have decided to start about 25% of our total requirements for imports till the situation in the Indian manufacturing of this steel stabilizes.

items.statement: Inventory increased INR80 crores March to September due to elongated import lead times for electrical steel; net debt elevated until sourcing stabilizes
items.quote: No, this is purely to protect ourselves from lack of availability of materials. As I mentioned in one answer prior, there's a huge disruption in the availability of various grades of steel in India.

items.statement: Net debt elevated due to inventory buildup; INR140 crores cash held for LC margins, long-term borrowings, and remaining INR70 crores capex
items.quote: Yes, it will remain at this level until this sourcing issue does not get stabilized. We had expected that this would get stabilized by April, but it continues to persist.

items.statement: Section 232 tariff imposes 50% on steel/iron/aluminum/copper content regardless of trade deals; acts as equalizer; India-US trade deal anticipated
items.quote: But if you see the fine print on the taxes and tariffs, there's a Section 232 tariff, which is applicable for all iron, steel, aluminum and copper parts. So irrespective of the trade deal with the United States, a 50% tariff is imposed on products containing these items.

items.statement: Wabtec modification business strong, new locomotive business expected to pick up from next year; Mexico benefiting from US tariffs as manufacturing shifts there
items.quote: The modification in –business continues to remain very strong in the current calendar year, and the new locomotive business is expected to pick up from next year.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions in North India for appliance/automotive segments; multiple competitors engaged; copper winding acquisition hesitant due to low ROCE
items.quote: There are multiple competitors in the industry, and we are engaging with all of them to see what would be available. If something is available at an appropriate time, we shall move on it.

items.statement: Lamination volume 17,722 tons in Q2; loose lamination 11,801 tons; high value-added assemblies 3,168 tons; integrated assemblies 1,146 tons; machine casting 2,434 tons
items.quote: Volumes for lamination were up from 16,792 tons to 17,722 tons, of which loose lamination and low value-added assemblies were 11,801 tons, down by 2% on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Raw material pass-through with customers every 3-5 years; overhead renegotiation based on transparent costing model; machine components growth to offset margin pressure from low value-added laminations
items.quote: The good part is every, three to five years, depending on the customer and the contract, we renegotiate the overhead that we add based on our transparent costing model.

items.statement: Data center demand growth of 50-60% flagged as potentially challenging to sustain; tariff situation fluid; electrical steel supply disruption may persist until FY27
items.quote: From here on in, we are given to understand further 50% to 60% growth in volumes. However, I remain cautious on this particular statement as the demand is huge. And to sustain this level of increased demand, I see some challenges in the future.

items.statement: Revised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 20%-25% from earlier 15%-20%
items.quote: Post-GST cut we are revising our revenue growth guidance for full year to 20%-25% from earlier guidance of 15%-20%.

items.statement: Revised FY26 capex guidance to Rs. 220-260 crores from earlier Rs. 180-220 crores
items.quote: Also, our CAPEX guidance for full year FY '26 which was earlier Rs. 180 crores-Rs. 220 crore is now revised to Rs. 220 crores-Rs. 260 crores with new upcoming facility at Bangalore.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margin for full year FY26
items.quote: And this year, our guidance is already close to double-digit margin. So, we are maintaining that in coming quarters and for the full year.

items.statement: Expecting 12%-13% EBITDA margin over next 2-3 years
items.quote: Going forward, I think, as I've always said that over the next 2 to 3 years, we should be inching closer to more, maybe a 12% to 13% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Expect similar 20%-25% revenue growth in FY27
items.quote: For FY'27, we do expect a similar growth as FY'26. But given a 3- to 5-year's horizon, I think we continue to maintain that we will probably grow much, much ahead of the industry, maybe close to a 15% to 20% CAGR over the next few years. But for next year, I think the guidance would be similar to FY'26 which is about 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Board approved new Bengaluru facility with Rs. 140 crore investment for Maruti Suzuki and Toyota orders
items.quote: Also, the board has approved the setting up of a new manufacturing facility in Bengaluru, Karnataka with a capital investment of approximately Rs. 140 crores. The plant will cater to newly secured orders from Maruti Suzuki and from Toyota.

items.statement: Chakan Phase 2 on track to commence operations in H2 FY26 for Skoda and Volkswagen
items.quote: The Chakan Phase 2 is on track and to commence operations from H2 of FY'26 which will primarily cater to Skoda and Volkswagen.

items.statement: No new long-term debt planned; capex to be funded through internal accruals
items.quote: As of now, we don't foresee that we'll need to have some extra debt. We'll do it through internal accruals.

items.statement: Bengaluru plant targeted for commissioning by Q4 FY27 with peak annualized turnover of Rs. 450 crores
items.quote: Once fully ramped up, the plant is expected to achieve a peak annualized turnover of around Rs. 450 crores. The facility is targeted to be commissioned by the Q4 of FY'26-'27.

items.statement: Order book healthy at over Rs. 1,800 crores with 85% LED-based
items.quote: Our order book remains healthy at over Rs. 1,800 crores providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters and reinforcing a confident outlook. I am happy to share that about 85% of our current order book is LED-based indicating strong alignment with future market demand.

items.statement: Order book conversion: 15-20% in FY26, ~1/3 in FY27, ~1/3-40% in FY28, residual 5-7% in FY29
items.quote: So, out of the total order book, which we are sitting at Rs. 1,850 odd crores, this year we only expect close to about a 15% to 20% of it coming into the P&L. As I mentioned earlier, almost one-third of it will come in FY '27, almost close to one-third to 40% in FY '28, and then a negligible residual 5% to 7% in FY'29.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 9%, impacted by forex; ex-forex would be 70-80 bps higher than Q1
items.quote: Our EBITDA margins stood at 9%. I would like to highlight that margins during the quarter were impacted by exceptional foreign exchange fluctuations. Excluding this one off Forex impact, EBITDA margins would have been around 70-80 bps higher than Q1 FY'26.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 9.1%, up 32.6% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA came in at Rs. 175 crores up 32.6% with margin at 9.1% again marginally impacted by the Forex movement in Q2.

items.statement: Raw material consumption expected to stay at 64%-65%; manpower cost to decline from ~12.5% to 11%-11.5%; other fixed costs to decline from 14%-15% to 12%-13% over next few years
items.quote: I think on raw material consumption, I would expect the raw material consumption to be in a similar state of about 64% odd to 65% odd. The manpower cost definitely should lower with the growth. Currently, I think we are sitting at close to around 12.5%. I definitely see this going down to perhaps more like closer to 11% or 11.5%. And also the other fixed costs will get offsetted. And currently, th

items.statement: LED share increased to 61% of revenue in Q2; front lighting 69%, rear lighting 22%
items.quote: During the quarter, we saw a strong growth of 24% in our revenues led by the increasing share of LED lighting to 61% which has led to higher content per vehicle and better performance of the models we are presenting.

items.statement: PV segment 64% of revenue, 2W 30%, others 6%; order book similarly two-thirds PV
items.quote: The passenger vehicle segment continued to dominate given the higher complexity and higher content per vehicles in PV lighting. PV contributed 64% of our revenue while 2 wheelers contributed 30% and the remaining 6% came from other segments. This trend is reflected similarly in the order book where nearly two -third is PV lighting with a balanced large ly in 2 wheeler lighting

items.statement: Top 5 customers contribute 79% of revenue: Maruti, Mahindra, Tata, Honda Motorcycle, Hero MotoCorp
items.quote: I think if I look at our top five customers today we have pretty much the key brands like Maruti, Mahindra and Tata Motors from the passenger car side and we also have Honda Motorcycle and Hero MotoCorp from the two-wheeler side.

items.statement: First headlamp business win for Toyota Kirloskar Motor; taken from competition
items.quote: Coming back to your question, this is the first time we have actually won a headlamp business for Toyota Kirloskar Motor. And that's the reason we will have to expand our headlamp capacities. And yes, we would have gotten this business from the competition.

items.statement: Forex impact from rupee depreciation (Rs 86-86.5 to Rs 89); import 25-30% components in USD
items.quote: So, I think it is known to us that the current global scenario wherein the rupee has depreciated from the range of Rs86-86.5 to Rs.89 or so. And that's the key reason that and since we import over almost 25% to 30% components in USD, so that is a broader reason that it has given an impact to us in this quarter.

items.statement: No significant rupee devaluation expected in next 3 months; forex impact should stabilize
items.quote: As of now, whatever certain analysts predict, I do not expect a significant devaluation of the rupee, at least in the next three months. So, I would still probably perceive tha t we should be able to maintain it at a certain level and not have any significant further hits to the P&L on account of currency

items.statement: Content per vehicle increasing; ADB technology and animation/customization driving higher value; some models already at 2x content value
items.quote: I think going forward there is a lot of animation, there is also a lot of customization which we foresee happening. A lot of new technologies like the ADB which was recently introduced on one of the models will become a lot more deeper penetration across different models. With that I do feel that the content per vehicle will also increase and again there are some models out there where we already

items.statement: EV constitutes only ~9% of order book (PV + 2W); expect EV penetration to plateau at 8-10% in 2-3 years
items.quote: EV constitutes only about 9% of our entire order book, which includes passenger vehicles as well as two-wheeler models. My sense is very simple. Yes, there are big names coming in and I think the EV industry in passenger car, there are a lot of forthcoming models, there are a lot of plans. However, given the current state also, it's a mere single digit penetration on EV clo se to about 4% -5%. Eve

items.statement: Inventory turnover ratio improving; working capital efficiency to support ROCE expansion to 15-18% in 2-3 years
items.quote: The second thing is, in terms of the working capital also, with the efficiency improvement, we see that our ITR is improving and that will also give us some leverage in working capital.

items.statement: SL Lumax JV (dedicated to Hyundai) subdued last 2 quarters due to Hyundai volume decline; new plant overheads also impacting
items.quote: we see that there's a comparatively lower bottomline and it is because their topline is also not picking up since they are primarily supplying to Hyundai and Hyundai was relatively lower in terms of the market growth there. So for coming next H2 also, it all depends how the Hyundai will pick up in the market. So in case they will pick up good then the SL will also start looking at a better growth

items.statement: HVAC production started Q3 FY24; currently supplying one OEM with peak revenue Rs. 35-40 crores annually; no significant new order wins
items.quote: Yes, I think HVAC, we already started production of it in Quarter 3 of FY'24. Currently, we are supplying to one OEM with a peak revenue of approximately Rs. 35 crores to Rs. 40 crores annually. And we are currently engaged with other customers as well to see how we could scale up this business. But as of now, we don't have any significant order wins for the HVAC.

items.statement: LED modules still imported; PCB assemblies and electronic components localized at 25-30%; target 50-60% localization
items.quote: So I think as of now the LEDs are still imported, the LED as in the LED module which is the source of light. We have been able to localize some of the PCB assemblies, PCB boards and certain other electronic components as well. I think going forward the current localization is about 25% to 30% and going forward it will probably get enhanced to maybe a 50% to 60%.

items.statement: Small car revival signs but sustainability uncertain; product mix impact unclear
items.quote: So, the small car is definitely seeing some signs of revival. However, it's too premature to say whether this is sustainable. Also, even if the production gets increased, how much of the product mix will really change is something which we'll have to wait and watch.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY26 guidance of 12-15% revenue growth and 15-20% profit growth
items.quote: Yes. We are sticking to our earlier guidance, I think. So more or less, things will be around that figure only.

items.statement: Export automotive market growing with additional business expected this year and next 2 years
items.quote: So the export automotive market is growing because of additional business. And we expect that the business will grow this year also and in the coming 2 years also.

items.statement: Export share increased from 38-40% in Q1 to 42% in Q2, expected to keep increasing
items.quote: As you've seen in last quarter, June quarter, it was 38% to 40%. Now it is 42%. So it will be keeping increased.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin increased 2% YoY and 4-5% QoQ; consolidated gross margin increased 2% YoY but impacted by inventory provisions
items.quote: Gross margin is also increasing. If you see in this quarter, our gross margin has increased 2%. And if we compare then in last quarter to this quarter, our gross margin has increased around 4%, 5%.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin increased 2% YoY but provisions for old inventory reduced full reflection
items.quote: Consolidated basis also increased 2% on Y-o-Y basis. 2% because we are keeping some provisions for old inventories also. Therefore, it is not getting full reflection.

items.statement: No tariff impact so far as supply routed through Mexico warehouse near US border
items.quote: So far, we have not impacted with tariff because we are supplying through Mexico, our warehouse. And the customers who are taking material from us all are located in Mexico-U.S. border.

items.statement: South India capacity expansion on drawing board, no definitive timeline; Mexico plant on hold due to strategic uncertainty
items.quote: We have not taken a definitive plan, but we can say very soon. I cannot give you a number that we will start from tomorrow. We are discussing about it. We will take a decision soon.

items.statement: New South India plant planned as single line adding 4-5 lakh meters/month or 5-6 million meters/year
items.quote: And we have plan on drawing for the South India. But wherever we will be putting the plant, it will be one line basis and capacity will be adding around INR4 lakhs to INR5 lakhs per month or INR5 million to INR6 million a year.

items.statement: PU volume 314,000 meters, value INR7.8 crores in Q2, up 21% volume and 32% value QoQ; PU utilization 23-25%
items.quote: Our volume from PU plant is, for the quarter, 314,000 and value is INR7.8 crores, which has increased by 21% in quantity and 32% in value over the last quarter.

items.statement: PU division loss INR5.8 crores last quarter due to depreciation, no cash loss
items.quote: Last quarter, it was INR5.8 crores loss -- actual, there is no cash loss, but the loss is because of depreciation.

items.statement: Export breakup: General INR29 crores, OEM INR71 crores; Domestic: Auto OEM INR49 crores, Replacement INR36 crores, Footwear INR43 crores, Furnishing INR8 crores, Others INR138 crores
items.quote: Export general, INR29 crores, export OEM, INR71 crores. Total exports is INR100 crores. Auto OEM domestic, INR49 crores, replacement, INR36 crores, footwear, INR43 crores; furnishing, INR8 crores and remaining is others, which comes to INR138 crores and total is INR238 crores.

items.statement: Major export customers: Stellantis Group and Ford in US market; Benz and BMW in South Africa; some business with Daimler
items.quote: Our major export is to the U.S. market with Stellantis Group and Ford, and the business is increasing with -- mostly with Stellantis and Ford and some portion with Daimler also.

items.statement: Talks ongoing with H&M and Adidas for sports shoes; samples submitted but no agreement yet
items.quote: Regarding the two brands for India like for sports shoes that you mentioned and H&M, still talks are going on. Samples are submitted, but no agreement has come to effect till now.

items.statement: Net cash balance ~INR450 crores; surplus cash kept for capex and new projects
items.quote: That will be -- we are keeping for the capex, new capex or any new projects.

items.statement: Anti-dumping duty on Chinese PU imports creates 20-40% price difference, aiding domestic PU competitiveness
items.quote: As you know, most of the PU material is coming from China and there is huge under advising. They have put anti-dumping duty. Now, what happens in anti-dumping is that you cannot under advise. But you can reduce or increase the quantity.

items.statement: Full year export revenue expected INR350-400 crores (up from ~INR250-300 crores last year)
items.quote: It will be around INR350 crores to INR400 crores. Up to July INR100 crores. April to September...

items.statement: Total sales volume 8 million meters in Q2
items.quote: Yes. 8 million meters for the quarter.

items.statement: Mexico plant decision deferred until March 2026 due to US policy uncertainty
items.quote: We will see, until next March. On that basis, we will take a final call whether we actually want to go over there or we want to keep that decision pending only.

items.statement: Chairman Suresh Poddar present and well; succession planning question deferred
items.quote: The day it happens, we will announce it. We are also as worried as you are.

items.statement: CSR: 45,000 plants planted; adopted schools for education, healthcare, sanitation, family welfare initiatives
items.quote: Under the Corporate Social Responsibility programs, we have contributed towards the regular plantations and 45,000 plants we have already planted and completed and have a plan to do it at a larger scale in coming years.

items.statement: Management targets INR 1,500 crore revenue for FY26
items.quote: I expect at least I'll reach INR 1,500 crores.

items.statement: Management confident of achieving INR 1,500 crore revenue in FY26 with INR 900 crore in H2
items.quote: Yeah, that is what I'm saying. We must -- I'm confident we will achieve INR 1,500 crores, the past year.

items.statement: Export sales fell INR 150 crore in H1 FY26 due to customers delaying purchases amid falling rice prices
items.quote: Yes, this quarter or this six month the export sales have come down by INR150 crore approx., but the profitability ratio is almost okay, perfect.

items.statement: Customers delaying purchases waiting for price bottom; buying now picking up quickly
items.quote: People are waiting for the -- I mean, waiting for the bottom down, and which I feel it is now. And in this particular season, the sales are very quickly picking up now.

items.statement: Good Basmati crop across India with minimal flood impact; prices low at INR 60-66/kg
items.quote: And secondly, this year the crop size is very good, Basmati. And overall, it's 100, 150, 1-million-ton rice production of the country

items.statement: Paddy prices currently INR 64-66/kg for key varieties, down from INR 71/kg average in FY23
items.quote: The price of 1718, 1509, 1401 varieties are INR 64, INR 65, INR 66 roaming around.

items.statement: Rice prices at multi-year lows around $800/ton; good procurement opportunity
items.quote: So, now the bottom out is there, prices are very low, INR 665, INR 600, you divide by 88, it's nothing, it's less than $800, around $800 costing, I'm talking.

items.statement: H1 FY26 margin 9.3%; expects margins to grow in H2 due to low-cost procurement
items.quote: definitely our sale will grow, our margin will grow. Because our buying is absolutely perfect, perfect time. We are regularly buying, every day we are buying. It's a good price, cheap price, and we know where and how to sell.

items.statement: All planned capacity commissioned: three SORTEX plants in Karnal, new Gandhidham unit opened July, old rented unit ready for trial runs
items.quote: Everything is commissioned now. The plants which were promised in Karnal, they are complete and working. In Gandhidham, new unit was put up, that was opened in July. And one old unit, which was in a rented godown, that has been brought out to the family. That will be in production, maybe -- I mean, it's ready, only the trial runs have to be done.

items.statement: Current operational capacity 25-30 containers per day; can achieve INR 2,000 crore revenue if demand exists
items.quote: Look, the capacity wise, we can achieve INR 2,000 crore if we really have the demand. But I will be little conservative and the INR 1,500 crore we are targeting and that definitely we are going to achieve.

items.statement: Inventory peaked at INR 500 crore; expected to cross that level in FY26 due to large procurement at low prices
items.quote: The peak level of inventory has been INR 500 crores, approx INR 500 crore because I raised my insurance accordingly. And I think it will cross this year.

items.statement: No inventory loss in H1 FY26; company holds stock until profitable sale due to financial strength
items.quote: No, we have not got any hit at all. You see, let's assume we have some rice purchased at a higher price. And if we sell at a low price, definitely we are going to hit. I believe that's your question. But the company is strong enough to keep the stock for any long period. We are cash rich.

items.statement: Exports to 95 countries with ~400 customers; 10-15% Maharani brand, rest private label
items.quote: Because we are in 95 countries. We have multiple, around 400 customers around the world.

items.statement: Private label customers loyal for 5-30 years; minimal switching despite competition
items.quote: Some people don't -- I mean, the customer who are with me for 10 years, 20 years, 30 years, 5 years, 6 years, they don't deviate you know. I mean, somebody buying from us, if they are happy, why should -- why would they go here and there?

items.statement: US exports impacted by tariffs but not halted; buyers absorbing tariff cost
items.quote: Supply has never stopped. It is going. But yes, of course, it has come down. It is going. I mean, complete halt is not there. It's going.

items.statement: Growing demand from non-ethnic consumers in Europe, US, Australia, Sweden
items.quote: But now you see even the British, these Gora people, Americans or Europeans, they love our rice. If you go to any Indian restaurant now in Europe, you will be -- sometime I feel I'm alone Indian, all our local German people sitting.

items.statement: MEP (Minimum Export Price) removed long back; open trade now governed by economic laws
items.quote: There is no longer MEP issues. It's long back it was withdrawn. There's no MEP issue.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues (US tariffs, Gaza freight) caused temporary demand pause in Q1
items.quote: The first quarter, this geopolitics issues matter a lot. When US came out with these tariffs. So, it hit not only US-India business, it hit all around business.

items.statement: Domestic sales volume Q2 FY26: 4,650 tons; company not focusing on domestic market
items.quote: Sir, the volume for domestic for Q2 was 4,650 tons.

items.statement: Aging requirement 1-1.5 months for new crop rice to reach optimal cooking quality
items.quote: So, with the aging of one month or one and a half month, it will start going quicker.

items.statement: Saudi client deal near maturity; contributes to INR 1,500 crore confidence
items.quote: That is almost at maturity state or a complete set of orders have come. But before the commencement or shipping, still some discussions are going.

items.statement: Russia business progressing: 2-3 existing customers plus 1-2 new from exhibition participation
items.quote: Yeah, yeah. We have two, three customers right now, and there is addition also, two -- one or two more have come. We, because we participated there in Russia, in the exhibition, and we got customers.

items.statement: Basmati cultivation expanding beyond traditional GI areas to UP, MP, Rajasthan; Punjab/Haryana quality superior
items.quote: Now in entire Punjab, entire Haryana, UP, the new evolved varieties of Basmati, they are grown all around. It's grown in MP also, grown in Rajasthan also. So, it's growing.

items.statement: No significant competition in private label; high switching costs for buyers due to quality consistency needs
items.quote: We have no competitions, truly. It's not so easy to do private label work. It's very hard. And for large quantities and continued sales, there is competition, but not too much.

items.statement: Targets CD ratio of 80%, NIM 3%+, ROA 1%+, cost-to-income 55-56% by end of FY26
items.quote: CD ratio is 80%. NIM, as I was always telling 3% plus, ROA 1% plus, and cost-to-income ratio to between 55% - 56%.

items.statement: Expects ROA between 1.1% to 1.2% by end of FY26
items.quote: We expect to end the year with the ROA between 1.1% to 1.2%.

items.statement: NIM fell to 2.72% in Q2 FY26 from 2.82% in Q1 FY26 due to repo rate cuts impacting EBLR-linked book
items.quote: Net Interest Margin stood at 2.72% for Q2 FY '26 versus 2.82% in Q1 FY '26 and 3.23% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Expects NIM to bounce back to 3%+ supported by higher-yielding retail loans and easing cost of funds
items.quote: We are expecting a bounce back of yield on advances supported through our focus on higher-yielding retail and direct to corporate advances and combined with expected easing in cost of funds, which should see us going back to the previous level of around 3% plus.

items.statement: Cost of deposits reduced to 5.54% in Q2 FY26 from 5.73% in Q1 FY26 due to lower bulk deposits
items.quote: Owing to our reduction in composition of bulk deposits in total deposits, our cost of deposit has reduced on a Q-on-Q basis from 5.73% for Q1 FY '26 to 5.54% for Q2 FY '26.

items.statement: Cost of funds at 5.58% in Q2 FY26, expected to improve further as repo rate cuts transmit
items.quote: Cost of funds stood at 5.58% in Q2 FY '26 compared to 5.77% in Q1 FY '25 and 5.58% in Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio grew INR 400 crores in October; targets INR 1 crore per month per branch from 800 branches

items.quote: Distribution business has clocked a turnover of around INR100 crores. So this year, we are expecting from the next financial year, the distribution business will also be a profitable business.

items.statement: Price reductions implemented over past year; GST cut benefit passed to consumers; MRP reduced
items.quote: And also, the prices has been reduced. We have already -- from last year, we have started this price reduction. In GST also, we have reduced the prices. So now the price reduction is more or less complete.

items.statement: GST rate cut to 5% for footwear under INR2,500 implemented in late September 2025
items.quote: During the quarter, the company also implemented GST successfully across its network, ensuring a smooth transition with the benefits effectively passed on to the consumer.

items.statement: Mid-segment demand (INR500-1,500) remains weak; volume degrowth arrested but not yet reversed
items.quote: But yes, what Indrajit -da was saying that the mid-price point from, say, INR500 to INR1,000, INR1,500, there the products -- the demand of products has been a little -- you can't really put a number. It's not what we want it to be.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of ~30% for FY26 maintained; EBITDA margin expected to exceed prior 8.5-9% guidance for full year
items.quote: On the turnover, we stand by 30% approximately growth esimates, give or take a couple of percentage points here or there. On EBITDA, we had guided 8.5% to 9% and seeing the performance for the first half year, which is now 10%, we are very confident that we'll be able to exceed the guidance which we had shared with the Street last quarter.

items.statement: Acquired 60% stake in Elcome (defense electronics) with INR205 cr revenue and 25-26% EBITDA margin; consolidation targeted in Q4
items.quote: Coming to the acquisition of Elcome and Navicom together with Mr. Gujral has already explained, we expect this to be consolidated in our overall financials in Q4. That's what we are targeting. The company together with Navicom is currently doing about INR205 crores of revenue with a healthy EBITDA margin of 25%, 26% and PAT margin of near about 15

items.statement: Joint venture with Elemaster (Italy) for railway segment; global supply chain integration expected in future years
items.quote: The second tie-up which we made, as we have announced earlier, was a joint venture with Elemaster of Italy. And Elemaster is again a very old company servicing clients across the world and the venture which we are setting up in India would in the initial phase cater to the demand of the Indian market.

items.statement: Acquired KSolare (solar inverters) with Premier; Syrma to manufacture modules at Pune facility; inverter revenues in KSolare books
items.quote: KSolare has been acquired 51% by Premier and 49% by Syrma SGS. So the consolidation will happen at the Premier end and not at the Syrma end. KSolare is manufacturing inverters, primarily rooftop and have capability of manufacturing other types of inverters also.

items.statement: PCB project ECMS approved; groundbreaking in December; trial production by December 2026; total capex INR1,500 cr over FY26-28
items.quote: The PCB project, which we are setting up since our last call, we have got the ECMS approval from the Government of India. We were the first among the 3 companies. And the project has already been approved by the Andhra Pradesh government, and we should be breaking ground for construction in the coming months, somewhere in December. And we hope that by December '26, we should be able to start out o

items.statement: H1 capex INR45 cr; expect INR60-100 cr in H2 including PCB investment
items.quote: Coming to capex for the half year, we had spent around INR45 crores during the H1 of this year, and we expect to invest around INR60 crores to INR100 crores, including my investments towards the PCB business also in the balance of the year.

items.statement: Order book INR5,800 cr as of September end; auto 35%, consumer ~35%, industrial ~35%, healthcare 6-7%
items.quote: With this when we see the overall order book position as of September end is approximately INR5,800 crores, which comprises maximum from auto segment, which is around 35%. Both consumer segment and industrial segment contributes near about 35% in the order book, open order book currently.

items.statement: Onboarded 8 major customers with $100M potential next year; signed long-term framework contract with $250M potential over 2-3 years
items.quote: For the current quarter, we have onboarded 8 major customers, which have a potential of giving revenues of $100 million in the next year. In addition to that, we have now started focusing on long-term framework contracts with the customers. And we have entered into one such contract with one of our major customers, which has the potential of giving a revenue of about $250 million over a 2-, 3-year

items.statement: Gross margin 23.8% in Q2, 24.3% in H1 (up 500 bps YoY); operating EBITDA margin 10.1% in Q2 and H1
items.quote: Our gross margin for the quarter is about 23.8% and for the half year it is 24.3% with a healthy expansion of 500 bps here. My operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at healthy around INR116 crores which is a 56% growth on a year-on-year basis and again 10.1% of EBITDA margin, operating EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Organic revenue growth 37% YoY in Q2; driven by auto, industrial, IT segments; export revenue grew 40% YoY
items.quote: For the quarter ending September 2025, we did INR1,146 crores of revenue, which is a growth of 37% on a year-on-year basis. This robust growth for the period is contributed by higher growth in auto, industrial and IT segment.

items.statement: Net working capital 73 days in Q2 (up 4 days YoY); target to reduce to 60-65 days by year-end
items.quote: Coming to our networking capital as of September end my overall networking capital days is around 73 days which is 4 days higher on a year-on-year basis. We again continue to make efforts to bring it down to below 65 days and we are confident of bringing down by another 5 to 7 days in next 2 to 3 quarters.

items.statement: Gross debt INR282 cr; treasury INR758 cr; net cash INR477 cr as of September
items.quote: Moving to our debt and treasury position, we have a total gross debt of around INR282 crores as on September 9. And on treasury we hold a healthy balance of around INR758 crores as of September 8. With this we have a net cash position of INR477 crores.

items.statement: Business mix improved: industrial 26% (vs 21% LY), auto 24% (vs 21% LY), consumer 32% (below 35% target)
items.quote: When we see this overall business mix wherein the industrial sector contributed 26% as against 21% in H1 of last year. So it has increased as the business mix here in this current year. Similarly, auto has also contributed 24% of my total business as against 21% of last year. And consumer sector has contributed around 32% in H1 as anticipated and previously communicated that we will bring it down

items.statement: No discounts on long-term framework contracts; capacity commitment mutual with customers
items.quote: See, there are no discount for things to be given on the long-term framework contracts. It's just that we have to build up capacity, we have to commit capacity. So with big customers, it's a mutual 2-way fee.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty impacting decisions; expect clarity before Christmas; US exports 5-6% of revenue currently
items.quote: On the tariff part, I think the last ball is yet to be born. There is still a lot of confusion, lack of clarity, and that has impacted us slightly decision-making and taking only need-based supply. But I think from whatever we hear in the press for whatever it is worth, I think the worst is behind us and in the coming few weeks or a month or so, I'm confident before Christmas, we should have a dea

items.statement: PCB Phase 1: multilayer line 700K sqm/yr; Phase 2 (CCL, HDI) to start end of FY27 based on utilization
items.quote: On the multilayer line, we are putting up multilayer line, which has a capacity of approximately 700,000 square meters per annum. The building and the facilities and the utilities are being put up for the complete 3 potential lines, which we'll be putting up.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty causing supply chain constraints; higher inventory (INR100 cr) for rare earth and tariff-related volume push-outs
items.quote: We are carrying higher inventory by almost INR100 crores, mainly because of anticipation of supply chain constraints around rare earth and some bit of volume push out related to the U.S. tariffs, which we see gradually in the second half, we should be able to liquidate the same quickly.

items.statement: PCB steady-state revenue potential INR2,500 cr on INR1,500 cr capex (1-1.5x asset turnover); domestic focus initially, exports post-FY28
items.quote: See, PCB industry typically works at 1, 1.2 of the gross fixed assets, 1.5 max-max. So if we are targeting an investment of about INR1,500 crores, so the max revenues, which we can expect from the business would be INR2,500 crores.

items.statement: PCB capex phasing: FY26 minimal, FY27-28 INR700-800 cr combined; state incentives 50% capex received next year
items.quote: So FY '26 may not be INR200 crores only for PCB, it will be even much lesser. Maybe the capex is slightly loaded in FY '27. So what we are anticipating between FY '26, '27, '28 together is what we would be spending around INR700 crores to INR800 crores together.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand for PCB indigenization from large multibillion-dollar groups across auto, industrial, healthcare, medtech, telecom
items.quote: And the number of calls which our teams have been receiving from big companies in India who want to indigenize their supply chain of the PCB. And I'm talking of big multibillion-dollar groups who are showing interest that when is the plant going on stream.

items.statement: Full-year revenue growth guidance maintained at 18%-20% despite 24-25% H1 growth due to Uniclan consolidation base effect
items.quote: But if you see in the second half in the base period, Uniclan was already consolidated. So there, we'll see the growth in line with our 18% to 20% targeted range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 16.5%-17.5% range for full year
items.quote: 16.5% to 17.5% is a decent range that we'll be comfortable operating in.

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated capex of INR150 crores including capital advances; full-year guided range INR210-225 crores
items.quote: For the 6-month period, we have done a consolidated capex of approximately INR150 crores including capital advances and are on track for our guided full year capex estimate in the range of INR210 crores to INR225 crores.

items.statement: 44-acre expansion project: first building possession expected Q4 FY26, commercial production from Q1 FY27; pencil capacity addition in first building
items.quote: But we are confident of getting the possession of the first building in Q4 FY '26 and start commercial production from Q1 FY '27.

items.statement: Pen capacity increased by ~1 million pens/day over past year; current capacity 3-3.25 million pens/day; targeting 5 million pens/day by end of FY26
items.quote: So by the end of this year, our combined capacity for pens, you know, which includes the regular ballpoint pens and one-time use examination pens, all put together to be close to 5 million pens a day.

items.statement: Core scholastic stationery/art capacity utilization upwards of 95%; office supplies/hobby & craft at 75%+ with continuous ramp-up
items.quote: But having said that, across all our core products like scholastic stationery, scholastic art material, our capacity utilization is upwards of 95%.

items.statement: GST 2.0 transition caused temporary disruptions in September (inventory clearance, order postponement); sales could have been 3-4% higher without transition impact
items.quote: But we believe that if this transition impact would not be there, our sales could have been about 3% to 4% higher than what we reported for the quarter.

items.statement: Post-GST restocking at distributor/retail level will be ongoing process coinciding with back-to-school period from December; no significant impact expected in Q3
items.quote: And the restocking at the distributor and the retail level will be an ongoing process and coincide with the back to school period, which will start from December.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 17.5% at upper end of guided 16.5%-17.5% range; employee cost increased 1% sequentially and 0.85% YoY due to hiring ahead of capacity ramp-up and GST disruption
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 17.5%. This consistent maintenance of EBITDA margins towards the upper end of our guided range of 16.5% to 17.5% demonstrates our operational efficiencies.

items.statement: GST rate reduction led to MRP reductions (e.g., pencil pack from INR60 to INR58); primary sales pricing increased 3-4% due to ITC loss on 0% GST products
items.quote: In terms of the company sales at the primary level, if you are asking me, the sales pricing would have increased by about 3% to 4%, not more than that, 3% to 4%.

items.statement: No significant margin impact from GST transition as cost increase from ITC loss passed through via revised MRPs
items.quote: So overall, I don't see a significant impact of this on the margins of the company.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 consolidated operating revenue INR567.9 crores (+24.1% YoY); domestic gross product sales +28% YoY, international +18.5% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated operating revenues for Q2 FY '26 stood at INR567.9 crores, a growth of 24.1% compared to the same quarter last financial year.

items.statement: 45-50% of total products impacted by GST rate reduction (45% from 12%/5% to 0%, 6% baby hygiene from 12% to 5%)
items.quote: So in terms of the product categories where GST has come down from 12% and 5% earlier to 0%, it currently contributes about 45% of our overall sales if we look at FY '25.

items.statement: Scholastic stationery, art, kits & combos combined grew ~4% YoY in Q2 and ~5.5% in H1 due to no significant capacity additions; growth from product mix change and slight ASP increase
items.quote: Like you said, this growth has been lower purely because there have no significant capacity additions that have happened in this segment. It's purely been growth due to change in product mix and slight increase in ASPs.

items.statement: General trade contribution declined to ~71% from 77% due to higher baby hygiene share (35% e-com), GST transition impact on GT, and festive season shift to gifting/decorative items; GT expected to return to ~75%
items.quote: And in the baby hygiene segment, almost 35% of sales come from e-commerce. Therefore, you'll see the modern trade and e-commerce segment on an overall consol basis increasing and GT coming a little low.

items.statement: US tariffs introduced in September; no significant Q2 impact as open orders fulfilled; going forward some orders postponed, capacity diverted to Chile (FILA distribution), Middle East, Sri Lanka, Nepal; no overall export sales impact expect
items.quote: So we believe that while from a U.S. perspective, in the current quarter and going forward, there will be an impact until the tariff issue is not resolved. But there have been alternative strong demand from markets.

items.statement: Discount incentives/rebates increased in Q2 due to GST transition credit notes for MRP reductions on channel stock
items.quote: In this quarter, we've had a slight impact, a little more scheme discount rebate given, again, because of the GST transition for whatever stock the channel had and the reduction in MRP that we did, we had to give a little -- we had to issue credit notes for that.

items.statement: Sales team expanded from ~800 to >900 people over past year; hiring ahead of production ramp-up for new plant, adhesives, mechanical pencils
items.quote: If you see over the last few quarters. Our sales team now is more than 900 people. And if I remember correctly, last year, same time, we were close to about 800 people.

items.statement: Revenue per rupee of capex target: INR3 revenue for every INR1 invested in capacity; plan capacity enhancements at 50-60% utilization
items.quote: So basically, for us, wherever we are investing INR1 in building capacities, we target to achieve revenues of INR3. And as soon as we believe that for a particular product or a category where demand also is still strong, and we believe a lot of value DOMS can add, as soon as we reach about 50%, 60% utilization, we plan for other capacity enhancements.

items.statement: GST 2.0 reforms slashed rates on key categories (12%/5% to 0%, baby hygiene 12% to 5%); structurally positive long-term but caused temporary September disruptions
items.quote: A notable highlight for the quarter was the government's announcement of GST 2.0 reforms, slashing rates across some of our key product categories. Although we believe GST reduction is structurally positive, it led to temporary disruptions in September.

items.statement: Kits/combo packs taxed at 18% GST (mixed supply rule); standalone 0% GST items in kits become ITC eligible; no strategic shift to push kits over standalone products
items.quote: Most of our kits and combination packs are sold at a GST rate of 18%. And for the 0 percentage items that go in that kits and combination pack where you're actually charging 18%, you become eligible for input tax credit.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guided flattish vs FY25; growth expected from FY27
items.quote: In the earlier calls, the guidance that we had given for this year is that we would remain flattish in this year because these are the changes that we intend to make.

items.statement: FY27 expected to return to growth trajectory
items.quote: So FY '26 will be flattish like FY '25. And the year after that, we certainly expect to see growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided 27-30% range
items.quote: Our EBITDA will remain in the range of 27% to 30% as we've always guided. In a bad time, it could be 27%. In a good time, it could be 30%.

items.statement: Capex funded through internal accruals, no leverage planned
items.quote: So, Apurva, we -- whatever capex or growth plans we have, we should be able to fund that through internal accruals. There should not be any leverage on the balance sheet for that purpose.

items.statement: Opened 5 premium flagship stores in H1 FY26; 4-5 more in pipeline
items.quote: As a part of this transition, we opened 5 new premium flagship stores in high potential and strategic locations during H1 FY '26.

items.statement: Net store count flattish for next 2 years; opened 15, closed 13 in H1; target ~23 closures and similar openings full year
items.value: 15 opened, 13 closed in H1; ~23 closures full year
items.quote: So in H1, we have opened 15 new stores and closed 13 old stores. And we intend by the end of the year to close totally about 23 stores out of 13 have already been closed. And we intend to open a similar number of stores by the end of the year.

items.statement: Soft demand and muted footfalls in H1 FY26
items.quote: Operationally, the first half of the year, we continued to face soft demand and muted footfalls.

items.statement: H1 FY26 gross margin 59%, up 200 bps YoY due to product mix change
items.quote: Supported by a gross margin of approximately 59%, up 200 basis points year-on-year, driven by a change in product mix.

items.statement: Website sales more than doubled YoY in H1 FY26
items.quote: Sales through our website have mor e than doubled year -on-year in H1 FY '26, reflecting a stronger brand salience, improved digital image and an enhanced omnichannel journey

items.statement: Working capital days 217 in H1 FY26; expected to revert to 170-180 days as sales normalize
items.quote: Our working capital days stood at 217 days for H1 FY '26. This increase is purely a reflection of our business model and current market conditions and not a structural change.

items.statement: Receivables fully secured via deposits; zero bad debt history
items.quote: Importantly, receivables remain fully secured through deposits and long-standing partner relationships and MUFTI has never incurred a bad debt in its history.

items.statement: Bangladesh supply chain disruption delayed ~2 lakh pieces (~INR20-25 cr revenue) from Q2 to Q3
items.quote: Around 1 lakh pieces, which we expected to come from Bangladesh in September and sold got delayed to October, November. And similarly, around 1 lakh pieces, we picked up earlier from -- last year, it was in October. This time, we picked up them back in September. So around 2 lakh pieces, the sales got impacted by around 2 lakh pieces, which should be around INR20 – 25 crores.

items.statement: 60-70% of portfolio below INR2,500 realized sale price; GST rate cut benefit to be passed on
items.quote: About 60% to 70% would be below.

items.statement: Supported franchisees and MBO partners during slow liquidation; long-standing relationships
items.quote: In a softer demand environment, we supported our franchisees and MBO partners due to slight slower stock liquidation and corresponding payments.

items.statement: Brand lifecycle differs from peers like Cantabil, Rare Rabbit; confident of bounce back
items.quote: See, I would say that depends on the life cycle that the brand is in its journey. Over a period of time, we have seen many ups and downs. We are very confident that we'll bounce back to our levels again.

items.statement: GST rate changes: some products below INR2,500 benefit, some above see price increase; benefit passed on per government directive
items.quote: What we see is that higher footfalls have been created for hard goods and not so much for apparel. However, in a brand like ours, we have to wait and watch as to how it pans out because not everything we make is below INR2,500. A lot of the products we make are above.

items.statement: Investment phase may keep profitability lower for next 1.5 years; marketing spend increasing to 6-7%
items.quote: However, profitability would still be lower in the forthcoming year because we will be enhancing our expenditures on marketing.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR284 cr vs INR310 cr YoY; PAT INR25 cr; ROCE 16%, ROE 14.5%
items.quote: crores in H1 FY '26 as against INR310 crores in H1 FY '25. Gross profit stood at INR167 crores with a GP margin of 59% for the half year ended. EBITDA for H1 FY '26 stood at INR79 crores. Our EB ITDA margin stood at 27.9%. PAT for H1 FY '26 stood at INR 25 crores. Our PAT margin stood at 8.9%. ROCE and ROE as on September 2025 basis stood at 16% and 14.5%, respectively

items.statement: No plans to enter women's or kids wear in medium term
items.quote: Anywhere in the medium term, we don't have in our mind to enter the kids wear or women wear.

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance of INR 1,750 crores will not be met due to Modasa plant commissioning delay of 4-5 months
items.quote: It will definitely not be possible to meet the guidance. Initially, we were saying that we will get the commissioning in July -August. So, we were assuming that we will get the benefit in our festive season.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% for Q4 FY26 under review; will reassess after sales numbers stabilize
items.quote: As Navinji said, we are assessing the situation. So, we will assess the sales number. Accordingly, we will revert back to the margin guidance.

items.statement: GST rate reduction caused trade disruption in September-October; revenue impact of INR 15-18 crores across two months
items.quote: In September in terms of value, there was an impact of around INR 8-10 crores. And in October there was an impact of INR 3-4 crores. In total, there was an impact of INR 15-18 crores.

items.statement: Festive season contributed INR 10 crores positive growth in Q2 FY26 despite low base and supply chain issues
items.quote: If we quantify it we get a positive growth of INR 10 crores due to the festival.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 gross margin 26.4% including INR 5.3 crores subsidy income; EBITDA margin 6.4%; PAT margin 6.8% with exceptional income
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR 99.2 crores, translating to a gross margin of 26.4% compared to 26% in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to stay in 25-26% range for rest of FY26 with 3-4% potential upward movement in raw material prices
items.quote: We are expecting the balance of the remaining year , there will be more or less stable prices around it. 3-4% upward movement can come but not much in expectation.

items.statement: Modasa plant capex mostly complete; INR 7-8 crores remaining to be spent in Q3 FY26
items.quote: Almost majority portion is completed some portion will come in Q3 because in October trial run has started, so some portion will come in October that is Q3 which will be in the range of INR 7 crores to INR 8 crores.

items.statement: Besan plant being installed at Nagpur; INR 20 crores capex for Rajkot reinstatement; no other major capex planned
items.quote: We are installing a besan plant in Nagpur that is under process. There it will come a little and somewhere else, as of now we don't feel the further capacity requirement.

items.statement: Modasa plant trial production started; billing for 3 hero products begun; full 26-product basket expected by end of November 2025
items.quote: The billing for 3 hero products has started from there . We are adding one product every day. We are adding a total of 26 products. So, by the end of November, all the products will be added.

items.statement: Third-party manufacturing agreements at Hiriyur (Karnataka) and Kashipur (Uttarakhand) add over 10,000 metric tons per annum capacity
items.quote: Together, these facilities add over 10,000 metric tons per annum of capacity, enabling us to serve southern and northern markets more efficiently and reduce lead times.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 41-45%; target of 70% utilization pushed out to 2-2.5 years from FY27
items.quote: Yes, I am saying that our current capacity utilization is around 41% to 45% It will take around 2 to 2.5 years to reach that.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR 697.8 crores; Q2 FY26 revenue INR 375.7 crores up 16.6% Q-o-Q; H2 FY26 revenue expected to exceed INR 700 crores
items.quote: It will definitely be more than INR 700 crores.

items.statement: GST reduction improved company retention by 0.5%; distributor margin maintained at 6.6% post-GST; retailer margin unchanged at INR 51 per strip
items.quote: In channel margin, our retention goes up by 0.5%. Earlier, we were giving 7.5% to the distributor at the gross level. Since 12% was GST, he used to get 6.6% post deducting 0.9%.

items.statement: Wafer realization improved ~6% via price hikes; trade incentives reduced (retailer margin cut); channel distributor margin fixed
items.quote: If you see, in wafer, our revenue growth as compared to volume growth is higher . That is a reflection of roughly 6% higher. We have improved our realisation in wafer.

items.statement: New product launches: popcorn (sustainable run rate INR 40-43 lakhs), wafer biscuits (INR 42 lakhs), Jeera Popcorn (INR 1.05 crores in October); target to reduce palm oil dependent products by 25% in 3-5 years
items.quote: So, in next 3 to 5 years, we intend in percentage term palm oil dependent products contribution we should reduce by 25%.

items.statement: INR 5 price point SKU contribution improved from 66% to 62% in Q2 FY26; focus on improving product mix for better realizations
items.quote: In INR 5 price points sku this quarter, it has improved from 66% to 62%.

items.statement: 858 active distributors as of Q2 FY26; double service initiative re-initiated in Gujarat; expanding depth in 350km radius of Nagpur and 200km clusters at Hiriyur and Kashipur
items.quote: By Q2 FY26, we had 858 active distributors, reflecting steady expansion and better on-ground execution.

items.statement: E-commerce revenue progression: INR 1.92 crores in Q2 FY26; H1 FY26 e-commerce INR 3.5 crores vs INR 1 crore H1 FY25; modern trade INR 1.32 crores in Q2 FY26
items.quote: Our last 6 quarters e-commerce progression is INR 37 lakhs, INR 63 lakhs, INR 1.19 crores, INR 1.03 crores, INR 1.53 crores and INR 1.92 crores.

items.statement: Wafer pricing had 17% gap vs competition; price hike reduced gap but impacted volume; supply chain disruption affected distribution pull for second product
items.quote: The aggressive stance we took in the wafer, we understand that it has not been converted into numbers. In that, the price hike we took was probably because there was a 17% gap between us and the competition.

items.statement: Potato inventory covered till December 15, 2025; new crop pricing uncertain; last year Q4 potato rates rose 3.5x to INR 35/kg impacting margins
items.quote: Last year, the rate of potatoes went up disproportionately in Q4. So, we have the cover till 15th December. We expect that we will be in control at that time.

items.statement: Insurance claim: INR 19.99 crores interim payment received; total loss INR 47 crores; expecting similar amount in FY26 in 2-3 more installments
items.quote: If I talk about this financial year, we are expecting the similar amount which has come now We are expecting some amount around this in this financial year.

items.statement: Acquisition budget up to INR 200 crores; no target finalized; focus on food business in Gujarat (core states), not namkeen; funding structure to be decided later
items.quote: Madam, nothing has been finalized yet, we are seeing it now but yes, one thing will be that we will acquire it, it will be in a similar kind of industry, if not same.

items.statement: Acquisition target: similar food business in Gujarat core states; category should not cannibalize existing portfolio; focus on inside-home consumption products
items.quote: We are looking for a category that does not cannibalize our existing product category, number one. Number two, which comes under the fitment of our yard vision, that how to make a brand of inside home consumption.

items.statement: Gujarat run rate target: INR 125+ crores per month in 2-3 years; current throughput per outlet to jump 30-40% via double service and marketing
items.quote: So, in Gujarat, we aspire that in the next 2 -3 years, our run rate per month should go beyond INR 125 crores.

items.statement: Supply chain disruption to reduce 90% after full Modasa product basket; conservative estimate 6-7 months to recover lost consumer base
items.quote: After getting the full product basket from Modasa, our supply chain disruption will reduce by 90%.

items.statement: Rajkot facility reinstatement on track; production not constrained as Gondal covering output; relocation from Gondal to Rajkot when ready
items.quote: Yes, it is on track . One thing is that our production is not constrained anywhere . So, whatever will be in Rajkot will shift from Gondal to Rajkot.

items.statement: Order book stands at over INR2,600 crores with INR1,600+ crores government and INR960+ crores corporate, executable over 3 years
items.quote: And to give you a little idea on the order book, we are sitting on an order book position of more than INR2,600 crores. And it has a great bifurcation, almost more than INR1,600 crores is government and more than INR960 crores is corporate.

items.statement: Corporate revenue grew 53% YoY in H1 FY26 with 92 new clients added across pharma, manufacturing, logistics, warehouse, IT/ITES
items.quote: Revenue from this segment grew by almost 53% year-on-year in the H1 FY '26. We added 92 new corporate customers during the H1 FY '26, building on the 114 clients added in the FY '25 totally.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.32% down 7 bps YoY due to higher employee and admin costs from expansion; H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 6.47% up 11 bps YoY
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding the other income for the quarter stood INR17.91 crores, up 5.3% year-on-year. Despite moderate growth in operating profit, EBITDA margin declined slightly by 7 basis points to 6.32% primarily due to higher employee and administrative cost associated with business expansion and establishment of new offices as a part of our pan-India penetration strategy.

items.statement: Government directive to cancel legacy renewable bids without PPAs does not affect Vikran's projects; private sector solar momentum strong
items.quote: So, absolutely we are not at all affected with that decision on that program. That is separate initiatives. We have n number of things shown in pipeline. But there is practically no progress.

items.statement: Strategy to expand into international markets, particularly Africa and Middle East
items.quote: As a part of our strategy growth roadmap, we aim to expand into infrastructure EPC projects within the private sector, explore opportunities across international markets, particularly in Africa and the Middle East, and stren gthen our presence in the Water segment.

items.statement: Team of 850 professionals across 22 states; 170 at Thane HQ with in-house design/engineering across Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Instrumentation, Signalling, Telecommunication
items.quote: So, with this capability, we are covering the complete infrastructure netwo rk in 22 states with our team size of 850 professionals across the board, and we have a very centralized 170 professionals sitting at Thane office.

items.statement: Positive cash flows expected from FY28 onwards after full deployment of IPO working capital
items.quote: In overall capacity, as we have said that, yes, this working capital deployment will take about around a year to deploy completely. And once that is deployed, probably from FY '28 onwards, you can say that, yes, you will start looking at the positive cash flows from there.

items.statement: With additional working capital, half-year solar revenue can grow for 7 months; next year overall target INR 2,000 crore+
items.quote: With this additional working capital, probably for half year, we can grow from here for 7 months, and next year definitel y we can reach to the overall target where the working capital is invested and probably will be INR 2000 crore plus.

items.statement: Deploying 35-40 project teams simultaneously for solar EPC execution across multiple sites in Jalna, Dharashiv, Solapur
items.quote: So, the strategy here is deploy around 35 to 40 project teams at site at a time to give it a better progress.

items.statement: India Ratings upgraded credit rating to A- stable reflecting consistent performance and financial prudence
items.quote: Reflecting our consistent performance and financial prudence, India Rating s has upgraded our credit rating to A minus stable.

items.statement: Strong structural tailwinds: India targeting 500 GW renewable capacity by 2030; transmission evacuation needs for 300+ GW renewable energy
items.quote: With India targeting 500 gigawatt of renewable capacity by 2030, Solar EPC, grid integration and transmission infrastructure are seeing strong traction.

items.statement: Selective bidding strategy maintains 20-22% win ratio; focus on profitable orders with better payment terms over volume
items.quote: So, keeping all these things, but our win ratio is consistently, we are maintaining it around 20% to 22%. So, we bid very carefully, like for example, some good project is there.

items.statement: Unbilled revenue (contract assets) ~INR 400 crore; contract liabilities ~INR 25-50 crore
items.quote: The total would be about INR 400 crores approximately. And there are some projects in which the billing is going ahead as compared to the cost incurred, you will find in the contract liabilities as well. Some of the amount from INR 25-INR50 crores will be there as well.

items.statement: Targets ₹600 crore top line in 24-30 months and ₹950 crore in 48-54 months, with ~₹300 crore from transformers
items.quote: Within about 24, 30 months, we are targeting around ₹600 crores of top line and within 48 to 54 months, we are targeting ₹950 crores of bottom line.

items.statement: Aims for ₹450 crore turnover with current overhead structure, enabling 9-10% bottom line
items.quote: We can achieve around ₹450 odd crores of turnover. The overhead incremental cost will be bare minimal. So once that is achieved, a bottom line of about 9%, 10% will not be a challenge for us.

items.statement: Working towards 9% bottom line target; EBITDA and EPS increased despite higher HR and marketing costs
items.quote: The major points to highlight here is that, we are working on our margins. So the bottom line target that we have of 9%, that we are gradually working towards that.

items.statement: Engineering, foundry, heating, hardening, casting segments picking up; steel segment sluggish due to monsoon and inventory
items.quote: But the engineering segment and the other segments like foundry, heating, hardening, castings, those have picked up and that is why we are seeing a differential.

items.statement: Induction capacity ~70% utilised post-expansion (can do ₹300 crore); transformer capacity available pending approvals and orders
items.quote: After capacity expansion, we are going at around 70 odd percent, you can say for the induction side. And transformer now, we are just, the capacity is available with us.

items.statement: Gaining share from Electrotherm in steel melting furnaces via energy efficiency; competing with Inductotherm in forging/foundry via application development; competing with mid-sized players (Shilchar, Indo Tech) in solar transformers 7-25 M
items.quote: We have the most efficient furnace. We openly say they are in all our marketing documents, proposals, everything. So that is helping us gain market share from Electrotherm.

items.statement: Building global partner network (US JV, Brazil/Mexico/Argentina ties, UK office); targeting retrofit market in US/Europe; CE/UL certifications in process
items.quote: a joint venture in the U.S. We are just ironing out the legal aspects before we make t he investments. T he company has been set up. Marketing has started. We have also tied up with companies in Brazil, Mexico, Argentina to cater to the South American market

items.statement: IPO proceeds: capex exhausted (~₹2 cr left), working capital portion mostly remaining, reserved for transformer working capital needs
items.quote: The CapEx fund is exhausted. I think only ₹2 crores is left for some machinery. That is exhausted. Some portion of the working capital has been exhausted, but most of the fund that is left now is essentially working capital.

items.statement: West Bengal incentive revocation no impact; only central MCIP subsidy (20% capex) factored, offset against fixed assets
items.quote: We have never taken that into our calculation. We have only taken the MCIP, the Ministry of Electronics Central Government. Those subsidies we get that is 20% of CapEx.

items.statement: Key risk is time for initial approvals/reference creation; once approvals and first orders secured, exponential growth expected
items.quote: the only thing I can see is that the initial reference creation or the initial approval process, that is taking a little bit of time. But once that is t hrough, I think then we are going to start seeing exponential growth

items.statement: Monthly revenue run rate dropped from ~6 crore to 1.8 crore after Amazon stopped selling refurbished products in February 2025.
items.quote: Many of you would be aware that this particular FY has been a challenging year for us, largely because of the Black Sun event of Amazon deciding to not sell any refurbished products on their Indian platform right. Uh, so our monthly revenue run rate dropped from almost 6 codes to 1.8 crore on a monthly basis, this as many of you are well aware of happened in February this year.

items.statement: Recovered ~75% of lost revenue in H1 FY26 by focusing on own web channel and expanding B2B/enterprise channels.
items.quote: So, in H126, the 6 months that we have just completed, right? I would say that we are slightly happy to, uh, also share with the group that we have been able to recover almost 75% of the lost revenue by focusing on our own web channel which is newjaisa.com.

items.statement: Expect full recovery of monthly run rate to pre-Amazon levels by end of FY26.
items.quote: So, by the end of this year, we feel we will would have in terms of like monthly run rate, we feel we would have done a full recovery by end of this year.

items.statement: Expect to remain in the red (EBITDA negative) for FY26 while rebuilding channels and investing in marketing.
items.quote: if we are looking at pure play on the pack levels and stuff like that, yes, I mean, this year, we will continue to be in red, as we build it back and we continue to invest on the marketing.

items.statement: COGS remained flat in H1 FY26; gross margins impacted by product mix shift toward lower-margin desktops in B2B channel.
items.quote: Looking at the COX, the COX remains flat for us, largely also driven because our product mix have a different cork structure. Desktops do not have high margins because it's a low value-add product. Whereas laptops have higher margin as we gravitated our business more towards B2B there was a large demand for the desktops which impacted our gross margins as such, though they remained flat.

items.statement: Employee cost dropped ~70% YoY in H1 FY26 after headcount reduction from 400+ to ~250; marketing spend increased as % of sales.
items.quote: if you compare from last H2 to now, as we are discussing, we have almost, it's a 70% drop in terms of the employee cost largely because we reduced our headcount there to manage the burn rate. Yes, we continue to over-leverage on marketing as we build our channel and that's the reason you see, as a percentage of the sale, marketing cost has gone up.

items.statement: Excluding one-time ESOP and inventory write-offs, operating loss was ~7% of revenue in H1 FY26, driven by ~5% higher marketing spend and fixed cost under-absorption at 40% capacity utilization.
items.quote: overall, if we remove the one-time impacts which have been like there, we have been 7% negative. Largely driven by higher marketing spend of around 5%, and of course, our other cost also includes a fixed cost right, and we are literally, in terms of capacity utilization, we have come down to almost 40% of the fixed assets that we are utilizing.

items.statement: Capacity utilization fell to ~40% of fixed assets after Amazon exit; expect to return to full utilization within a year.
items.quote: we are literally, in terms of capacity utilization, we have come down to almost 40% of the fixed assets that we are utilizing. Of course it is impacting all this, but I think the good aspect of the thing is that 5 to 6 months, it's been a time, kind of a 200% growth on the other channels as such, so that we will be hopefully within a year back to full utilization as such.

items.statement: D2C website monthly run rate grew 4x from ~50-60 lakh in Feb 2025 to 2.5+ crore; active users >1 million; website ranking improved >1000%; social followers grew from <3,000 to 50K+.
items.quote: from our rock bottom of around, where the website was only contributing around 50 to 60 lakhs a month in February to 2.5 plus kind of a run rate, that is a 4X growth in the last 4 to 5 months.

items.statement: B2B/SME/Enterprise revenue grew from <1 crore monthly run rate in Q4 FY25 to >4.5 crore in Q1 FY26; closed 50+ accounts including a top-3 EMS company and second-largest NBFC.

items.statement: Went live on second-largest tech marketplace in India (pilot phase); expanded modern trade partnership to 4 stores of a 60-store chain in another southern state.
items.quote: We went live on the second largest tech marketplace in India. This is again in a pilot phase. I will not be able to talk more about it at this moment.

items.statement: Received R2 certification (international accreditation), enabling direct procurement from large corporates and MNCs; only 5 companies in India hold this.
items.quote: also to share with the group, we formally received the R2 certificate, this is an international accreditation and only 5 companies in India have that, which allows us to directly procure and work with large corporates and the multinationals, because it's one of the prerequisites there.

items.quote: Right now, they stand at around 6% to 7% direct purchases rest are via recyclers, but I think this month we are already the team…We have to as I said, I think the team also we took very conservative approach, let go of a lot of people, as you saw the headcount coming around drastically from 400 to 250. items.quote: Key things I want to call out are like a couple of things, So first is in terms of inventory in hand, there is definite reduction of almost 5 crores as such which is so and we will continue to keep our focus on the inventory, it is still on a higher side slightly but as the sales pick up, We are very confident that we will be able to come to a much more manageable level as such. Trade receivables

items.quote: So, I think fresh purchases were to the tune of 9 crore something like that, yeah So that was for space but at the same time for the inventories also.

items.statement: Conservative inventory write-offs: wrote off pre-4th gen models, DDR3/DDR4 RAM, older HDDs; 10-15% of inventory remains 6th gen and below; use 15-20% annual depreciation on internal inventory aging.

So, for example, like, if we have sold out a particular product line and there is certain excess of the spares that has come out of that particular model, we are writing those off. We also wrote off some of the

items.statement: Headcount reduced from 400+ in Feb 2025 to ~250 by May 2025; now incrementally rebuilding team for H2 FY26 growth.
items.quote: In February we were around 400 plus headcount which we over the next 3 months, which is your Feb, March, April and May we brought it down to around 250. As we look at the next subsequent slides, a good part is that the growth is there and we are revamping the team or rescaling the team again in a prudent manner.

items.statement: Customer support complaints spiked during channel transition from Amazon to own channels; implemented Salesforce and phone support in last 20 days; ratings 4.3+ on 3,800 reviews.

We were… Amazon was most of the sales were through Amazon, so customer support was given by Amazon. items.quote: Desktops do not have high margins because it's a low value-add product. Whereas laptops have higher margin as we gravitated our business more towards B2B there was a large demand for the desktops which impacted our gross margins as such, though they remained flat.
