items.quote: So, when you do the rental calculation, you take a RV value, there you take an accelerated depreciation of almost 35-40% on a yearly basis. So, if it is going for 2 years you will depreciate, so you know that you're giving asset for X. You will only get like.

items.statement: Management aspires to maintain double-digit revenue growth of 20%-30% for FY26 and beyond.
items.quote: We are making every effort and are confident of maintaining the same double-digit growth between 20%-30% kind of thing. That is our aspiration.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined 60 bps to 12.4% in H1 FY26 due to currency volatility; management expects to adjust pricing and maintain previous year efficiencies by year-end.
items.quote: Our EBITDA stands at INR 979.9 lakhs, which marginally declined by 60 bps from 13% to around 12.4% due to currency volatility growth.

items.statement: Residential segment carries better margins than Corporate segment due to tendering and reverse auctions in corporate projects.
items.quote: The Residential segment typically has a little better margin than the Corporate segment. Companies tend to sometimes have things like a tendering system or reverse auction and those various kind of things.

items.statement: Strong demand visibility across residential automation and enterprise AV integration driven by rising disposable incomes, luxury housing growth, and workspace modernization.
items.quote: We see strong growth visibility across both residential automation and enterprise AV integration, supported by our longstanding brand partnerships and national distribution reach.

items.statement: Indian professional AV market projected to grow from $6.5 billion in 2025 to $17.3 billion by 2031; Smart Home segment to reach $30 billion by 2030 at 29% CAGR.
items.quote: With the Indian professional AV market projected to grow from $6.5 billion in 2025 to $17.3 billion by 2031. This vertical is positioned to be a key growth engine for the company in the years ahead.

items.statement: Human capital is the key constraint for faster expansion; hiring and training technically skilled staff takes 3-6 months before deployment.
items.quote: It is definitely not the capital. It is probably human capital . W e need to bring in , all these locations, people with the right skillset s in those locations, right

items.statement: Non-distribution revenue share increased from ~30% to 35% in H1 FY26 (distribution down from 70%+ to 65%), carrying higher margins.
items.quote: Last year and the year before, we see 70% plus, which is distribution. This year, it's now it is the first half, it's 65% distribution. So, we have actually increased. We have increased the non-distribution part, which is more margins also for us.

items.statement: Currency volatility caused margin dip; pricing adjustments lag import cost changes but are corrected over the full year.
items.quote: When there is some amount of volatility, and most of our products are imported. So, when there is some amount of volatility, we are not able to immediately correct pricing.

items.statement: Bulk of portfolio is imported; company does not hedge regularly, only on occasion during extreme volatility, and plans to introduce local products in future quarters.
items.quote: to be honest with you, we don't hedge much. We hedge on occasion when we see extreme volatility, sometimes hedging just beco mes a cost to company, right

items.statement: Residential clients include HNIs, celebrities, industrialists; corporate clients include enterprises modernizing workspaces, hospitality, education, and government projects.
items.quote: some of the biggest industrialists in the country and I cannot name them. So, we have some of those projects with them. And we have really residential projects, it just happens to be from a corporate source i n crores of rupees

items.statement: Competition is 90% disorganized, single-city operators with no service capability; Pro FX differentiates via pan-India service (28 centers), widest SKU range, 48-hour delivery, and technical support.
items.quote: Most of our competition, 90% of competition is totally disorganized competition, right? And the disorganized competition may be a little asset light, and you know, things like that. But in the long run, people want service.

items.statement: Business remains asset-light and efficiently managed with focus on working capital optimization.
items.quote: Our business continues to be asset-light and efficiently managed. We remain focused on margin stability, prudent cost management, and working capital optimization.

items.statement: Bringing in senior leadership for corporate, retail, and experience center verticals to ensure management bandwidth does not limit growth.
items.quote: we are bringing in also senior people within the team, who c an give dedicated attention and focus, because as the company grows management bandwidth shouldn't become a limiting factor

items.statement: Project execution timelines (2-3 years for large residential projects) create revenue recognition lag and constrain near-term scaling speed.
items.quote: The biggest constraint happens to be the time it takes to kind of work and executing certain client projects. So, we are happiest when somebody's project actually is getting over in a couple of months, and they are in a hurry. But very often, when we are working with these large big-ticket clients, some of them come to us at a design stage, the project is 2 years, 3 years in the pipeline.

items.statement: Management targets consolidated PAT margin improvement from current ~5% to 8-10% over next 1-2 years driven by B2C growth and new subsidiaries becoming operational
items.quote: I think we can move ahead to 8-10% is something that we are eyeing. But eventually we will see how the operations add up and at what period they add up.

items.statement: Management expects B2C revenue share to reach 18-20% by end of FY26 from current 13% in H1
items.quote: As we are talking about H1 right now, our B2C business growth grew from 4% last year to 13% for H1 so we are still waiting for considerable growth from 13% to probably 18 to 20% before the end of this financial year.

items.statement: Management targets B2C revenue share of 20-25% within next 1.5 years
items.quote: we look at at least this year and a year to come after we are looking at 20 to 25% of our B2C to be around 25% in next 1.5 year.

items.statement: Management expects B2C segment to grow another 6-8% in H2 FY26
items.quote: we are eyeing that again the next 6 months on B2C will be at least 6% to 8% more on that that is what our ideally our target is.

items.statement: Standalone B2B EBITDA margin is 32-33%; B2C EBITDA margin currently 35%+ and expected to improve further
items.quote: our B2B margin which we have been presenting our numbers for past few years, our EBITDA margin is around 32 to 33% which we continue that we will be in that range on the B2B side and on the B2C side, as of now we have initiated our revenues right now which we are already looking 35% plus EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin is ~7% due to US subsidiary (Espee) contributing ~80% of revenue with lower margins but high ROE
items.quote: Overall, from the consolidated revenues, around 80% is from our US subsidiaries.

items.statement: B2C business grew from 4% to 13% of revenue in H1 FY26; management focusing on niche rare molecules and first generic approvals
items.quote: During the period under review, our B2C business witnessed strong momentum, increasing from 4% to 13% with B2B accounting for the remaining 87%.

items.statement: Launched Rivastigmine patches across multiple Latin American markets, first entry into transdermal patch segment with more pipeline products
items.quote: We also marked a significant milestone with the launch of Rivastigmine patches across multiple markets. This is the first time we have been introducing a new therapeutic segment where our portfolio has these patches being distributed, sold in several Latin American markets.

items.statement: Secured two product awards in Nicaragua national tender; entered Algerian market with product registrations initiated; Bolivia subsidiary Relius Pharma SRL launched products in cardiovascular, hematology, neurology, anti-infectives
items.quote: In Central America we successfully participated in Nicaragua national tender and secured two key products awards further consolidating our presence in the important markets. In addition, we have entered Algerian market and initiated product registration activities a key step in expanding our presence in North Africa region.

items.statement: US subsidiary Espee is among top 3 global providers of Reference Listed Drugs (RLDs) for pharmaceutical research and development
items.quote: if you ever look it out on the numbers where this category of RLDs that we do, we are in amongst top 3 providers of RLDs which is reference listed drugs.

items.statement: Acquired US subsidiary Espee in 2024; recovered 80-90% of investment through profits earned since acquisition
items.quote: we acquired the subsidiary in 2024 and I think after that, since then we have been tracking the financials and I can say that we have almost like recovered 80 to 90% of our investment, what we have done to our profits.

items.statement: Planning to add subsidiaries in 3 new countries this financial year: Kenya, Chile, Dominican Republic
items.quote: putting it for this year, this financial year we are looking at three countries to add on our subsidiaries.

items.statement: Secured 37 new product approvals in ASEAN region during H1 FY26
items.quote: During the period we also secured 37 new approvals further deepening our regulatory footprint in the ASEAN region and reinforcing our commitment to broad based growth in emerging markets.

items.statement: Products reach 40+ countries; 95%+ of exports from advanced/niche formulations; strongest footprint in Latin America
items.quote: At Remus, we take great pride in the fact that our pharmaceutical formulations today reach patients in more than 40 countries around the world. Over the years, we have built a truly global presence, but our strongest footprint has been Latin America where we have not only achieved reach but more importantly earned real trust among doctors and patients.

items.statement: Actively participating in national tenders across countries with 20+ product submissions per market; focusing on private market in Africa with niche portfolio
items.quote: Lastly, we are actively participating in national tenders across various countries with submissions over 20 products per market. This reflects our continued focus on expanding access to our products and strengthening our participation in institutional business segment which is government tenders.

items.statement: Algeria strategy involves tech transfer and licensing deals earning royalties, licensing fees, and know-how transfer rather than direct manufacturing
items.quote: what we have been doing is we are doing a tech transfer and a licensing deal with them where every product that in future if they manufacture it at their end we get the royalties on the product that they sell along with that we get a licensing fee and a know-how transfer as well.

items.statement: Management acknowledges Africa tender market is cutthroat on pricing; chooses private market (20% share) with niche portfolio for higher margins over tender volume
items.quote: I know it is a cutthroat competition in terms of costing and pricing and everything but again our focus is always going to be the molecules that others don't make or there is hardly any player in the market who has a first generic approval of those products.

items.statement: MD personally travels ~180 days/year for market due diligence; spent 7-8 days in Algeria recently assessing market, distributors, regulations
items.quote: I personally travel almost 180 days a year checking all the markets, see how the markets are, looking at it. Even the new market which we recently started, I spent a good 7-8 days in Algeria to know how the market is.

But I believe if fingers crossed, everything goes well by December, we should see ourselves on the main board. That's how we see it, maybe early in December or something.

items.statement: Raw material price risk managed through immediate steel mill booking for short contracts and price variation clauses for long-term contracts

Then there is another contract, which is a long-te

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance revised to ~₹350 crore from earlier ₹365 crore, implying 8-10% growth vs prior 15-20%
items.quote: instead of, 15-20% probably we'll be at 8-10%, I would say. So we are looking at around 350 crores of revenue instead of 365 what we were, looking at.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 revenue expected ₹80-83 crore; Q4 FY26 revenue expected ₹95-98 crore
items.quote: We should be able to do 95, 98 -odd crores in quarter four, and 80 to 83 crores in Quarter 3.

items.statement: FY26 overall EBITDA margin expected ~16% with additional H2 revenue
items.quote: with, another addition of 30 to 40 crores in the revenue, we should be well in 16% margin, EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Domestic Q2 sales declined due to early/extended monsoon and lower offtake from a major beverage customer; volumes expected to improve in Q4
items.quote: Domestic revenues for H1 were ₹133.48 crores, compared to ₹147.24 crores last year. In Q2, domestic sales were ₹64.37 crores, lower than ₹77.73 crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 14.78% vs 14.93% YoY; COGS improved to 60.26% from 62.75%; fixed costs up due to Unit 3 ramp-up
items.quote: Our EBITDA for H1 stood at ₹24.96 crores with margins at 14.78% as compared to ₹24.93 crores last year with margins at 14.93%.

items.statement: Injection moulding EBITDA ~11%, PBT ~7-7.5%; margins expected to improve with volume scale and value-added products
items.quote: In injection moldings, we our EBITDA is low at around 11% or so, but also our depreciation and interest are also low because It's not a high capex this thing, so around on PBT level, we are able to operate at around 7-7.5% over there.

items.statement: Olive Ecopak JV: Q2 revenue ₹12.05 crore, EBITDA ₹0.05 crore; targeting ₹16-18 crore in Q3, ₹22-24 crore in Q4; 50% capacity utilisation by Feb-Mar 2026

items.quote: We remain confident of achieving ₹16 to 18 crores revenue in Q3 and continuing the journey toward profitability.

items.statement: Olive Ecopak full capacity revenue potential ₹200-215 crore; FY27 target ₹140-150 crore at 15-16% EBITDA margin; full utilisation by FY28
items.quote: the, the capacity for JV when it operates to full scale, will be around 200 to 215 crores. Ramswaroop Thard: So, we are looking at reaching at least 140, 150 crores for 26-27, and maybe the idea will be to use to the full capacity by 27-28

items.statement: Injection moulding capacity expanded by 1,500 MT to 4,800 MTPA on tolling basis; can add 1,000-1,200 MT more in same space; further additions await tariff clarity
items.quote: On the capacities, we have expanded our Injection Moulding capacity by 1,500 MT, taking the total to 4,800 MTPA on a tolling basis.

items.statement: Thermoforming capacity increased from 8,770 MT (FY23) to 12,000 MT; operating at 70-75% utilisation due to mould change batch process; H1 output rose from 3,587 MT to 4,400 MT YoY
items.quote: now we are at 12,000 metric tons. So generally, we operate at 70% to 75% of the installed capacity in thermoforming as a segment due to the mold change process, because it's a batch process.

items.statement: Olive Ecopak installed capacity: 27,000 MTPA paper coating, 15,000 MTPA packaging; H1 utilisation low but improving (1,233 MT coating, 1,244 MT finished goods)
items.quote: Our installed capacities at Olive include: 27,000 MTPA for paper coating, and 15,000 MTPA for packaging products.

items.statement: Volume growth 7% offset by 5-6% price decline due to lower raw material prices; COGS improved from 62.75% to 60.26%
items.quote: Yes, so there was a volume growth of 7% and there is a price degrowth of around 5-6%.

items.statement: Injection moulding revenue surged 142% in H1 (₹12.97→₹31.44 cr) and 176% in Q2 (₹18.58 cr); thermoformed stable ~₹100 cr H1; sheets declined (₹48.88→₹36.29 cr H1)
items.quote: Injection Moulding products grew very strongly — up 142%, from ₹12.97 crores to ₹31.44 crores.

items.statement: Existing US injection moulding customers continuing despite tariffs (customer bears 50% tariff); new customer onboarding difficult; export markets: UK, Middle East, US
items.quote: customers, are continuing. They are not disturbing the supply chain. Manu Gupta: Okay. Ramswaroop Thard: Because probably they are also of the view that this will get diluted, but onboarding new customer, is difficult in current supply

items.statement: US tariffs challenging for new customer acquisition in injection moulding; expanding to UK, Europe, Middle East, Australia to diversify
items.quote: While tariffs in the U.S. have been a challenge for many Indian exporters, our export growth has continued mainly because of strong demand for our Injection Moulding products from existing customers. However, adding new customers in the U.S. has been tough under the current tariff environment.

items.statement: GST rate changes had minimal impact on product categories; Sarigam unit GST benefit ₹15-16 lakh in Q1, estimated ₹30-40 lakh in Q2
items.quote: I think so for our category of business, there's no change as such. Even in the beverage segment the duties were same. The end product also same way.

items.statement: Olive Ecopak export split at peak: 40% UK/Europe, 40% US, 20% Middle East; export margins slightly better than domestic
items.quote: I would say 40% from UK and Europe, 40% from US and 20% from Middle East.

items.statement: Principle to avoid new debt for next 2 years; fund Odisha capex via internal accruals; no equity dilution planned
items.quote: But the overall idea still remains not to go for any debt, huh? That's the principle, at least for next two years.

items.statement: Buyback proposal to be placed before board for consideration
items.quote: This decision will be taken by the board, so we'll definitely put up this proposal that, which has come from you, and let's see if, as the board takes decision, we'll let you know.

items.statement: Chairman's daughter joined handling export marketing; son to join in 2-3 years; co-promoter's daughter may join in 2 years; marketing team ~14-15 people, no CMO
items.quote: My daughter has just joined, and she is taking care of some export marketing. Ramswaroop Thard: And my son is still studying. Ramswaroop Thard: So, It's another 2 to 3 years for him to

items.quote: especially from the US markets, the sales, what we were expecting, due to this tariff we are not able to convert although many samplings has been done, rates have been approved by many of the customers.

items.statement: Targets FY26 revenue growth of 30-35% and PAT margin of 12-12.5% for full year
items.quote: If you see in a percentage-wise, we are going to target around 35% growth in top line and definitely, we want to have around 12.5% to 12% on PAT.

items.statement: Targets vessel operations to contribute 30-40% of total revenue next financial year
items.quote: What we are targeting out of our total top line, we are targeting that vessel operation next year should give around 30% to 40% of our top line.

items.statement: Plans to have four chartered vessels operational by end of December 2025
items.quote: Our plan is to have four vessels by end of December.

items.statement: Chartered vessels are 1,100 TEU each with effective capacity of ~700 TEU for heavy cargo
items.quote: We are deploying only 1,100 TEUs. And technically, if you see the heavy cargo, we can load around 700 TEUs on a vessel.

items.statement: NVOCC revenue grew from Rs 2.09 crore in H1 FY25 to Rs 31.93 crore in H1 FY26, up over 1,400%
items.quote: NVOCC revenue increased from 2.09 crores in the first half of Financial Year '25 to 31.93 crores in the first half of the Financial Year '26, a phenomenal growth of over 1,400%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin expanded 379 bps to 17.9%; Q2 EBITDA margin expanded 391 bps to 18.1%
items.quote: EBITDA grew 59.6% to Rs. 50.6 crores, with margins expanding by 379 basis points to 17.9%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 PAT margin improved to 11.4%; Q2 PAT margin improved to 11.5%
items.quote: Profit after tax for the half-yearly stood at Rs. 32.4 crores, recording 38.1% growth year-on-year, with PAT margin improving to 11.4%.

items.statement: Project cargo demand driven by transmission tower projects in Latin America and Africa, and earth-moving equipment
items.quote: Transmission tower project demand has actually gone up in the Latin American sector as well as into the African sector, which helps in increasing our business also.

items.statement: Ocean Cargo revenue Rs 243.5 crore in H1 FY26 (up 12.8% YoY); ODC, tyre & project cargo Rs 126.6 crore (up 40%); yarn & commodities Rs 106.62 crore (up 0.63%)
items.quote: Ocean Cargo revenue rising to Rs. 243.5 crores, reflecting a 12.8% year-on-year growth. Within this, yarn and yarn commodities delivered revenue of Rs. 106.62 crores, recording a steady 0.63% growth. ODC, tyre and project cargo continued to be the key drivers, contributing Rs. 126.6 crores, supported by a strong 40% growth during this period.

items.statement: Targets 70-80% of vessel cargo from own forwarding and NVOCC customers; will sell spare slots to third parties if needed
items.quote: We are targeting that 80 to 90% of the cargo is generated out of the forwarding as well as the NVOCC division.

items.statement: Long-term loans & advances increased ~Rs 43 crore mainly due to security deposits for vessel charters; deposits refundable on vessel return
items.quote: When we talk about the security, it has gone up mainly because of the charter of the vessels, basically. When you have a charter agreement with the vessel operation, you have to have a deposit with them.

items.statement: Increase in long-term borrowings is lease liability for ~3,000 leased containers per accounting standards; no actual debt increase; additional working capital facilities being arranged
items.quote: It is mainly a lease finance that is as per the accounting standard because we have around 3,000 containers (inaudible) 3,000 containers on a lease rental. So, as per the accounting standard, you are a chartered accountant. So, asset side as well as the liability side, we have to show that. Otherwise, there is no increase as far as long-term borrowings are concerned.

items.statement: NVOCC division scaled from Rs 2.1 crore to Rs 31.9 crore in H1 YoY, driven by Gulf and North African operations
items.quote: The NVOCC division delivered exceptional performance, generating Rs. 31.93 crores in the first half of the Financial Year ‘26 and recording S J Logistics (India) Limited November 18 th, 2025 a remarkable 1427% growth, driven by strong traction across our Gulf and North African

items.statement: Management cites geopolitical conditions, cargo flows, and SEBI disclosure restrictions as factors affecting guidance and communication
items.quote: We see the geopolitical conditions, we see the cargo outflow from India, cargo inflow in India. So, all these studies we do very periodically, very disciplined, and very systematically.

items.statement: Overall FY26 revenue growth target maintained at 25-30%
items.quote: We are sticking to the same number.

items.statement: FY26 EBITDA margin guidance 20-25% excluding other income
items.quote: I think between 20% to 25% we should achieve this year.

items.statement: IzmoMicro next year gross margin 30-40% and EBITDA margin at least 25%
items.quote: This year we will break even. And next year onwards, you will see a 30% to 40% gross margin and at least 25% EBITDA coming from there.

items.statement: IzmoMicro to reach 50-50 revenue contribution with legacy business in 3 years
items.quote: In the next 3 years, we expect 50-50 contribution of Izmo Micro and the rest of the business.

items.statement: Legacy automotive business normalized growth 10-15% once tariff issues resolve
items.quote: I would expect a 10% to 15% steady growth at least for next year and maybe more in the following year once things get stabilized.

items.statement: Current izmoMicro packaging capacity supports INR 80-100 crore revenue; post-expansion INR 1,000 crore
items.quote: See with the current capacity, I can do INR100 crores, maybe INR80 crores to INR100 crores. After the expansion, I can do INR1,000 crores turnover.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 23.4% excluding other income
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding other income for the 6 months increased 23.4% Y-o-Y to INR 18.79 crores and corresponding EBITDA margin is 23.4%.

items.statement: Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 22.5% excluding other income
items.quote: Our EBITDA, excluding other income for the quarter grew 42.4% Y-o-Y to INR13.51 crores, while corresponding EBITDA margin is 22.5%.

items.statement: Strong international and domestic demand for silicon photonics packaging; clients ramping up volumes
items.quote: The demand frankly, has surprised us. We had never expected such a hard -- but actually, we realized all this work was being done outside, which is now moving here.

items.statement: FrogData added 78 clients last quarter and launched two new products
items.quote: FrogData business is growing steadily. We added 78 clients last quarter. We also added two more products, like I said earlier.

items.statement: AI Factory leveraging India cost advantage for enterprise AI solutions
items.quote: AI Factory delivers enterprise-grade AI solutions at a fraction of Western pricing, a huge competitive moat.

items.statement: FrogData launched FixedOps Mojo and FixedOps Velocity targeting service marketing
items.quote: This quarter, we launched two new offerings, FixedOps Mojo and FixedOps Velocity, targeting the untapped service marketing opportunity.

items.statement: Engaging with 3 US OEMs; already have 2 US OEM clients
items.quote: We are working with three OEMs right now. We are talking to three OEMs. We already have two OEMs in US who are already our client.

items.statement: IzmoAuto acquired 22 new clients in Europe this quarter; completing major OEM rollout for 900 dealer sites
items.quote: This quarter alone, we acquired 22 new clients in Europe, proof of our multilingual platform, which resonates global ly. We are completing a major OEM contract for rollout of our digital marketing web platform for 900 dealer sites in Europe

items.statement: DSIR recognition driving inquiries from defence PSUs for indigenization projects
items.quote: We are getting a lot of inquiries coming in from most of the DPSUs after we received this that can we work on some projects for them?

items.statement: Government-driven fab initiative under Indian Semiconductor Mission with 50% central subsidy and state incentives
items.quote: the fab initiative has actually been driven by the government. They have told us that they would like us to be the leader in silicon photonics and also move towards the fab. So it's something which is being driven by the IS M Indian Semiconductor Mission

items.statement: Silicon photonics packaging market $2-3B today, projected $10B+ by 2030 at 25-30% CAGR
items.quote: Silicon photonics packaging is a $2 billion to $3 billion market today, projected to hit $10 billion plus by 2030, 25% to 30% CAGR, driven by explosive AI and data center demand.

items.statement: US/Europe auto market sluggish due to tariff confusion; dealers and OEMs cautious on spending
items.quote: The market in the U.S. and Europe has been subdued overall because with so much of confusion created by tariffs and all that mess, there has been a slow uptake of cars, slow -- I mean, less stocking of vehicles.

items.statement: Order book over ₹3,300 crore, 99% smart meters, AMISP-driven
items.quote: At the end of the quarter, we carried an order book of over ₹3, 300 crore, of which roughly 99% is smart meters.

items.statement: Expect Q3 better than Q2, Q4 much stronger; full-year revenue around ₹1,900-2,000 crore
items.quote: Whether it's ₹1, 900 crore or ₹2, 000 crore, we should be looking at somewhere in that zip code.

items.statement: Smart meter uptake improved over 12% sequentially in Q2; further step-up expected Nov-Mar FY26
items.quote: Smart meter uptake improved by over 12% sequentially in Q2. Going forward, we expect a further step-up in deliveries from November to March FY26 as on-ground inspections accelerate and AMISP roll-outs gather pace.

items.statement: Metering segment EBIT margins improved to ~17.5% in Q2 despite softer revenues
items.quote: Even in a quarter of softer metering revenues, segment EBIT margins improved to around 17.5%, thanks to pricing discipline, procurement efficiency and a richer mix of smart meters.

items.statement: C&I segment EBIT margins around 11%; expect similar margins until volumes scale significantly
items.quote: Right now, as I just said, we are seeing good movement, we are probably around 11% on EBIT basis. As volumes go up, maybe by FY27 or FY28, if the same momentum continues and we are able to make that happen, then we can work towards better margins.

items.statement: Most metering capex done; FY27 onwards mainly maintenance capex
items.quote: Right now, if you look at the medium-term capacities that we are expecting, I would say that most of the capex on the metering front is more or less done.

items.statement: C&I revenue mix: ~40% switchgear, ~40% wires & cables, ~20% lighting
items.quote: Roughly 40% is switchgear, 40% is cables, and about 20% is lighting. Fans are still small and can be clubbed within lighting for now.

items.statement: C&I segment targeting double-digit growth; aim to double C&I business in 3 years
items.quote: In three years' time, the ideal would be to double our C&I business. That is how we are looking at it. It's a strong vertical for us and a strong focus area.

items.statement: C&I revenue share expected to settle around 45% in H2 FY26
items.quote: Overall, metering could grow at a much faster pace because the uptake could be higher. But I think anywhere between 45–50% is where C&I should be.

items.statement: Debtor days ~125 including GST, improved 50-60 days vs March; inventory to reduce ₹50-60 crore in H2
items.quote: If you look at it including GST, it's about 125 days overall on debtor days, which is about 50–60 days better than March.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings up ~₹60 crore in H1 for capex; operating cash flows to reduce working capital borrowings
items.quote: There has been capex in the first six months and long-term borrowings have increased by about ₹60 crore. On working-capital borrowings, any additional realisations will go towards bringing short-term debt down.

items.statement: Strong manufacturing capacity; added automated machines for switchgear; wires & cables capacity expansion planned
items.quote: We have also added a lot of automated machines, especially on the switch side, over the last one–two years. That enhances quality, consistency and reduces human intervention, even in final testing.

items.statement: Supplying to almost all AMISPs; added 2 new AMISPs; order pipeline healthy with breakthroughs expected
items.quote: If you see my opening remarks, I did say that we are covering almost everybody now in the AMISP universe as a customer. Anybody who is there, big or small, we are somehow connected with them and we are supplying to them.

items.statement: Industry cumulative smart meter installations ~4.5 crore; run-rate 60-70 lakh/month
items.quote: The last figures in the public domain are about 4.5 crore smart meters already installed. So now at least some meaningful numbers are coming in, because we are already talking about double-digit implementation rates.

items.statement: Government extended 25-crore smart meter target to March 2028; ministry pushing AMISPs to speed implementation
items.quote: The government had earlier Transcribed by ElevEase 23 extended the deadline and this time I think there will be a much bigger push to adhere to it

items.statement: Execution challenges: skilled labour shortage for installations causing delays; some AMISP schedule postponements of 30-45 days
items.quote: My understanding is that, at times, meters and data are available but the requisite skilled manpower for installation is missing. That is my view; there could be other issues too.

items.statement: Copper prices volatile with 3 hikes in Sep-Oct; recently stabilising; global sourcing for electronic components
items.quote: Wires and cables still contribute a good chunk of the business and remain commoditised. There is a lot of play on copper prices. Only in the last two–three weeks we've seen some stabilisation; otherwise they've been volatile, with almost three price increases in September–October.

items.statement: Fans launched in exports (14 countries, international approvals); India launch from Dec, target 70-80% market coverage by June FY26
items.quote: In India, we have all the mandatory approvals, including for star rating. For the Indian market, we are looking at starting in December and then building up into June–July of FY26, which will be the first full season where we will participate.

items.statement: Havells settlement positive; no change to operating freedoms; consideration received by HPL group including promoter entities
items.quote: Overall, I think it's been very positive for both groups to set aside the dispute and move forward. I would say it has been positive for both sides.

items.statement: C&I growth above reported industry growth (EMA); market share still low with headroom
items.quote: Our growth in most segments is above reported industry growth (EMA figures etc.). If H2 comes in strong, we will put longer-term strategies in place to make this sustainable.

items.statement: Global sourcing for ICs, active/passive components, polycarbonate; procurement efficiencies in metering
items.quote: We are doing global sourcing for many items, ICs, active and passive electronic components, polycarbonate, etc. Wherever we get the best pricing and quality, we source from there.

items.statement: Metering orders structured over 2.5-3 years; bulk of ₹3,300 crore order book scheduled for FY27-FY28
items.quote: On the order book of about ₹3, 300 crore, normally any order we get is to be supplied over about 2.5–3 years. Many of the orders currently in our order book are actually scheduled for the end of this year, FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Q3 FY26 better than Q2; Q4 FY26 very strong based on confirmed AMISP delivery schedules
items.quote: Q3 is definitely going to be better than Q2, and Q4 should see much stronger growth. From our point of view, our teams are working to make sure that we are able to cover up the shortfall and then have growth as expected in the metering part.

items.statement: Consolidated margins healthy with room for efficiency-driven improvements; metering supply chain stable
items.quote: So, consolidated margins should remain healthy, with room for efficiency-driven improvements.

items.statement: No single state materially impacts order book; business aligned to AMISP customers not state-wise
items.quote: No particular state has such a large share that it can significantly impact our overall order book. Since ours is mainly a supply business to AMISPs, it is the AMISP that matters more than any single state.

items.statement: C&I strategy mainly traditional offline retail; builder projects strong; online focus for fans from Q4, then lighting/accessories
items.quote: Right now, our strategy is mainly traditional and offline. We address the market through the traditional retail channel. We have seen growth in terms of outlets or points of sale we are addressing, across all product lines.

items.statement: Brand investment ~2% of C&I sales in H1 FY26; stepping up in H2 FY26
items.quote: In the first half of FY26, we invested about 2% of C&I sales in advertising and promotion. We intend to step this up further in the second half of FY26, as we clearly see evidence that brand salience and distribution depth are translating into better-quality growth and pricing power over time.

items.statement: FY26 pump volume target 70,000-75,000 units
items.quote: Aditya Vora: Roughly 70,000 to 75,000 you are looking at? Gopal Rajaram Kabra: Yes.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to remain same or improve positively in FY26 and FY27
items.quote: And our EBITDA margin will remain same, or it is going to improve more positively. We are not looking towards any downside on the margins as well.

items.statement: Total order book INR 863.98 crores as of 30 Sep 2025 including 36,444 solar pumps worth INR 846.15 crores and 4 MW rooftop worth INR 17.83 crores
items.quote: Total order book, we are standing with 863.98 crores as on 30, September 2025.

items.statement: Magel Tyala-III empanelment tender for 1 lakh pumps submitted 13 Nov 2025; expect orders in Q3 FY26
items.quote: It is an empanelment for the 1 lakh pump.

items.statement: No slowdown expected in decentralized solar pump segment; demand remains aggressive
items.quote: But on the decentralized area where we are working, it is going more aggressive now. We are not looking towards any slowdown in the coming time.

items.statement: Current installation capacity 8,000-10,000 pumps per month; targeting 25-30% increase by April 2026
items.quote: We are targeting to increase around 25% to 30% capacity without stretch in comfort zone.

items.statement: 1 GW solar module line facility land acquired in Solapur, Maharashtra; work started; operational by Sep 2026 or earlier
items.quote: Yes. So, land acquisition is already done and the other things is in process. And it is a 1 gigawatt line definitely will be operational by the September 2026 or it will be before.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 20.20% vs 18.96% YoY; Q2 FY26 EBITDA margin 20.57% vs 19.83% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for H1 from business was INR 132.04 crores; it is basically 65.07% increase over INR 79.99 crores last year, with EBITDA margin expanding to 20.20% compared to 18.96% in H1 FY 2025.

items.statement: Input raw material prices decreased alongside selling prices; margins intact due to volume-based vendor negotiation
items.quote: See, definitely, I would not say pressure, price has been decreased, but input raw material price also has been decreased. So, price decreased and input raw material price also got decreased. So, ultimately, we GK Energy as the EPC player standing 100% with the intact margin what we have.

items.statement: Receivable days increased from 135 to 192 days (Sep 2024 to Sep 2025) due to monsoon delays, software integration, IPO work; expect normalization in Q3 FY26
items.quote: We have looked towards a little bit delay into the receivable from the previous time; it was 135 to 192 days in September 2024 to September 2025.

items.statement: Inventory turnover days increased from 31 to 55 days in H1 FY26 aligned with Q3 execution plan
items.quote: Our inventory turnover day increased from 31-days to 55-days in H1 FY26, and this increase was aligned with our execution plan as we are preparing to deliver and install significantly higher volume of the pump in Q3 2026.

items.statement: Debt primarily for working capital; interest rate 9% +/- 1%; net debt may increase in FY27 due to higher volumes
items.quote: See, debt is what we have, it is majorly for the working capital only. And the interest rates vary from the banker-to-banker, but in the range of 9% plus/minus 1% it will be there.

items.statement: Definitive agreement for procurement of 875 MW solar DCR cells for next financial year
items.quote: Furthermore, we are entering the definitive agreement procurement of 875 megawatt of solar DCR cell for the next financial year.

items.statement: Realization per pump varies by HP mix (3, 5, 7.5 HP); 3 HP volume increased lowering average realization
items.quote: It is about the mix of the 3, 5 and 7.5 HP. So, the little bit volume of 3 HP has been increased. So, 3 HP have the less price, 5 HP is more price and 7.5 HP is more price, right.

items.statement: Revenue share outside Maharashtra 10-15%; expanded presence in MP, UP, Rajasthan, Haryana
items.quote: It will be in the range of 10% to 15% outside Maharashtra.

items.statement: Asset-light pure-play EPC model protects margins vs integrated manufacturers; historic market share 15-18% per CRISIL
items.quote: See, number one thing, we are the asset light company. Number two, we are pure play EPC player.

items.statement: PM-KUSUM 2.0 opportunity expected not less than 3x previous scheme; industry belief based on government endorsement at ISA
items.quote: So, we are expecting a very good number and it is not less than 3x of the last PM-KUSUM what we have, this is what the industry believe I am having it.

items.statement: H1 FY26 installed 24,502 solar agri-pumps (+50.77% YoY); Q2 FY26 installed 13,675 pumps (+26.32% YoY)
items.quote: We have installed 24,502 solar Agri-pumps in H1 of '26. It is a 50.77% increase over the 16,251 pumps in the last year FY 2025 H1.

items.statement: H1 FY26 rooftop solar installed 1.24 MW; order book 4 MW (INR 17.83 crores)
items.quote: During the first half of FY2026, we have installed 1.24 megawatt of the rooftop capacity.

items.statement: Receivable delay risks from monsoon, software integration, IPO workload; AIIB USD 1.1bn funding to MSEDCL disbursement pending
