items.statement: Internal disclosure framework revised; 24-hour escalation protocol for statutory notices implemented
items.quote: Our internal disclosure framework has been comprehensively revised. And all department notices across compliance, finance and tax will now be evaluated strictly under Regulation 30. We have also implemented a mandatory 24-hour intra-department escalation protocol for all statutory notices.

items.statement: Share price down ~two-thirds from IPO; management acknowledges concern but focuses on execution
items.quote: We fully acknowledge that our share price has fallen from the IPO leve l and we understand the concerns this creates for our valued shareholders

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR 42.13 crores, YoY growth 36.59%; EBITDA INR 4.78 crores at 11% margin; PAT INR 3.46 crores at 8.21% margin
items.quote: Total revenue for H1 was INR 42,12,72,000. Total income for H1 was INR 43,45,19,000. A year-on-year growth of 36.59% and 40.7% respectively. EBITDA was INR 4,78,16,000 at an 11% margin. Net profit stood at INR 3,45,87,000 with a margin of 8.21%.

items.statement: Executive search expected to grow 15-20% YoY organically; new businesses to add growth over next 12-18 months
items.quote: On the executive search business, we have seen that we have delivered, even last year, we delivered about 15% growth on an organic basis. And we expect that trend to continue and actually improve.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target around 20% on steady state basis
items.quote: Kushal Parmar: Sure. It would be around 20%.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin 19.2%, up from 11.35% in H2 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the first half of the current fiscal year was around Rs. 8 crores with an EBITDA margin of 19.2%, which has sequentially grown from 11.35% in H2-2025, indicating cost optimization and efficiency gains.

items.statement: Next 18 months margins may be volatile due to investment phase in new businesses
items.quote: Yes, in the first half, for instance, though despite spending about Rs. 5.5 crore on new people investments, we were able to maintain our margins. So that would be a fair assumption. I think in 18 months on a steady state basis, we should be able to maintain those numbers.

items.statement: Spent Rs 5.25 cr on new employees in H1 FY26; expect similar scale of investment going forward
items.quote: The company has spent approximately Rs. 5.25 crores on new employees, which has been charged to the P&L in the first half.

items.statement: Will continue investing at similar scale for next 18 months to scale JD Professional and JD Global
items.quote: See, Kushal had mentioned earlier that we spent about close to Rs. 5.5 crores on the people front in the first half of the year. That was the investment. So you can assume that we will continue to make investments on that scale as we go forward.

items.statement: Signed 49 new clients in H1 FY26; robust pipeline for H2
items.quote: The number of new clients that have been signed up is 49.

items.statement: Executive search has 65% repeat business, 35% new clients; 30% annual churn
items.quote: See, every year there is a 30% churn. We have a 65% repeat business and 35% new clients. So the client signings are an ongoing process.

items.statement: Strong pipeline and deal throughput in executive search; healthy visibility for H2
items.quote: I think we have a good strong pipeline in terms of what we are seeing as the deal throughput in the executive search business. So, I can say that we have a healthy visibility in terms of the way the numbers are looking at this time.

items.statement: Target equal revenue split across three businesses (EMA Partners, JD Professional, JD Global) in 3-5 years
items.quote: I think we expect both professional JD, professional and JD Global to scale and have somewhat some sort of an even key between all the three businesses as we go forward. So you will see a distribution pretty much spread between search, professional search as well as the James Douglas Global business.

items.statement: JD Professional targets 20-25 employees by March 2026 across India and Dubai
items.quote: We expect to end the year for James Douglas Professional by March, we hope to have about at least 20 people on board, 20 to 25 people on board between both Dubai as well as India.

items.statement: JD Professional steady-state productivity Rs 90L-1Cr per employee per year; 18 months to full productivity
items.value: Rs. 90 lakhs to a crore per year
items.quote: But on an average basis, steady state basis, we expect that each employee should generate anywhere between Rs. 90 lakhs to a crore per year on a steady state basis. But we keep constantly adding people there until we achieve that steady state. So, we expect that business to scale rapidly in the next 18 to 24 months as we continue to add people there.

items.statement: JD Global leadership team in place; MatchCore AI platform launched; now in build-out and pitching phase
items.quote: So, the RPO size, we have the leadership team in place. So, typically in the RPO business, the scale-up happens in parallel to the projects. Okay, so that team has been in place for the last quarter. And if you see that in the last three months, we have actually launched our MatchCore platform, the technology platform, which has now got launched.

items.statement: Appointed investment banker to scout M&A opportunities in India in synergistic sectors; Rs 100 cr cash on books
items.quote: Yes. So as I mentioned earlier, we have appointed an investment banker. We are sitting on close to Rs. 100 crores of cash on the books. And we are evaluating potential opportunities which are in synergy.

items.statement: Three business lines now address new client segments beyond core executive search
items.quote: The fact now today that we have three begets in terms of businesses has given us more opportunity actually to add more clients. So we see that there is a robust pipeline of potential new clients and opportunities as we speak. Because we are also tapping into an entirely new set of client segments through the new businesses as well as our core business in executive search.

items.statement: JD Global differentiates via technology-first, AI-led MatchCore platform vs established RPO players
items.quote: So, here, as I said, our approach has been technology first and it will be technology-led platform, which is a distinct advantage for us as we compare ourselves to some of the other established players in the market.

items.statement: JD Professional addresses Rs 8,500-10,500 cr fragmented mid-senior hiring market (Ken Research)
items.quote: So, you will see that that is a Rs. 10,000 crore, Rs. 10,500 crore market opportunity or Rs. 8,500 crore market opportunity which we are looking to address. And that is a pretty much non-institutional fragmented market, which is what we are looking to address.

items.statement: Middle East margins compressed due to investment in JD business and leadership reshuffle
items.quote: The Middle East, if you see, we are also investing in building the James Douglas business in the Middle East. So, we are again in an investment phase. And we actually had a leadership reshuffle in James Douglas Middle East. And we are adding constantly, we are adding to our teams there. That is why you will see on an overall basis, the margins probably compressed.

items.statement: JD Professional employee productivity reaches Rs 90L-1Cr/year after 18 months gestation
items.quote: Yes, it is a fair assumption. And you should give about 18 months for an employee to reach full productivity.

items.statement: Targets 3,000 keys by FY28, adding ~1,000 keys per year
items.quote: Yes, 28, we are looking at 3,000 keys. You're very right, sir.

items.statement: Targets INR 550 crores revenue by 2029-30
items.quote: By the blessings of God and by all the support of my investors, I think our dreams will ensure that we go and reach the target what we have committed.

items.statement: Luxury Udaipur property acquired at INR 6.5 lakhs per key vs typical 30-40 lakhs
items.quote: But I have got a hotel which is at 6 lakhs per key for that luxury collection where I can charge more.

items.statement: Budget hotel renovation cost confirmed at INR 7.5-8 lakhs per room
items.quote: You're right, you're perfectly right.

items.statement: Will not pursue luxury projects costing over INR 9-10 lakhs per key
items.quote: Because if it is going to cost me anything more than 9-10 lakhs per room key, I'm going to be not going to go in for it as of now.

items.statement: Added ~400 keys from Feb 2025 to Sept 2025 (161 in H1, 223 in last 6 months)
items.quote: So, 161 keys were operationalized during the end of H1 and about 223 keys came into operation in the last six months.

items.statement: Two new properties confirmed for H2 FY26: Gurgaon and Vellore (by Feb-Mar 2026)
items.quote: Yes, we are still, we have two properties coming up. One in Gurgaon we are opening up and one in Vellore we have signed up which will go in the by February, March of 2026.

items.statement: Pilgrimage portfolio to grow from 128 to ~275 keys in 2026 with Varanasi, Somnath, Rameswaram
items.quote: So if you ask me, we have another 150 keys lined up for the pilgrimage center in this coming year, in this coming 2026.

items.statement: Corporate travel recovering steadily, domestic leisure demand strong, rising consumption favors branded mid-scale
items.quote: Corporate travel continues to recover steadily, domestic leisure demand is strong and India's rising consumption base continues to favor branded mid -scale

items.statement: November occupancy rocking, best month of the year; December picking up well
items.quote: November is rocking for us. It's doing really good. The numbers till date are also showing very, very positive on the top line. It's been one of the best months of this year for me.

items.statement: Mature business hotels stable at 31% EBITDA margin at unit level; overall EBITDA 20% due to leisure seasonality
items.quote: If you look at our mature business, our business hotels are very stable with a almost a 31% EBITDA margin which we have maintained at the unit level. We have been impacted due to seasonality in leisure hotels bringing down the overall EBITDA level to 20%.

items.statement: New hotels broke even at INR 11.6 cr revenue and INR 24 lakh EBITDA (381 keys)
items.value: INR 11.6 cr revenue, INR 24 lakh EBITDA
items.quote: So, if you see that our revenue from the new properties which was roughly 381 keys. It was about INR11.6 crores and our EBITDA is 24 lakhs. So, we have just broken even which means the costs remain the same.

items.statement: Lease cost 35-40% in first 1-2 months of new hotels, drops to ~25% as revenue picks up
items.quote: In these hotels, let us say that when we are having low occupancy, the leas e cost can go in the first one or two months to 35 % or 40%. Okay. And then from there, we d rop the cost drop to about 25% as the revenue picks up

items.statement: Targets stabilized revenue of INR 1 lakh per key
items.quote: So we look for a stabilized revenue of about 1 lakh per key. That is what we aim for in our hotels.

items.statement: Launching regional sales offices in Mumbai, Delhi/Gurgaon, Ahmedabad to drive corporate bookings
items.quote: We have started our regional sales offices in Mumbai and we have started our regional sales in Delhi, in Gurgaon also today. And very shortly, we are going to have regional sales person in Ahmedabad today.

items.statement: Funding next 1,600 keys via mix of internal accruals and debt; bankers supportive
items.quote: So, we feel we can do it from a mix of internal accruals and debt. We look at it like, let us say, a tranche-wise or a wave-wise of growth. We are ready and now with enough funds for the next set of keys that we have to launch.

items.statement: Strengthened corporate governance: hired COO (Oct 1), President Operations, full HR, procurement, IT teams for 50-75 hotel scale
items.quote: Now, we have recruited a COO in place. We have a President Operation in place. We have the full HR team in place today. We have a procurement department which has been set. We have started -- we have recruited an IT in place.

items.statement: Occupancy: new hotels ramped from 30% (Apr) to 70% (Sept); overall portfolio hitting 75-80% currently
items.quote: Today we are hitting also about 75% occupancy because it's a good business period at this point in time. So we are hitting 75% to 80% levels on today.

items.statement: Landlord rentals rising with industry boom; careful property selection needed to protect bottom line
items.quote: Today, as the industry is booming, what we are trying to earn, even the landowners have started understanding that there is a huge demand for buildings and they also started raising their rentals. So, we should be very careful in choosing it because that p lays a very important role in the bottom line of the company

items.statement: Incorporated wholly owned subsidiary in Delaware, US for long-term international alignment; no investment yet
items.quote: One of the most important strategic developments this year has been the incorporation of our wholly owned subsidiary in Delaware US Grand Continent Hotels Corporation. This is the beginning of a new chapter for us.

items.statement: Dubai: 1 property (123 keys) on franchise model, zero investment; testing for 6 months before expansion
items.quote: As far as the outside India properties are concerned as of now we have just one property which we have taken and that's a property in Dubai and 123 room key property. From that Grand Continent Hotels India has no t invested anything in the property. We are taking the property and a franchisee model where we are going to give them only our SOPs and our expertise in operating the hotel

items.statement: H1 FY26 consolidated: Revenue INR 58 cr, EBITDA INR 3.62 cr, PAT INR 2.11 cr (after minority interest)
items.value: Rev 58 cr, EBITDA 3.62 cr, PAT 2.11 cr
items.quote: So first with the result summary, we have done a top line of INR58 crores against INR41 crores in the last half year and we have a proximity of INR3.62 crores and a PAT of INR2.11 crores on consolidated level after minority interest.

items.statement: Management confirms pursuit of Rs. 220 crore revenue target for FY26
items.quote: Yes, that's the pursuit. My team is on.

items.statement: Management indicates margins in H2 FY26 should be similar to last three years and better than H1
items.quote: So, you can take the cue from the last three years. And yes, it should be in the similar lines.

items.statement: Current opportunity pipeline stands at Rs. 150 crore
items.quote: See, the overall team has participated currently with an opportunity worth of Rs. 150 crores in the marketplace right now.

items.statement: H1 FY26 EBITDA margin reported at 15.05%
items.quote: EBITDA came in at Rs. 16.69 crore with margin of 15.05%.

items.statement: Strong enterprise demand for cloud adoption, cyber security, and automation initiatives
items.quote: Demand from enterprise clients for cloud adoption, cyber security, and automation initiatives remained robust.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiary setup incurred one-time statutory costs in H1 FY26
items.quote: So, that is one reason of the previous question. Why the expenses have gone up is because of the overseas subsidiary expenditures as well.

items.statement: Plan to double consultant capacity in digital transformation, IBM technologies, and cyber security over next two years
items.quote: So, these are areas we are investing and we have to, our vision is to double capacities in the next two years' time by seeing the overall business outlook and we are bullish about it.

items.statement: Employee count increased from 160 in March 2025 to 175 in September 2025, with 25 more hires planned this year
items.quote: So, we should be around 175 people right now. And we are adding another 25 this year.

items.statement: Borrowings at Rs. 53 crore; no significant increase expected, may use invoice factoring for complex projects
items.quote: Not much. I think we are having good cash flow right now. I think we don't owe anybody much. So, yes.

items.statement: Medical automation product in oncology patient care management under development with AI partner trials ongoing
items.quote: So, the conversations are on. So, we are yet to finalize the AI partner for this technology for our product. So, currently, I think the conversations are on, the trials are on, work is in progress.

items.statement: Manufacturing sector adopting AI for smart factories; BFSI continues to lead digital transformation demand
items.quote: So digital transformation we are seeing in manufacturing. Yes, BFSI always leads. Their requirements are completely different. But what we are seeing is manufacturing adopting AI.

items.statement: Exploring partnerships with Israeli cyber security vendors for niche areas like drone and campus aerial security
items.quote: Yes. We are talking to a few cyber security vendors from Israel and these kind of areas. Well, that's what I said. You can expect some announcements very soon in niche areas.

items.statement: Plan to migrate from SME to main board listing within 18-24 months upon reaching Rs. 250 crore revenue
items.quote: Yes, that's the plan for the next 18 months to 24 months. That's what our pursuit is. So, once we reach the Rs. 250 crore mark, I think, yes.

items.statement: Employee benefit expense dropped from Rs. 8.41 crore to Rs. 3.12 crore due to reduced external consultant costs and in-house capability building
items.quote: And moreover, I think, as Sukanya well said, our execution costs have come down big time because we have built a framework within ourselves.

items.statement: Stock in trade/work in progress of Rs. 14.71 crore expected to close in H2 FY26 through milestone-based projects
items.quote: We hope to complete it this half year. There are multiple milestone-based projects that are in pipeline. And we expect it to close down in the H2, hopefully.

items.statement: Key operational challenge in international expansion is sourcing quality manpower requiring 18-24 months training investment
items.quote: See, operational challenge is getting quality manpower. That is for sure. With that reason, we are hiring and training people. Yes, those youngsters will get ready in 18 months, 24 months kind of a training.

items.statement: Management expects H2 FY26 performance to be as good as H1 or slightly better
items.quote: We are at the end of the second month of the third quarter. Okay? So, we are doing equally good and we hope to perform as good as the first half or even a little better.

items.statement: Total capex for YEIDA facility is Rs.184.16 crores; Rs.53.64 crores deployed in H1 FY26 (Rs.7.07 crores from IPO, Rs.46.57 crores from internal accruals)
items.quote: The total facility is approximately Rs.184.16 crores and we are going on the track and we are making the good progress. And we have incurred already Rs.46.57 crores through internal accruals and Rs.7.07 crores from IPO proceeds.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded to 26.98% in H1 FY26 from 20.22% in H1 FY25; management says expansion is sustainable due to high-margin product mix, operational efficiency, cost control and pricing strategy
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded significantly to 26.98% from 20.22% in the same period last year, reflecting improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management.

items.statement: Strong demand across all categories; domestic market contributed Rs.25.52 crores of incremental revenue; growth driven by new customers, new products and organic growth from existing customers
items.quote: Domestic market continue to be the key growth engine, contributing Rs.25.52 crores of the overall increase. Our growth was supported by the addition of new customers, addition of more products, and organic growth from existing customers.

items.statement: Business is sticky with no customer losses in decades; customers provide quarterly, half-yearly or annual schedules; new facility built under customer pressure for capacity
items.quote: Ours is a very sticky business. We are in the business of fragrances and flavors which are not the commodities. Our product becomes the identity of the end product and we are dealing with the best of the companies. In the last many decades of my business experience, touchwood, we have not lost any business.

items.statement: Raw material cost fluctuations managed through strategic sourcing and inventory management; benefits passed to customers to keep them competitive
items.quote: We at Sacheerome mitigate this through strategic sourcing and inventory management as I mentioned you earlier, and we will continue to do so effectively.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue split: fragrances Rs.75 crores, flavors Rs.1.46 crores; flavors expected to catch up in H2; dedicated flavor tower in new facility
items.quote: From the fragrances, we have generated around Rs.75 crores and the flavors we have generated Rs.1.46 crores. And the flavors segment which is a little sometimes seasonal and sometimes there is a demand, but we will be doing better than the previous year in the flavors also.

items.statement: Working capital cycle optimized to ~23 days from ~45 days previously
items.quote: One of the examples could be how we were able to optimize our working capital cycle as well which we have been able to operate at about 23-days compared to 45-days which we were doing in previous year.

items.statement: Term loan of Rs.60 crores from HDFC Bank secured for YEIDA facility; will be drawn after IPO proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: We have the term loan from HDFC Bank and we are fully covered. And, as per need base, we will withdraw... we will utilize the term loan. We will use the internal accruals and IPO first, then we will start using as and when required.

items.statement: Export market giving huge acceptance; Indian companies gaining global confidence; not taking share from global players but creating own space
items.quote: We will not say that we are taking away the business from our able competitors. We are creating our own space. Okay? And there is a much scope. Every day there are new launches of the new products, Indian products are doing so well, as well as we are looking at the export market also, which is also giving us a huge acceptance.

items.statement: Revenue grew 51.75% YoY to Rs.76.56 crores in H1 FY26; PAT Rs.14.94 crores
items.quote: We delivered robust revenue growth of 51.75%, with revenue from operations increasing to Rs.76.56 crores compared to Rs.50.45 crores in the same period last year, leading to an overall quantum increase of Rs.26.11 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization over 100% (above 95-97%); operational efficiency improvements and debottlenecking enabled volume growth despite constraints
items.quote: 760,000 is our current capacity. And, as you say, necessity is the mother of invention, we were under pressure and with our operational efficiency, we are able to produce all of our customer requirements.

items.statement: New facility revenue contribution expected from Q1 FY27; Q4 FY26 production start will be very small
items.quote: The last quarter will be the start of the production at our new facility. But let me tell you, they will start from there maybe, but it is very small, it will take some time, but at the same time, we will continue to maintain from our existing facility and there will be no loss of any business. From the first quarter of the next financial year, the revenue will start coming from the new facility a

items.statement: Management confident EBITDA margin of ~25% sustainable despite new capacity ramp-up; cites top-line growth, product mix, efficiency, cost control and pricing strategy
items.quote: As our top line grows, as our turnover grows, and which we are sure, I do not think it is a forward-looking statement, but I will say we are confident and we will be able to maintain our EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Margins higher than listed peers due to R&D innovation, qualified talent, quality products, regulatory compliance, deep customer relationships and proprietary technologies like Sach Veda
items.quote: Our competitive edge comes from a combination of R&D innovation, highly qualified human resources, high-quality standard products, regulatory compliance, and deep customer relationships. We provide tailor-made solutions aligned with consumer preferences, which help us to maintain the better profit margins.

items.statement: Multi-generational team with 40-45 years promoter experience; 54 R&D personnel; R&D is backbone of business
items.quote: I am in this industry myself for over 40-years, 45-years and I belong to third generation, Dhruv belongs to fourth generation, many people in our company are from second generation, their father was working, their son is working, their mother was working, their daughter is working. And it is like a family.

items.statement: Raw material supply risks (fire at BSF, COVID, China supply, climatic scarcity) managed through advance inventory planning and supplier relationships
items.quote: There are three turbulences we have faced, everybody in the industry, not only we. First of all, there was a fire in BSF, then there was COVID, then, China products, and sometimes, due to the climatic conditions, due to some reasons, there is scarcity. But, we plan our inventory very well and we plan in advance.

items.statement: Targets 25% CAGR revenue growth over next 3-4 years, aiming to double business size
items.quote: So, we have already given a guideline. So, we see the next 3 to 4 years, we are looking for double the size of the current business. So, with a 25% CAGR year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets 100 bps EBITDA margin improvement in short term
items.quote: So, madam, we are looking for a short term 100 basis point improvements in EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Consolidated H1 FY26 EBITDA margin at 8.62%, standalone at 9%
items.quote: EBITDA increased to 19.92 crores, it's up 13% H-on-H, so with the margin at 8.62%.

items.statement: IFM margins around 2-2.5%, hard services higher than soft services
items.quote: and other verticals also. So, if we compare the facility management business, the margins are thin in the facility business. And if we compare with the competitors, the margins come to around 2% to 2.5

items.statement: Converting clients from soft to hard services to improve margins
items.quote: Our plan is that only. And we have already initiated that step. And we have also converted few clients from soft services to hard services.

items.statement: Business pipeline over 1,200 crores provides strong visibility
items.quote: And our business pipeline of over 1,200 crores provides strong visibility for the upcoming quarter.

items.statement: Outsourcing penetration increasing across manufacturing, IT, ITES, retail sectors
items.quote: So, there are immense opportunity for the IFM services because in India, whether it is a manufacturing sector or maybe IT, ITES or maybe the retail sector, basically, they want to focus on their core activities.

items.statement: Entered pharmaceutical sector with good opportunity and expertise
items.quote: Apart from that, we have started in the pharmaceutical sector. So, there is a very good opportunity and we have the expertise to deliver as well.

items.statement: IFM contributes ~60% revenue, employee transportation and production support have better EBITDA margins
items.quote: So, if you see the mainly IFM business have a major revenue side that is the top line which contribute almost 60% of the business. And if we see the margin wise, it's employee transportation contributes better, that has contributed.

items.statement: Cross-selling adds revenue but margins remain same per service line
items.quote: So, margin enhancement for the cross-selling, it's like, definitely it will add, the margin will remain the same for the services we are offering, but revenue, definitely it will help on the top line.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute 50% revenue, but serve 140+ clients with pan-India multi-location contracts
items.quote: Yes, these clients are contributing first top 10 clients are contributing 50%. But apart from that, also, we have a clientele of almost 140 clients, like 50% contribution is from those clients.

items.statement: Key multi-service clients include Tata Motors, Volkswagen, JCB, Thermax across IFM, transport, food solutions
items.quote: Yes. So, for Tata Motors, we are giving the PAN India services for IFM and the employee transportation as well. Similarly, for Volkswagen facility management and the employee transportation services, these are the top clients.

items.statement: Employee transport capex only for 5-year exclusive contracts with back-to-back vehicle financing
items.quote: So, whenever there is a contract which has a 5 year duration and exclusivity with the clients, then only we invest in the vehicles and that will be have a back-to-back locking agreement for 5 years.

items.statement: Expanding geographic presence in North (Delhi NCR) and South (Chennai, Karnataka) manufacturing hubs
items.quote: So, if you see that in South region, so almost all the manufacturing industry is located in Chennai region. So, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, there we are focusing a lot of industry bases over there. And in the North region, the Delhi NCR, there we are focusing.

items.statement: New regions expected to contribute minimum 30% of future growth
items.quote: New region if you see that minimum 30% growth will come from the new region.

items.statement: Receivable days stable at 85-95 days due to MNC payment terms of 60-75 days post-invoice
items.quote: So, if you see, madam, the receivable days, it comes around 90 to 95 days, even in FY25 and current also. So, the receivables are coming into the 3 months, that is a cycle.

items.statement: Debt levels to remain at current levels even at 800-1,000 crore revenue scale
items.quote: So, when we close that business of 800 to 1,000 crores, the margins will improve and the debt levels will remain the same levels what we have at currently.

items.statement: Signed MoU for acquisition in South, acquisition not yet closed; evaluating more targets selectively
items.quote: So, no, Amit, we have just signed a MoU with them for acquisition. It's, acquisition has not been closed.

items.statement: Inorganic growth selective for geographic expansion or similar business segments
items.quote: So, the main expansion or improvements in business comes from organic. In that we are targeting the inorganic at a selective basis on the specific geographical expansion.

items.statement: Set up training division for skilled manpower sourcing and placement across pan-India network
items.quote: So, we have also set up a training division from where we are training people and placing them to our clients to give the quality of services.

items.statement: Client retention rate 85%, average client tenure 25 years with contract renewals
items.quote: I should say that we have an impressive 85% client retention rate. So, can I know, what initiatives are helping you to deepen the relationship and increase the wallet share within?

items.statement: Manpower cost 62-63% of revenue, rises proportionally with revenue in IFM business
items.quote: The manpower cost is directly related to our business because we are like in IFM business, which is mainly a manpower-oriented business. So, when the revenues increase, the manpower cost proportionately will get increased. So, it will rise into the similar percent of 62% to 63% of the total revenues.

items.statement: Long-term contracts enable year-on-year margin improvements
items.quote: So, if we have a contract constant for long-term, we definitely margin get year-on-year improvements.

items.statement: Clients shifting to single-vendor integrated contracts for admin and support services
items.quote: Yes, that was the trend like currently the market are shifting to single service provider for all the services. So, if you see the portfolio of services which we have, that is all related to the admin services and support services.

items.statement: Adopted Pazo technology platform for digital checklists, SAP workflows, automation and data-driven processes
items.quote: So, we have the Pazo technology which we have opted so far.

items.statement: Corporate food solutions expanding via in-house kitchen model (no capex) starting in West zone
items.quote: So, nowadays, like company has their in-house kitchen. So, we don't have to invest or set up a kitchen for them. So, they have their in-house kitchen. So, those opportunities we are trying to tap and wherever means we can expand that into the various regions in India. So, our focus basically first for this food solution is the west zone because that way our revenue is hardly 1.5 crores and all mon

items.statement: FY26 revenue guidance INR2,600-2,700 crore with PAT margin 11-12%
items.quote: FY ‘26, we keep a guidance of about INR2,600 crores to INR2,700 crores as a top-line guidance with a PAT margin of about 11% to 12

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR3,100-3,200 crore with PAT margin 11-12%
items.quote: For FY ‘27, which is next financial year, we keep a top-line target of about INR3,100 crores to INR3,200 crores with a PAT margin of again 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Total order book INR9,135 crore split energy INR5,869 crore and telecom INR3,266 crore
items.quote: So, as Rajeev was explaining, we have a total order book of INR9,135 crores, with the bifurcation of energy and telecom.

items.statement: Energy order book expected to increase by INR8,000-10,000 crore by end of FY26
items.quote: Going forward, we see our energy projects order book to increase by INR8,000 to INR10,000 crores before end of this financial year.

items.statement: Full year FY26 PAT margin expected to stabilize at 11.5%
items.quote: So, the current number of 13.61% will get stabilized at 11.5% for the complete financial year.

items.statement: Telecom product EBITDA margin 15-18%, EPC 13-14%; Energy product 15%, EPC 10-12%
items.quote: The telecom products has a n EBITDA margin of about 15% to 18%. The EPC has a margin of about 13% to 14%. And on the energy side, as we have started recently, the product margin is about 15%. EPC margin is about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Annuity O&M business EBITDA margin 80-85%
items.quote: So, these annuity business, the revenue, the EBITDA margin is about 85%, 80 to 85%.

items.statement: BESS facility expansion from 5 to 10 GWh requires additional INR100 crore capex
items.quote: Plus, for expansion of another 5 gigawatt hour, we need to spend another, say, INR100 crores more, because the fixed installations like the factory building is all common.

items.statement: IPO funds INR630 crore allocated for developer project, INR150 crore already spent from internal sources
items.quote: And we have already spent about INR150 crores, say, either from the debt sources or from the internal accruals for the project. The IPO funds, as it is, as it is received only in October, we are yet to spend from the IPO funds for this project.

items.statement: Current BESS orders 4.0-4.3 GWh, expected to cross 6-7 GWh by end FY26 and 10 GWh by facility commissioning
items.quote: So, at this point, we have orders for more than 4.0 to 4.3 gigawatt. And by end of this financial year, we are expecting orders to cross beyond 6 to 7 gigawatt.

items.statement: Strong demand for BESS from state discoms and central PSUs for EPC projects, private customers for product supply
items.quote: The projects that we're executing, which are EPC and developer projects, are usually state discoms or the public sector companies like the SECI or the NTPC, whereas we also have private customers where we only manufacture and supply our equipment.

items.statement: FY26 revenue mix: Energy INR500-550 crore, Telecom INR200-250 crore ICT, rest pure telecom
items.quote: And this year, we expect this energy segment to touch about INR500 to INR550 crores for this financial year, against a target of INR2,600 crores

items.statement: Won SECI BESS EPC INR1,159 crore, TTL O&M INR185 crore, MAHAGENCO solar EPC INR920 crore
items.quote: We have won three major projects, that include one project from SECI for battery energy storage system for INR1,159 crores for 600 /1,200 megawatt-hour battery energy storage system supply and installation, EPC project. We have also won a O&M contract with the telecom company TTL, Tata Teleservices, for INR185 crores for a period of three years. We have also recently won an EPC project for solar w

items.statement: Net working capital INR970 crore as of Sep 2025, expected to reduce by March 2026 as EPC projects complete and retention money releases
items.quote: So, the net current asset, we have about INR970 crores for this as on 30th September. So, which is expected to go down because of the project nature that we have, the EPC projects, which is at the verge of completion.

items.statement: Total debt INR150 crore, debt-equity 0.11x, net worth INR1,331 crore, cash/FD INR213 crore as of Sep 2025
items.quote: The debt, that is the company's debt, overall debt stands at about INR150 crores, and we have a debt equity ratio of about 0.11x. Again, the company has a net worth of about INR1,331 crores with a cash and FD balances of about INR213 crores.

items.statement: IPO proceeds received October 2025, INR630 crore for developer project equity, INR120 crore for two more projects
items.quote: So out of the INR820 crores of the IPO issue, INR630 crores goes for one specific project. So, beyond this, there are two more projects which are already signed off. There, we would be putting balance of IPO funds, which is about INR120 crores net of the issue expenses.

items.statement: Developer model 4 projects INR3,300 crore to yield INR420 crore annual revenue at 85% EBITDA from FY28, INR150 crore in FY27
items.quote: Four projects which we have as on date is about INR3,300 crores. This is expected to give an annual revenue of about INR420 crores without GST and EBITDA margin of a round 85%. So, with this, the next financial year, this particular number is going to come from FY28. But from FY27, we'll have a portion of it coming to the P&L.

items.statement: Annuity O&M order book INR3,300 crore yielding INR412 crore annual revenue, expected to grow to INR1,000 crore
items.quote: Yes. So, standing today, the order book that we have for this annuity business is about INR3,300 crores, which will give an overall top line of about INR412 crores every year. And this is expected to grow up to, say, INR1,000 crores in the upcoming years.

items.statement: Lithium-ion cells 50-60% of BESS cost, imported from China with back-to-back price locking; 5% customs duty vs 20% on finished goods
items.quote: So, the import content is the cell alone, which would – the battery cell alone will come to about 50% to 60% of the total cost. The remaining ancillaries are all manufactured in India, and we do the manufacturing and assembly here.

items.statement: MSEDCL project includes VGF of INR27 lakh per MWh paid in installments: 10% advance, 45% on commissioning, 45% over 3 years
items.quote: The developer model of this comes with a VGF of about 27 lakhs per megawatt hour, again. So, these are the components, I would say, if you want. I think I have answered your question. So, the VGF is like, say, it would be paid in different installments, like, say, 10% is paid on advance, 45% is paid on commissioning of the plant and the balance 45 % is paid over a period of three, next to three ye

items.statement: BESS competition increasing with infra companies bidding aggressively; PACE has cost advantage from in-house manufacturing and backward integration
items.quote: There is huge demand and huge competition that has started coming in over the last two, three months now. And there is a lot of infra and other types of companies coming in to bid for such projects. But as PACE, we have an advantage where we have the control of the product.

items.statement: Recent BESS tenders bidding below INR2 lakh/MW/month seen as unsustainable, expected to correct in coming months
items.quote: But we see that that numbers are closer to impossible and because of which this will go through a correction over the next few months.

items.statement: Kenya and Africa expansion driven by telecom infrastructure growth, supplying power equipment and hybrid solutions
items.quote: Kenya and Africa in the last few years have invested a lot in the telecom industry and have expanded a lot in the telecom industry. So, we see a big need and we've been working in the past few years, in expanding the telecom side, providing our power equipments, doing the supply and installation of our power equipment and the hybrid solutions.

items.statement: Workforce 1,500+ on-roll and 1,500+ off-roll employees across India
items.quote: We have a strong workforce of 1,500 -plus people across India on roll and more than 1,500 off roll.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of minimum 15% year-on-year; FY27 revenue target around INR300 crores
items.quote: So, FY '27, probably, we have -- as we have already given some targets, like 15% year-on-year growth minimum. And CAGR, it was. So, we will be probably around 300 or around that line.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 10% for full FY26; expects further improvement in FY27
items.quote: Yes, yes. We would be able to. This was just lowered down due to we have been shifting our pultrusion process from rented to the new premises. So, it affected our operational efficiency somewhat and the revenue also. Also, the US part somewhat was affected. So, ultimately, H2 would be much more better than the H1.

items.statement: Carbon fiber project machinery investment between INR8-10 crores; rebar five lines capex approximately INR7.5 crores including bend machines
items.quote: So, on the carbon fiber side, probably our i nvestment is going to be between INR8 crores to INR10 crores This is only machineries and then there are other ancillaries and all that

items.statement: New Mehsana facility 51,671 sq m operational end of Sep 2025; full 22,000 metric tons capacity over next few quarters; targeting over 70% utilization by FY27
items.quote: The unit has become operational at the end of September 25 and is currently in the scale-up phase with full 22,000 metrics and capacity expected to be achieved over the next few quarters.

items.statement: FRP rebar: 2 lines installed, scaling to 5 lines by end FY26; each line ~300 MT/year generating INR5-7 crores
items.quote: So, each machine has a capacity of approximately 300 metric tons a year and that would generate approximately anywhere between, depends on the diameter, but it will generate probably around INR5 to INR6 crores. Between INR5 to INR7 crores, I would say, depends on the diameter per machine.

items.statement: Carbon fiber pilot plant expected installed capacity by end FY26; approvals 8-12 months; full scale-up FY28
items.quote: We are hoping that by end FY26, we have the installed capacity for carbon fiber product. And going forward, all these carbon fiber is more technical product and the approval is also there. So, we will start approval process and as we go forward with approvals, we can add on capacities in carbon fiber as well.

items.statement: Current order book INR45 crores, executable in FY26
items.quote: So, there is no bifurcation right now with respect to customized or not, but our current order book is INR45 crores.

items.statement: FRP rebar and carbon fiber margins projected at least 4% higher than existing business; carbon fiber higher than rebar
items.quote: I think the margins are higher, at least by -- this is what our projected are, by 4% than our existing line of business, at least by 4%.

items.statement: Pricing flattish in H1; some specialty chemical raw material volatility; potential domestic price increase if anti-dumping duty on glass fiber imposed
items.quote: So, the pricing is more of a flattish right now. There are certain raw materials which are specialty chemicals has been little bit volatile. But overall, the international global scenario has been flattish with respect to price of FRP products and with respect to the raw material of the major raw materials.

items.statement: FRP rebar market acceptance growing fast; government promotion by MoRTH/NHAI; customers adopt gradually per project
items.quote: Market has been receptive with respect to FRP rebar. It's been almost just two years since the government has started promoting this product and started accepting this product. And the feedback from the market is also very positive.

items.statement: Key rebar clients: Shaligram (Ahmedabad developers), IRB (highways), L&T; optic fiber rods to Apar Industries, KEC, OFS/Furukawa; EPC contractors and end-users across sectors
items.quote: In Ahmedabad, there are a few developers. One of the big names is Shaligram. And then, on highways, IRB, we are already supplying in IRB. I think that is a good, big enough name to address the highway developers. We are also supplying to L&T.

items.statement: FRP rebar competitors: Jindal Advanced Materials (JSW group) and Rathi Steel (Delhi) with ~10+ machines combined; Aeron to be among few large manufacturers with 5 lines
items.quote: One is Jindal Advanced Material, which is a JSW group company. then there is Rathi Steel, they are based in Delhi. I t hink these two have good enough capabilities right now at this point. There are other manufacturers as well with one machines or two machines, but these two are having good capabilities. And probably with our five lines, we will be among the few large manufacturers

items.statement: MoRTH/NHAI promoting FRP rebar adoption; guidelines issued encouraging use; anti-dumping duty hearing on glass fiber products may raise domestic raw material prices
items.quote: This is further supported by growing regulatory momentum, most notably the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways under Mr. Nitin Gadkari and NHAI, which has actively promoted the adoption of FRP rebar and issued guidelines encouraging its use.

items.statement: Exports 55% of H1 revenue (down from 61% due to plant shift); supplying to 39 countries; Western countries stronger demand; USD/INR at 89
items.quote: Export revenue contributed 55% of the total revenue during the first half, underscoring the strength of our international presence and brand acceptance.

items.statement: Receivables typically 60-90 days; >6 months receivables increased FY24 to FY25 but improving in H2 FY26
items.quote: Generally, it is between 60 to 90 days in general.

items.statement: Long-term debt for buildings; short-term working capital ~INR25 crores; cash ~INR40 crores from IPO proceeds; no plan to prepay long-term debt with IPO cash
items.quote: Long term, which is our debt for the term loans we have taken from the bank, which is for current buildings, which we have achieved right now for pultrusion and molded. And short terms will be around INR25 crores, which is plus minus according to the utilization of the working capital.

items.statement: IPO proceeds INR53 crores; total gross block after full implementation ~INR110-120 crores including term loans and internal accruals
items.quote: So overall, if we talk about our gross block in total with whole implementation, let's say total term loan plus our internal accruals would be INR33 crores, our gross block till '25, it was INR35 crore s and INR53 crore s of total of IPO proceedings. So overall, it would go around INR110 crores or INR20 crores total gross block after complete implementation

items.statement: FRP rebar NSR assumption INR140/kg; each rebar line ~300 MT/year at INR5-7 crores revenue
items.quote: Right now, we are taking INR140 a kg.

items.statement: US tariff uncertainty affecting exports; mitigation via new non-US customers if deal fails; carbon fiber approvals 8-12 months delay revenue
items.quote: Meanwhile, if the tariff, the deal does not get through, then we are, of course, we have already started to talk to outside US customers to improve their offtake from us, basically. And we are -- we will be adding new customers to offset that loss of revenue in that case, in the tariff deal…

items.statement: Integrated 360-degree FRP provider: pultruded profiles, molded grating, UV-cured FRP rods, CFRP rebars; adding carbon fiber pultrusion (wind blades, HTLS core rods) and autoclave (auto, rail, defense)
items.quote: These high -performance, high -margin composites aimed at sectors such as wind energy, railways and automo tive represent the next step in broadening our advanced material portfolio

items.statement: Rent savings ~INR32 lakhs/month (INR36 lakhs with GST) from owned Mehsana plant; additional INR10 lakhs/month plant installation cost savings; depreciation and interest to offset
items.quote: So we'll be saving a rent per month of approximately INR32 lakhs. With GST, it becomes INR36 lakhs. So that is per month basis. And then we are projecting that our efficiencies in terms of material handling and reducing the wastage will also improve.

items.statement: Trade receivables >6 months increased FY24 to FY25 (INR1.9 cr to ~INR4 cr); management states improving in H2 FY26
items.quote: Mainly in this year, we are improving that. And in this H2 also, it would be improving. So we are surely on the improvisation stage right now.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue INR116.7 crores; EBITDA INR8.7 crores (7.5% margin); PAT INR7.2 crores
items.value: INR116.7 cr; INR8.7 cr; 7.5%; INR7.2 cr
items.quote: Revenue from operations stood at INR116.7 crores, showcasing steady growth. EBITDA for the period was INR8.7 crores with a margin of 7.5%, while P AT comes in at INR7.2 crores

items.statement: Revenue guidance for FY26 is Rs. 110-120 crores, tracking in line with projections
items.quote: So, our revenue guidance is in line and our performance is in line with the revenue guidance that we gave. So, we are tracking those numbers and we are confident that we will touch the Rs. 110-Rs. 120 crores mark by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins typically 25-30%, PAT margins 17-20%; Q2 FY26 higher due to one good order execution
items.quote: So, see, generally, our margins are in the range of like EBITDA, you can expect anywhere between 25%-30% and the PAT remains anywhere between 17%-20%. And on an average, that has been our consistent performance.

items.statement: Order book similar to March levels; executing long-lasting orders supporting Q4 FY26 predictions
items.quote: So, it is the same pattern that we are talking. The orders are long-lasting orders. So, that is how we are predicting our quarter 4 numbers.

items.statement: BOOT project payback period 3-4 years; client invests 20-30% equity; BOOT includes O&M revenue stream
items.quote: And the payback period is generally 3-4 years and it comes along with, any BOOT project that we do has to be compulsorily coming along with an O&M service also.

items.statement: EPC working capital cycle 6-8 months with 10% advance; BOOT invoicing 45-60 days; higher inventory for O&M spares
items.quote: So, in EPC, generally, the cycle would be turnaround and the entire cycle will move in 6-7 months kind of a period when you from procure to direct, getting all the payments done, 7-8 months would be gone in that process.

items.statement: Capital not a constraint for current order book; funded via equity, debt, internal accruals; good bank lines available
items.quote: As of now, we don't see any constraint for the order book that we currently have. We do not see any capital constraint as of now, or the bank or debt constraint.

items.statement: Oman Phase-II deferred to next year; focusing on growing revenues at existing facility month-on-month
items.quote: So, Phase-II is something which we will take up not at this moment, maybe in the next year, because we are now growing the revenues for the Oman facility and that is showing improvement month-on-month.

items.statement: Revenue split ~35-40% O&M, balance EPC; FY26 EPC contribution higher due to large EPC projects under execution
items.quote: Operation and Maintenance still contributes almost as of now, we can say 40% of the turnover till the current numbers that we have 35%-40%. And the balance comes from the EPC.

items.statement: EPC EBITDA 15-20%, BOOT/O&M EBITDA 20-25%; blended margins maintained at 25-30% EBITDA
items.quote: EPC is about 15%-20% again with a lot of dynamics. But yes, EPC attracts lower EBITDA and the O&M attracts the higher EBITDA.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expectation Rs. 180-200 crores driven by O&M ramp-up from current year project executions
items.quote: But this is what our expectation is that we will touch FY '27 anywhere around Rs. 180-Rs. 200 crores. Because the projects that are getting executed in this current year will start generating O&M revenue from April-May next year.

items.statement: FY26 EPC project value ~Rs. 60-70 crores out of Rs. 110-120 crore revenue target; BOOT proportion lower this year
items.quote: EPC would be somewhere around what we can say, just give me a second, EPC would be somewhere around Rs. 60-Rs. 70 crores. That would be roughly the number this year.

items.statement: Plastic recycling revenue expected Rs. 3-5 crore/month with 5-10% margins plus EPR credits; commercial production in FY26
items.quote: You can reasonably expect anywhere between Rs. 3-Rs. 5 crores of revenue per month from those because it is a fast processing. It doesn't take so much time and it is a fast moving production item. And anywhere between 5%-10% would be the kind of margin that we can expect.

items.statement: Metal recovery from hazardous waste targeting 99.9% purity copper/zinc; revenue not before FY27-28; technology developed, partners identified
items.quote: From the metal part of it, we don't see anything happening before even the plant setup and everything will go up to the end of next Financial Year or something prior to that. So, it may not be something before Financial Year '27-28.

items.statement: Other income of Rs. 6 crore in FY25 was one-time; current year other income nominal
items.quote: No, that was one time. But this year, if you see the other income figure is very nominal. So, it is very nominal and that was onetime kind of a thing.

items.statement: Warrant forfeiture proceeds credited to capital reserve, not P&L; balance sheet adjustment only
items.quote: That has been credited to, I think, the capital reserve, means it has been credited to capital reserve. Hiral Nandu: Is it an income part this quarter or? Nishant Sharma: It is not reflected in your P&L. It is an adjustment to the

items.statement: Order acquisition through word-of-mouth, peer references, tenders; not aggressive sales; orders typically Rs. 5-20 crore
items.quote: So, it is more of a word of mouth publicity that has happened over a period of time. And see, there are a lot of tenders that come in the market. We do those bidding and all those things also.

items.statement: FY27 expected to be better than FY26; team starting new order bidding in January or September
items.quote: I see FY '27 to be better than FY '26. And of course, FY '26 is better than FY '25. As far as the order books or commitments are concerned, we have seen some work. But yes, our team will be starting or maybe in January or September.

items.statement: ROCE target 18-20% on invested capital across both EPC and BOOT models
items.quote: So, generally, what we try to achieve is around 18%-20% is the ROCE that we expect to achieve on the investment or the capital that is employed.

items.statement: Oil processing capacity 100 tons/day across Gujarat and Oman facilities; 34,260 sqm production area; 485 employees
items.quote: Felix's oil processing plants have a capacity of 100 tons per day, supported by robust infrastructure in India and Oman, handling the entire life cycle from collection to its refining.

items.statement: Key projects: 3,500 KLD WIP at Pharma SEZ, 1,000 KLD dairy system, 1,050 KLD WIP for oil & gas, upcoming 4,000 KLD multi-sector ZLD CETP
items.quote: To name a few key projects include a 3,500-KLD WIP plant at Pharma SEZ, a 1,000-KLD system for a dairy producer, 1,050-KLD WIP unit for leading oil and gas companies, and an upcoming 4,000-KLD multi-sectorial mixed-effluent ZLD plant CETP.

items.statement: Plastic recycling acquiring existing facilities in Surat, Baroda, Ahmedabad; test batches produced virgin-quality granules from milk pouches
items.quote: Same way, on the plastic waste cycling, there are already 2-3 units that are in operation, in Surat, Baroda and one in Ahmedabad. So, we are not going directly as a new player in the market. We are acquiring those entities and we have already produced as a test batch in those facilities, certain virgin plastic materials which can be used by different industries from the waste like our milk pouches

items.statement: Steel sector order: Rs. 1.43 crore EPC for 75 KLD ZLD; O&M to commence after installation
items.quote: This is a Steel Contract on an EPC basis, and Operation & Maintenance will commence after the plant installation

items.statement: Rivita Solutions (Oman) has O&M contracts: Rs. 2.2 crore, Rs. 1.87 crore, Rs. 1.9 crore for 3-year oil & gas operations
items.quote: So, these are all contracts from oil and gas. These are related to this Rivita. These are orders where we would be doing, these are revenues from Operation and Maintenance only. These 2.2 and 1.9 and 1.87.

items.statement: Aiwasun heat pump and Rosoft home water purification are consumer products separate from core EPC/O&M business
items.quote: Rosoft and Aiwasun are both home-use technologies offered by Felix. Rosoft provides a complete process for delivering clean, safe, and potable water for household use. Aiwasun is a heat pump system that supplies hot or cold water based on the surrounding air temperature.

items.statement: BOOT projects only with financially strong counterparties; EPC preferred for smaller/weaker clients to mitigate counterparty risk
items.quote: All BOOT projects are fundamentally, one thing is clear, the counterparty has to be strong enough so that we can take a risk on that party for the amount that we are investing. So, BOOT projects are only undertaken for very reputed or strong and financially very strong companies.

items.statement: H1 FY26 revenue dropped due to prolonged heavy monsoon delaying harvest cycle and GST changes pushing sales to later months; expects YoY growth in H2 and full year
items.quote: As we all know that monsoon in this year has been really long and it was heavy which pushed the you know the harvesting cycle a bit farther and the sales got a bit delayed and we are very positive that in the second half of the year we will do great business and we will definitely show growth on year-on-year basis

items.statement: Cannot commit exact numbers but expects increasing turnover in coming years with growth visible from FY26
items.quote: I can't like commit any exact numbers to you right now but the total figures will be in an like in an increasing order and it will be start like you will be able to see the results from this year only

items.statement: Capex for new manufacturing facility on track; shed construction and machine orders underway
items.quote: Yes, it's on track. It's not such it's delayed. We have already started like the shed like the construction shed material manufacturing sheds construction and it's underway and the machines orders are underway and everything is going smoothly

items.statement: New capex will add two manufacturing lines with ~300 harvesters annual capacity per line; expects commissioning impact from next financial year
items.quote: So with this the manufacturing line that we will manufacture that that we will be we will set up we will be having around 300 harvesters of manufacturing capacity with just one manufacturing line. So we will be having two manufacturing lines

items.statement: Targets selling up to 1,000 harvesters in 4-5 years using current capex; thresher volumes to grow nominally
items.quote: our target is go up to thousand harvesters in numbers like in the coming four to five years we will definitely achieve that with this much capex and everything only

items.statement: Operating margin rose to 22% due to harvester mix (local manufacturing vs imported Chinese units) and lower raw material costs; expects margins to increase further
items.quote: So the margins that went up because they were primarily because of two reasons. The first is because of the introduction to harvesters because harvesters we have a good like operating margin in that product

items.statement: Harvester revenue share expected to reach 50-60% in a couple of years from current lower base
items.quote: we are expecting to go around 50- 60% of sales in harvester in a couple of years

items.statement: Harvesters use Eicher engine, JCB hydraulic parts, Eicher tractor electronics; only rubber track and clear box imported from China; plans to localize in 2-3 years
items.quote: all the mechanical parts and all the machinery parts we are manufacturing by ourselves except from the engine we buy it from Eicher company and there is just one there a couple of things that we import from China.One is rubber track which the harvester used to crawl on and the second is the clear box

items.statement: Dealer network expanded in Bengal; exclusive dealer agreements for threshers; count was 49 in FY25 but exact current number not recalled
items.quote: we have definitely expanded this year in Bengal state. So I need to double check this because I don't know the exact numbers right now. But yeah, we must have like added some more dealers this year

items.statement: No listed Indian competitor in harvesters; Chinese imports are main competition; thresher market fragmented with local manufacturers in every state
items.quote: if you talk about Indian make harvesters, we have we don't have any competition if you talk about the general harvester markets in India then yes Chinese, Chinese brands are definitely our comp competitors

items.statement: GST implication this year pushed sales to later months compared to normal monsoon year
items.quote: the impact of the GST implication which the government came up with, which also pushed our sales a little bit like in the later months rather than in the earlier months

items.statement: Promoter open to considering share buyback given current share price below IPO level
items.quote: we will definitely consider consider the option. Nishant Gupta: Okay. Kamaljeet Singh Kalsi: Yeah, I know that the share price has gone like we know what the track of the share price is and yeah, we will definitely consider this option as well

items.statement: Mahindra co-branding contract for threshers renewed every two years; relationship expected to continue either directly or through Mahindra
items.quote: the Mahindra contract is renewed after every two years. It's not a like a 10 years contract. Every two years they renew the contract and we keep going working with them

items.statement: Harvester price point 25-26 lakh rupees with ~20 lakh average finance amount; financing through government banks (SBI, Canara, BOB, RRBs) not NBFCs due to high rates
items.quote: harvester is basically 25 to 26 lakh rupees like it costs 25 - 26 lakhs and on an average basis 20 lakh rupees is the finance amount that a farmer needs

items.statement: Seasonal concentration risk: sales concentrated in few months when monsoon harsh; harvester multi-crop use (paddy, wheat, maize) expected to enable year-round sales
items.quote: when the monsoon is a bit harsh on some areas then the harvesting cycle becomes really small like the timeline becomes really small and each states come up with the harvesting cycle at the same time. So our sales get concentrated in a couple of months

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 350 crores with INR 650 crores pipeline
items.quote: To highlight, currently, our order book stands at INR350 crores and the order pipeline of INR650 crores.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of 35% year-on-year for next couple of years
items.quote: we look to grow at around 35% for next couple of years

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to be upwards of previous year levels
items.quote: Margins will be upwards of what we are achieving or what we've achieved even last year.

items.statement: Design-build projects have better margins than pure contracting projects
items.quote: Design-built project definitely has a better margin as compared to the only contracting project.

items.statement: Healthy traction across domestic and international markets with robust order pipeline
items.quote: We continue to see healthy traction across both domestic and international markets. The order pipeline in our core vertical remains robust.

items.statement: Proposed acquisition of Krew Instruments to enter healthcare infrastructure segment
items.quote: With our proposed acquisition of Krew, we are laying the foundation for a multiyear growth opportunity.

items.statement: 85% of revenues from exports, 15% domestic; export orders 75-80% of order book
items.quote: As of date, when we speak, 85% of our revenues are from export, actually. And 15% from domestic businesses.

items.statement: Design-build projects expected to be 15-20% of revenue mix going forward
items.quote: In going ahead, you can see the increase in the number for the design-built project.

items.statement: Targets 30% Oil capacity utilization in H2 FY26
items.quote: I think next financial year, H2 will be utilized almost 30% easily. We can reach up to 30%.

items.statement: Demand environment encouraging; confident of sustaining growth momentum in H2
items.quote: The demand environment continues to be encouraging and we are confident of sustaining the growth momentum in the second half.

items.statement: Expanded modern trade presence: 40 KPN stores, DMart online Hyderabad, Big Basket Telangana/AP, 29 Ushodaya, 13 Balaji Grand Bazaar, Vijetha, Qmart stores
items.quote: Our recent placement across 40 KPN stores has further strengthened our modern trade footprint.

items.statement: No competition in pure groundnut oil segment; only two brands maintain pure oil
items.quote: No, there is no competition at all in the groundnut oil segment. The pure brand is only. Two brands are maintaining the pure oil rather than all brand only.

items.statement: Pooja products market 95% unorganized; no organized player with full portfolio; sees first-mover advantage
items.quote: This product is actually, 95% market is unorganized. So, we have a very good potential and growth and margins in that. So, no other brand in India is focusing fully on this.

items.statement: Atta 1kg B2B pricing ~Rs. 47; 90% revenue from 1kg, 5kg, 10kg packs
items.quote: Around Rs. 47. Subhanu: Yes. Narayan Das Rathi: That is for B2B actually. That is not for the consumer

items.statement: Advertising spend Rs. 5-6 lakhs monthly on regional TV channels; annual target below 1% of revenue
items.quote: Altogether monthly we are spending Rs. 5-Rs. 6 lakhs on the media channels, new media channels.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased due to OD on last day of September
items.quote: Actually, mainly there was one OD came on the last day of September. So, that contributed so much towards short-term borrowings.

items.statement: No equity raise planned; will use debt from bankers if needed for expansion
items.quote: We will be going for the debt as of now. If we need exactly, we will go for the debts of the bankers.

items.statement: Export market expansion planned for FY27 targeting Middle East, Singapore, US
items.quote: Definitely. But in FY '27. Next year, we will plan for the expansion. Next year, we are into the planning for that.

items.statement: H1 FY26: Revenue Rs. 78.77 cr, EBITDA Rs. 13.43 cr, PAT Rs. 7.20 cr; YoY revenue growth 49.08%, PAT growth 46.66%
items.quote: Revenue stood at Rs. 78.77 crores, EBITDA at Rs. 13.43 crore and PAT at Rs. 7.20 crore. Our profitability remained healthy with EBITDA margin of 17.05% and PAT margin of 9.14%. On a Y-o-Y basis, revenue grew by 49.08% while PAT increased by 46.66% compared to H1 FY '25.

items.statement: Geographical expansion challenging due to established brands, high placement time and advertising costs; prefers portfolio expansion in home states
items.quote: Because brands have already acquired 42 from last 25, 30, 40 years. So, it will take a lot of time for the placement also. And second thing is, we have to put a lot of budget on the advertisement, if you go for the new state.

items.statement: Sold Srivari Supply Chain (Paushtik brand); no longer wholly owned subsidiary
items.quote: Regarding Paushtik, as we have already informed, and even in the AGM also it was discussed, we have totally sold Srivari supply chain. It is no more connected to Srivari.

items.statement: Awarded Excellence in FMCG Spices Brand at ET Excellence Awards 2025; featured in Forbes India August 2025
items.quote: We are also pleased to share that the company was honored with the excellence in FMCG Spices brand award at ET Excellence Awards 2025 in Telangana. Additionally, our Srivari Spices portfolio was featured in Forbes India in August 2025 edition.

items.statement: Expects reasonably good revenue numbers by year-end, not necessarily surpassing prior levels
items.quote: by this year end, we will be, I think, if no t surpassing, but we will be doing reasonably good a s far as revenue is concerned, revenue numbers are concerned in current year

items.statement: EBITDA margins declined due to heavy investment in IP creation and upskilling; expects similar EBITDA to last year while building asset value
items.quote: this year we might have a similar EBITDA like last year, but creating this value proposition will also result into extraordinary valuation like what we got in DevX.

items.statement: Plans to invest Rs. 12-18 crore over next 12-24 months on AI, blockchain, cybersecurity R&D and center of excellence
items.quote: all in all, around 12 crores to 18 crores is what we are expecting to invest for R&D or for a center of excellence creation.

items.statement: Current order book provides visibility of Rs. 130-140 crore for FY26, with Rs. 30-38 crore continuing into FY27; expects Rs. 25-28 crore new orders in next four months
items.quote: our current order book is around 40% of our total revenue. So, if I add my current order book, so I have a visibility of around Rs. 130 crores to Rs. 140 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: FY27 order book visibility at Rs. 38-45 crore including expected new orders
items.quote: for order book is concerned for FY '27 is around Rs. 38 crores to Rs. 45 crores including what we are going to receive order in next four months.

items.statement: Recurring revenue ~60% from annual contract renewals (80%+ renewal rate), 40% new business
items.quote: you can say 60% are recurring business and 40% are new business.

items.statement: Facing pricing pressure in all markets; North America payment terms extending from 30 to 45-60 days; India is price-conscious but predictable
items.quote: pricing pressure, we are definitely facing not only in India market, but also in North America market. Everywhere, pricing pressure as well as payment pressure are there.

items.statement: New labor code cost impact not yet quantified; majority of contracts have government regulatory increment clauses covering cost pass-through
items.quote: That's really not been done remotely. So, I cannot predict any number right now.

items.statement: Secured new strategic projects from RajCOMP, Gujarat Informatics, Gujarat Info Petro, NICSI in e-governance, cloud migration, financial management
items.quote: We secured ne w strategic projects from RajCOMP , Gujarat Informatics Limited, Gujarat Info Petro, NICSI across enterprise software development, and that too in e-governance ecosystem

items.statement: Targeting $1-3 million US e-governance business via Dhyey partnership in FY27; seeing strong Canada traction in ERP and cybersecurity; planning direct Australia presence next year
items.quote: our target is also said that at least $1 to $3 million of business will be done in FY '26-'27.

items.statement: International margins materially stronger than domestic due to exchange rate and lower delivery cost
items.quote: international market, because of exchange and because of our service delivery cost is low, margins are obviously high in export business.

items.statement: Preferential warrant proceeds to fund acquisition of non-India company or physical presence in North America/Europe/Australia
items.quote: those money will be utilizing for acquiring a local non-India based company, mainly into North America or Europe or in Australia, but mainly in North America.

items.statement: Talligence 2.0 AI/ML blockchain product ready; 4-5 serious partners enlisted and selling; targets 10% of 4 crore Tally users by 2028
items.quote: Our target is to achieve, if not 100%, but to achieve 10% of Tally, this 4 crore user by 2028.

items.statement: Cybersecurity business unit grew from launch; expects revenue to grow from $500k to $2 million by next financial year-end
items.quote: we see that business growing from $500,000 to $2 million in next financial yearend.

items.statement: Blockchain IP under Minddeft nearing launch; building citizen document verification solution for government bodies at POC stage
items.quote: We are building one of the unique blockchain -based solutions for India market, which will definitely solve lots of hassle for every citizen of this country.

items.statement: DevX expanding from 28 to 35-40 co-working centers, focusing on tier-2 cities; adding 2 centers each in Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Rajkot, Surat
items.quote: currently, they ar e having 28 locations. And very soon, they will be reaching to around 35 - to 40-odd co-working spaces in different parts of India.

items.statement: Subsidiary revenue (Dhyey + Minddeft) ~Rs. 25 crore; expects Dhyey to at least double in next couple of years; Minddeft building blockchain products for annuity revenue
items.quote: in our consolidated balance sheet, it's around Rs. 25 crores of revenue coming from two subsidiaries, mainly Dhyey and Minddeft.

items.statement: Rolled out ESOP program reflecting confidence in future and belief in building employee wealth through asset valuation
items.quote: Our ESOP program rolled out this quarter as well reflected our confidence in the future and our belief in building wealth for employees who are part of our journey.

items.statement: Dev Accelerator (DevX) public issue of Rs. 143.35 crore strengthened balance sheet; DevIT stake diluted from 23% to 17%; exceptional gain of Rs. 93.55 crore recognized
items.quote: The public issue of our subsidiary, Dev Accelerator Limited, worth Rs. 143.35 crore, was also an important milestone.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty in US (tariffs), Canada (trade treaty), driving focus on India market sustainability and high-value asset creation
items.quote: We don't know what is going on with North America. We don't know what are our tariff implications on IT services business, as far as the U.S. is concerned. We don't know about our trade treaty with Canada.

items.statement: Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra offering data center incentives; in final talks with data center creator for management services
items.quote: in GIFT. In Gujarat, government has started providing incentives to data centers. Similarly, in states like Chhattisgarh, states like Maharashtra, they are also offering more incentives to data centers

items.statement: GIFT City ecosystem play: DevX center positioned to provide end-to-end solutions (real estate, IT, compliance) for GCCs entering GIFT City
items.quote: we are creating an ecosystem where we will be providing end-to-end solutions to those companies entering in GIFT City, starting from real estate to IT to compliance, everything that will be under one banner.

items.statement: Revenue will increase in FY26; second half revenue will be high and more than expected
items.quote: Revenue will increase. Second half revenue will be high. Revenue will be more than expected.

items.statement: EBITDA margin will remain intact for FY26
items.quote: Yes, margin will be intact.

items.statement: Competition will reduce in the livestock feed sector
items.quote: Competition will reduce.

items.statement: Overall margin is good; value-added products carry superior high margin potential
items.quote: Overall margin is good.

items.statement: Raw material price volatility managed through buffer stock policy and daily averaging; no impact over 12 months
items.quote: Overall, ma'am, there is no impact from around the year. And we already keep concentrating on it. And there is daily average of it. And there is no effect in the period of 12 months.

items.statement: Working capital cycle will reduce; working capital has increased compared to last year
items.quote: Working capital cycle will reduce. Working capital has increased compared to last year.

items.statement: Borrowings increased due to inventory buildup; some leverage must be borne
items.quote: Concentration is like that. Some things we have to bear.

items.statement: Farmer education and advisory programs will be launched to increase scientific adoption
items.quote: Farmer education. We will launch farmer education. We will bring that into effect.

items.statement: H1 FY26 total income Rs 2,369.51 lakhs; EBITDA Rs 327.48 lakhs at 13.82% margin; PAT Rs 204.56 lakhs at 8.63% net margin
items.quote: For the half year financial '26, total income was Rs. 2,369.51 lakhs. EBITDA stood at Rs. 327.48 lakhs with a margin of 13.82% and PAT increased to Rs. 204.56 lakhs with a net margin of 8.63%.

items.statement: Non-GMO compliance maintained; no GMO material used
items.quote: We do not use GMO material.
